玉音

嘉靖二十六年三月初九日，太子少保、禮部尚書兼翰林院學士臣費寀等於奉天門奏為科舉事：會試天下舉人，取中三百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合擬讀卷官及執事等官，少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華盖殿大學士夏言等六十六員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

特進光禄大夫、上柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華盖殿大學士夏言〔丁丑進士〕。

特進光禄大夫、柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、謹身殿大學士嚴嵩〔乙丑進士〕。

資德大夫、正治上卿、吏部尚書聞淵〔乙丑進士〕。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Twenty-sixth Year of Jiajing (1547)

Imperial Words

On the ninth day of the third month of the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing, your servant Fei Cai, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and others submitted the following memorial at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations:

“In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates (juren) from throughout the realm, three hundred candidates were selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we should nominate sixty-six officials as Readers and other functionaries, including Xia Yan, Junior Preceptor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.

“The classes of metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao. The first class shall, as customary, comprise three men: the first shall receive rank 6b, and the second and third rank 7a, with the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate with honors.’ Those in the second class shall receive rank 7b and the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate.’ Those in the third class shall receive rank 8a and the distinction ‘equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’”

The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Readers

Xia Yan was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement, Supreme Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year (1517).〕

Yan Song was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement, Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the yichou year (1505).〕

Wen Yuan was Grand Master for Fostering Virtue, Senior Minister for Correct Governance, and Minister of Personnel. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the yichou year (1505).〕

… Zheng Datong, Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel, was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year. Li Rujin, Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue, was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Officials responsible for sealing candidates’ identifying information:

Zhang Dian, Grand Master (tongyi dafu), was Left Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently an Orthographer in the Editorial Service. He was a Confucian scholar.

Zhang Wenxian, Grand Master (tongyi dafu), was Transmission Commissioner of the Office of Transmission. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Peng An, Grand Master (yazhong dafu), was Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Tan Xiang, Grand Master (yazhong dafu), was Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. He was a Confucian scholar.

Zhou Ling, Grand Master (tongyi dafu), was Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently an Orthographer in the Editorial Service. He was a licentiate.

Chen Zhang, Grand Master (jiayi dafu), was Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, administering the affairs of the Court of State Ceremonial. He was a student of ritual.

Yan Shifan, Grand Master (zhongxian dafu), was Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, administering the affairs of the Imperial Seals Office. He was a student admitted by virtue of official family status.

Wang Huai, Grand Master (fengyi dafu), was Right Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. He was a government student.

Xi Zhong, Grand Master (fengzheng dafu), was Chief Minister of the Imperial Seals Office. He was a government student.

Sun Sheng, Gentleman (chengde lang), was Right Secretary of the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Huang Tingyong, Gentleman (rulin lang), was a Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Xing Yifeng, Gentleman (wenlin lang), was a Junior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.

Sun Chi, Gentleman (chengzhi lang), was Assistant Minister of the Imperial Seals Office. He was an Imperial University student.

Li Lun, Gentleman (chengshi lang), was Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Rites. He was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Hu Yongtong, Gentleman (chengshi lang), was Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War. He was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Liu Kai, Gentleman (rulin lang), was Vice Director of the Left Office of the Court of Judicial Review [?; the transcription repeats “Left Office”], acting as Librarian of the Hanlin Academy. He was an Imperial University student.

Zhang Lian was Librarian of the Hanlin Academy. He was a Confucian scholar.

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing (1547), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the nineteenth day of the third month, the civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard arrayed the ceremonial regalia within the vermilion steps and courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow proclamation, led by drums and music, out through Chang’an Left Gate and posted it outside. Once this was completed, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the twentieth day of the third month…

translation_en:
…An imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the rites.
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate was granted court robes, a cap, and a girdle, and the metropolitan graduates were granted paper currency.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial expressing gratitude for imperial favor.
On the twenty-fourth day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite.
The Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Li Chunfang: 〔Registered in a civilian household in Xinghua County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region; a native of Jurong County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, his courtesy name was Zishi. He ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month.〕 His great-grandfather was Xiu, his grandfather Xu, and his father Tang; his mother was née Xu. His parents and grandparent generation were living. His younger brothers were Qifang and Chengfang, and his wife was née Xu. He placed 117th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chun: 〔Registered in a civilian household in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, his courtesy name was Renbo. He ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month.〕 His great-grandfather was Yongling, his grandfather Duanjiao, and his father Tianzhi; his mother was née Shi. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Hanbo, Shaobo, Junbo, Yingbo, and Rubo; his younger brothers were Huabo, Xinbo, Shibo, Taibo, Zuobo, and Zaibo. His wife was née Wu. He placed eighty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Zhengmeng: 〔Registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, his courtesy name was Zhengbo. He ranked tenth in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month.〕 His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Jie 〔an official awaiting selection for appointment〕, and his father Qing; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xianzhi, Yuzhi 〔a tribute scholar (gongshi)〕, Zhunzhi, Zhizhi, and Xianzhi; his younger brothers were Zhengxue, Zhengjia, Zhengzi, and Zhengxin. His wife was née Weng. He placed seventy-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

惲紹芳〔貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字光世，行一，年三十，二月十七日生。〕曾祖禧〔贈南京戶部郎中〕，祖鎡，父訓，母趙氏。具慶下，弟紹元、紹亨、紹德、紹祖、紹賢、紹美、紹文，娶張氏，繼娶龔氏。應天府鄉試第八十四名，會試第四十二名。
translation_en:
Second Class: ninety men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Kang Siqian: registered in a civilian household in Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-three sui old, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather, Sheng, was a prefectural Registrar; and his father, Feng[?] (逢𩆩), held a seventh-rank prestige title. His father's former wife was née He, and his mother was née Zheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Sizhong. He married a woman née Lu and subsequently a woman née Tian. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tangsun: registered in a military household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhenzong; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two sui old, born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gongxian, his grandfather Rongqing, his father Zigao, and his mother née Ding. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Jinsun and his younger brother Haosun. He married a woman née Lu. He placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yun Shaofang: registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guangshi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty sui old, born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Xi, was posthumously appointed Director of a bureau in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Zi, his father Xun, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shaoyuan, Shaoheng, Shaode, Shaozu, Shaoxian, Shaomei, and Shaowen. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Gong. He placed eighty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Chaobin, registered in an artisan household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University who specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yingzhi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Shitai, and his father Honglian, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Bao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Chaoyi and Jiezhi, both tribute students (gongshi), and Chaocai, Chaoshi, Chaohuan, and Chaofeng. He married a woman née Wu. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Jin, registered in an artisan household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a prefectural government school student who specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruli, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Liang, and his father Feng; his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Kai. He married a woman née Jia and subsequently a woman née Song. He placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhenghe, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural government school student who specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yili, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yuhui, his grandfather Daxing, who held an honorary official title for longevity, and his father Yuanfang; his mother was née Lu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Zhengmo, a tribute student (gongshi), Zhengsi, and Zhengyi. He married a woman née Yu. He placed fifteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Cheng, registered in a civilian household in Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student who specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Benjing, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Xianxiang, his grandfather Tianjie, and his father Pin; his mother was née Yao and his stepmother née Ye. His father was deceased, and his mother or stepmother was living. His elder brothers were Qing and Pan, the latter a District Magistrate; his younger brothers were Ji, Yuan, Pei, and Chao. He married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Bao. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Zhu, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Guofan; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and male cousins, was forty-three sui, and was born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunqing, his grandfather Conghe, his father Lin, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tie, and his younger brothers were Kai, Yue, and Yu. He married a woman née Gong. He placed thirty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Juzheng, registered in Jingzhou Guard, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a Jingzhou prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shuda; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was twenty-three sui, and was born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Zhen, his father Wenming, and his mother née Zhao. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Juren, and his younger brothers were Jujing, Ju’an, Juyi, Jukuan, Juye, Juxue, and Juzheng [the candidate’s own name is repeated here; ?]. He married a woman née Gu. He placed thirtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Jie, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziwen; he ranked eighth among his brothers and male cousins, was twenty-six sui, and was born on the ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lizan, his grandfather Kanggu〔holder of an honorary official title for longevity〕, his father Ji〔Ceremonial Usher〕, and his mother née Xu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Dong, and his younger brothers were Kui and Jian. He married a woman née Tu. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jisheng, registered in Rongcheng County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongfang; he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-two sui, and was born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Qing, his father Fu, and his mother née Cao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jichang and Jimei. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

慈侍下　兄顯　弟顥　試　娶陳氏
福建鄉試第六十五名　會試第二百二十五名
===
奚世亮
貫湖廣黃州衛官籍　黃州府學生
治禮記字仲明行五年三十三十一月二十六日生
曾祖鎮　祖淮　父朴〔知縣〕　母姜氏
具慶下　兄帯〔百户〕　世豪　世鸞　弟世英〔監生〕　世文〔貢士〕　世方　世言　世彦　娶王氏
湖廣鄉試第五十一名　會試第二百二名
章世仁
貫直隸池州府青陽縣民籍　國子生
治詩經字元卿行一年三十二六月三十日生
曾祖叔泰　祖校　父時文　母王氏
重慶下　兄世隆〔貢士〕　世昭〔貢士〕　弟世儀　世作　世仰　世仕　世修　娶施氏
應天府鄉試第一百二十八名　會試第七十五名
punctuated:
楊豫孫〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣民籍，青浦縣人，國子生，治《詩經》，字幼殷，行一，年二十七，十月二十日生〕。曾祖溥〔七品散官〕，祖欽〔典膳正〕，父樞〔推官〕，母李氏。重慶下，兄晋孫，弟蒙孫、益孫、觀孫、萃孫、升孫、賁孫、鼎孫、井孫，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第三十五名，會試第一百七十七名。

高超〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍鹽籍，府學生，治《詩經》，字廷華，行二，年三十四，八月二十六日生〕。曾祖賜祿，祖綱，父通〔知縣〕，母張氏。慈侍下，兄顯，弟頡、試，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第六十五名，會試第二百二十五名。

奚世亮〔貫湖廣黃州衛官籍，黃州府學生，治《禮記》，字仲明，行五，年三十三，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖鎮，祖淮，父朴〔知縣〕，母姜氏。具慶下，兄世榮〔百戶〕、世豪、世鸞，弟世奕〔監生〕、世文〔貢士〕、世方、世言、世彥，娶王氏。湖廣鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百二名。

章世仁〔貫直隸池州府青陽縣民籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字元卿，行一，年三十二，六月三十日生〕。曾祖叔泰，祖校，父時文，母王氏。重慶下，兄世隆〔貢士〕、世昭〔貢士〕，弟世榮、世作、世仰、世仕、世修，娶施氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十八名，會試第七十五名。
translation_en:
Yang Yusun, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, and a native of Qingpu County, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Youyin, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu, a seventh-rank prestige official; his grandfather was Qin, Director of Food Service; his father was Shu, a Judge; and his mother was née Li. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Jinsun, and his younger brothers were Mengsun, Yisun, Guansun, Cuisun, Shengsun, Bensun, Dingsun, and Jingsun; his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Chao, registered in a military salt-service household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tinghua, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cilu; his grandfather was Gang; his father was Tong, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Xian, and his younger brothers were Jie and Shi; his wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xi Shiliang, registered in an official household of Huangzhou Guard, Huguang, was a student of the Huangzhou prefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zhongming, he ranked fifth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather was Huai; his father was Pu, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shirong, a Company Commander, Shihao, and Shiluan; his younger brothers were Shiyi, a National University student, Shiwen, a tribute scholar, Shifang, Shiyan (世言), and Shiyan (世彥); his wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shiren, registered in a civilian household in Qingyang County, Chizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanqing, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the thirtieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shutai; his grandfather was Xiao; his father was Shiwen; and his mother was née Wang. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Shilong and Shizhao, both tribute scholars, and his younger brothers were Shirong, Shizuo, Shiyang, Shishi, and Shixiu; his wife was née Shi. He placed 128th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖文德〔贈監察御史〕　祖綬〔壽官〕　父彬〔教諭〕　母曹氏
具慶下兄與之　益之　憲之　元之　熙之　官之　弟從之　娶葛氏

王惟恕貫福建漳州府長泰縣軍籍　國子生
治書經字行甫行一年二十七十月二十一日生
曾祖光重　祖廷表　父瑩之〔知州〕　母謝氏
重慶下　弟惟惠　惟憑　惟懋　惟應　娶薛氏
福建鄉試第二十二名　會試第一百七十六名
punctuated:
任惟鈞〔貫四川重慶府巴縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字子範，行一，年三十七，十一月十一日生〕。曾祖瑛，祖卿，父冕〔通判〕，母李氏。具慶下，弟惟鏜、惟銓、惟鑑、惟鑰、惟鉉、惟鈺。娶曹氏，繼娶劉氏、蹇氏。四川鄉試第十七名，會試第一百七十八名。

莫如士〔貫龍驤衛，軍籍，廣東新會縣人，國子生，治易經，字子元，行四，年三十六，六月二十四日生〕。曾祖滿，祖雄，父違仁〔封監察御史〕，母蘇氏〔贈孺人〕。嚴侍下，兄如爵〔監察御史〕、如齒、如德、如善〔貢士〕，弟如學、如誠。娶黃氏，繼娶蔣氏。順天府鄉試第二十九名，會試第一百七十三名。

謝登之〔貫湖廣岳州府巴陵縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字汝學，行六，年二十九，八月初六日生〕。曾祖文德〔贈監察御史〕，祖綬〔壽官〕，父彬〔教諭〕，母曹氏。具慶下，兄與之、藎之、定之、元之、熈之、官之，弟似之。娶葛氏。湖廣鄉試第一名，會試第一百五十名。

王惟恕〔貫福建漳州府長泰縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字行甫，行一，年二十七，十月二十一日生〕。曾祖光重，祖廷表，父瑩之〔知州〕，母謝氏。重慶下，弟惟惠、惟憑、惟懋、惟應。娶薛氏。福建鄉試第二十二名，會試第一百七十六名。
translation_en:
Ren Weijun, registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zifan, he ranked first in his family, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Qing, and his father Mian (Assistant Prefect); his mother was née Li, and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Weitang, Weiquan, Weijian, Weiyue, Weixuan, and Weiyu. He married a woman née Cao and subsequently women née Liu and née Jian. He placed seventeenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mo Rushi, registered in a military household of Longxiang Guard and originally from Xinhui County, Guangdong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyuan, he ranked fourth in his family, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Man, his grandfather Xiong, and his father Weiren [?] (granted the title of Investigating Censor); his mother was née Su (posthumously granted the title of Lady). His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Rujue (Investigating Censor), Ruchi, Rude, and Rushan (tribute scholar); his younger brothers were Ruxue and Rucheng. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Dengzhi, registered in a military household in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruxue, he ranked sixth in his family, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wende (posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor), his grandfather Shou (holder of an honorary title for longevity), and his father Bin (Instructor); his mother was née Cao, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuzhi, Jinzhi, Dingzhi, Yuanzhi, Xizhi, and Guanzhi; his younger brother was Sizhi. He married a woman née Ge. He placed first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Weishu, registered in a military household in Changtai County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xingfu, he ranked first in his family, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Guangzhong, his grandfather Tingbiao, and his father Yingzhi (Department Magistrate); his mother was née Xie, and his grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Weihui, Weiping, Weimao, and Weiying. He married a woman née Xue. He placed twenty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王時槐

曾祖續友　祖希禮　父一善　嫡母劉氏　生母姜氏

貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣軍籍　國子生

曾祖芩〔七品散官〕　祖節〔州判官〕　父大綱　母邵氏
具慶下　兄世善　弟世英　世華　世美　世蕃　娶毛氏　繼娶黃氏
浙江鄉試第四十一名　會試第三十一名
punctuated:
徐光啟〔貫江西廣信府貴溪縣官籍，國子生，治書經，字叔賢，行七十八，年三十，九月十二日生〕。曾祖孔福，祖潮〔壽官〕，父椅〔太醫院醫士〕，母楊氏。重慶下，兄焞〔省祭官〕、熿、焌、燧、光亨，弟光行、光國、光天、光宙，娶江氏。江西鄉試第八十三名，會試第一百六名。

張邦彥〔貫山東青州府臨朐縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字才甫，行一，年三十九，十二月十四日生〕。曾祖鳳，祖繹〔通判〕，父一中，母金氏。慈侍下，弟邦本、邦直〔監生〕、邦教、邦土，娶黃氏，繼娶劉氏。山東鄉試第四十五名，會試第一百八十名。

王時槐〔貫江西吉安府安福縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字子植，行六，年二十六，七月初二日生〕。曾祖續友，祖希禮，父一善，嫡母劉氏，生母姜氏。具慶下，兄時椿、時梅、時松、時柏、時桂，弟時格、時梧、時相、時棟、時楠、時權，娶陳氏，繼娶鄒氏。江西鄉試第二十名，會試第二百十三名。

楊世芳〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字懋德，行五十三，三十四，三月初一日生〕。曾祖苓〔七品散官〕，祖節〔州判官〕，父大綱，母邵氏。具慶下，兄菩，弟英華、世美、世蕃，娶毛氏，繼娶黃氏。浙江鄉試第四十一名，會試第三十一名。
translation_en:
Xu Guangqi, registered in an official household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shuxian, he ranked seventy-eighth in his family generation, and he was thirty years old, born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Kongfu; his grandfather, Chao, held an honorary office for longevity; his father, Yi, was a physician in the Imperial Medical Office; and his mother was née Yang. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Tun, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan) [?], Huang, Jun, Sui, and Guangheng; his younger brothers were Guangxing, Guangguo, Guangtian, and Guangzhou. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed eighty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Bangyan, registered in a military household in Linqu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Caifu, he ranked first in his family generation, and he was thirty-nine years old, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather, Yi, was an assistant prefect; his father was Yizhong; and his mother was née Jin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Bangben, Bangzhi, a student of the Directorate of Education, Bangjiao, and Bangtu. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed forty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shihuai, registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zizhi, he ranked sixth in his family generation, and he was twenty-six years old, born on the second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xuyou; his grandfather was Xili; his father was Yishan; his legal mother was née Liu; and his birth mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shichun, Shimei, Shisong, Shibai, and Shigui; his younger brothers were Shige, Shiwu, Shixiang, Shidong, Shinan, and Shiquan. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Zou. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shifang, registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Maode, he ranked fifty-third in his family generation, and he was thirty-four years old [?], born on the first day of the third month. His great-grandfather, Ling, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather, Jie, was an assistant subprefect; his father was Dagang; and his mother was née Shao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Pu; his younger brothers were Yinghua, Shimei, and Shifan. He married a woman née Mao and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed forty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Queyi, registered in a civilian household in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zishen; he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the eleventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Yu, and his father Shu; his father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Cui. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Quewen. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Li. He ranked sixty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yikui, registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhangfu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Li was Left Assistant Administration Commissioner in the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather was Tang, his father Zhonggui, and his mother née Peng. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yilong and Yiyin. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Menghe, registered in an artisan household in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jun was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Revenue. His grandfather Qing was granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Transmission Commissioner in the Office of Transmission, and posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Revenue. His father Jing was Minister of War, and his mother, née Su, was granted the title Lady. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mengchuan, Mengcao (formerly a prefectural registrar), Mengdai, Mengheng, Mengyun, Mengdou, Mengqi, Menglu, and Menghuang. He married a woman née Shi. He ranked forty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhi, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziming; he was tenth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian. His grandfather Li was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Personnel. His father Fu was a county vice magistrate and received successive posthumous grants culminating in the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Personnel. His father's former wives were née Lin and née Qian; his mother, née Gu, was granted the title Grand Respectful Lady and posthumously granted the title Chaste Lady. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Long (an official by contribution), Sheng, Heng (a sacrificial official [?]), Sui, Fu, Jie (Left Vice Minister of Personnel), Sheng, Chen, and Fang; his younger brother was Lin. He married a woman née Song. He ranked twenty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Geng Suichao, courtesy name Ziheng, was registered in a military household in Hua County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty, born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Biao, his grandfather Run, his father Jie, and his mother née Wu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Suiguo; his younger brothers were Suiqing (a jinshi of the same examination cohort), Suixiang, Suixing, Suizuo, Suijian, Suiyong, Suixiao, and Suidi. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Yongyi, courtesy name Xingfu, was registered in a banner household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Haining County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-nine, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Zhen; his legal mothers were née Xia and née Wang, and his birth mother was née Ma. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Qi; his younger brothers were Junyi, Weiyi, and Shiyi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed 125th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Guoxiang, courtesy name Yingfu, was registered in a banner household of Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Taizhou, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Yong, and his father Yu; his father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Guoshi and Guochen. He married a woman née Ji. He placed forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ling Yunyi, courtesy name Rucheng, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in his family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang, his grandfather Gao, his father Kun, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruzhi (a district magistrate) and Ruxue. He married a woman née Xue. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

藍璧〔貫江西瑞州府高安縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字完卿，行三，年三十七，十二月十六日生〕。曾祖惟祥，祖安成，父賢，母劉氏，繼母黃氏。具慶下，兄瑩，弟壟、塗、壂。娶鄒氏，繼娶謝氏。江西鄉試第四十六名，會試第一百二十六名。

丘瓚〔貫留守中衛軍籍，福建惠安縣人，順天府學生，治詩經，字獻卿，行二，年三十三，十二月十七日生〕。曾祖亦民，祖俊，父銳，母葛氏。嚴侍下，兄璋，弟珎、瑀、琦、瑗。娶寗氏。順天府鄉試第一百三十名，會試第六十六名。
translation_en:
Zhu Ji, registered in a civilian household in Taoyuan County, Huai'an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Maoxue, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-six, born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather, Luan, was an Assistant Magistrate; his father, Hong, was a Guard Clerk; his mother was née Xia, and his stepmother née Shan. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Jian, Fu, Jie, Fei, Huang, Guan, Qian, Zhuan, Gan, Tong, and Yue. He married a woman née Tian and subsequently a woman née Gong. He placed sixty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Qi, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xianhan, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was thirty-nine, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Wanbiao, his grandfather Shangli, his father Yue, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ke, a Subprefectural Judge; Bi, an acting Office Manager; Xuan, an Assistant Magistrate; Yuan, an Imperial University student; and Rong. His younger brothers were Yu; Qiu, an Imperial University student; Heng, an Imperial University student; Chong, an Imperial University student; Bin, an Imperial University student; and Tian. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lan Bi, registered in a civilian household in Gao'an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wanqing, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was thirty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Weixiang, his grandfather Ancheng, his father Xian, his mother née Liu, and his stepmother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ying, and his younger brothers were Long, Tu, and Dian [?]. He married a woman née Zou and subsequently a woman née Xie. He placed forty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Zan, registered in a military household of the Central Guard of the Defense Command (Liushou Zhongwei) and a native of Hui'an County, Fujian, was a Shuntian prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xianqing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yimin, his grandfather Jun, his father Rui, and his mother née Ge. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Zhang, and his younger brothers were Zhen, Yu, Qi, and Yuan. He married a woman née Ning. He placed 130th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

李敬〔貫陝西西安府涇陽縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字直夫，行二，年三十八，十月二十四日生。〕曾祖節，祖錦，父蘭，母王氏，繼母張氏、程氏。具慶下，兄愛，弟豸、采、徵、宦，娶秦氏。陝西鄉試第十九名，會試第二百九十四名。

王春澤〔貫福建漳州府漳浦縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字以潤，行三，年三十三，四月二十二日生。〕曾祖亨，祖龍，父豸，母林氏。具慶下，兄春瀾，弟春淮、春洛，娶林氏。福建鄉試第四十九名，會試第一百十八名。
translation_en:
Weng Shiqi, courtesy name Deqing, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was an attached student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His family birth-order rank is recorded as “二二” [?]; he was twenty-seven years old and was born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongze, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Yuan; his mother was née Ni. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shimian, Shizhong, Shimin, and Shitai, and his wife was née Yan. He placed eighty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Jiucheng, courtesy name Zishao, was registered in a civilian household in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was an attached student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked eighty-second in family birth order, and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, his grandfather Da, and his father Keng; his mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Luo. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Jiusi and Jiuzhang, and his wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jing, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in a civilian household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked second in family birth order, and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie, his grandfather Jin, and his father Lan; his mother was née Wang, and his stepmothers were née Zhang and née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ai, and his younger brothers were Zhi, Cai, Zheng, and Huan. His wife was née Qin. He placed nineteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chunze, courtesy name Yirun, was registered in a military household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked third in family birth order, and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng, his grandfather Long, and his father Zhi; his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chunlan, and his younger brothers were Chunhuai and Chunluo. His wife was née Lin. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gu Bing 顧抦, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to an artisan household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Wenqian; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Yanxing, his father Yin, and his mother née Deng. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Mo and Ge, and his younger brothers Zhen, Kai, Xu, and Yinglong. He married a woman née Lu. He placed eighty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Dengying 彭登瀛, registered in Lingui County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was originally from Fengcheng County, Jiangxi. He was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Xuanzhi; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the tenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wansan, his grandfather Yuan, his father Fu, and his mother née Wang. His mother alone survived. He married a woman née Pei. He placed ninth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yan 吳衍, registered in Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zifan; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged forty-seven, and was born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qikang, his grandfather Jie, his father Chengxun, and his mother née Mei. His father alone survived. His elder brother was Sheng. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mianxue 張勉學, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to an artisan household and was a county school student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Yifu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Cheng, his father Qin, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Zhou 輖. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Tang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cai Wen 蔡文, courtesy name Fuzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Nanjing County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a native of Longxi County. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongyan, his grandfather Hong, his father Deliu, and his mother née Yan; both parents were living. His elder brother Yi was a sacrificial attendant (shengjiguan), and his younger brother was Huai. He married a woman née Huang. He placed forty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Yue 蔡鑰, courtesy name Boqi, was registered in an officer household of Chengtian Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Tongzhou, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Ying held the military prestige title General of Illustrious Resolution (zhaoyi jiangjun) and served as Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; his grandfather Liang held the same prestige title and served as Guard Commander. His father Shen was a student of the Directorate of Education. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ming, Vice Battalion Commander, and Qin, who held the military prestige title General of Manifest Might (mingwei jiangjun) and served as acting Guard Vice Commander; his younger brother was Lian. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twentieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Qin 劉芹, courtesy name Zixian, was registered in a civilian household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jieming, his grandfather Ruzhao, and his father Haichuan; his mother was née Liu and his stepmother née Yao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zuo, Da, and Jie. He married a woman née Feng. He placed sixty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zunxun 黎遵訓, courtesy name Xiaoruo, was registered in a military household in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zan was posthumously granted the prestige title Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and the office of Left Vice Minister of Works. His grandfather was Yongxiao, and his father Qian held a seventh-rank prestige title. His father's former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zunmo, and his younger brothers were Zunzhao, Zungao, and Zunhui. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Wei. He placed eighty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liang Zuo, registered in a military household of Dali Guard, Yunnan, and originally from Lanyang County, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Yingtai, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhong (holder of an honorary title for longevity), his grandfather was Cai (holder of an honorary title for public beneficence), his father was Jin, and his mother was née Zhao; both parents were living, his younger brother was You, and his wife was née He; he placed fifth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Shiping, registered in a civilian household of Pingyuan County, Dezhou Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Keyi, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Wu, his grandfather was Tianxi, his father was Hongdao (an Imperial University student), and his mother was née Yao; his father was deceased and his mother living, his younger brothers were Shiyi, Shixiao, Shide, Shiqing, Shishen, and Shiqin, and his wife was née Tan; he placed twenty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dongzhou, registered in a military household of Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziyong, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twentieth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Chaobin, his grandfather was Zhongrong, his father was Xi, and his mother was née Chen; both parents were living, his elder brother was Donglu, and his wife was née She; he placed twenty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yuanyu, registered in a civilian household of Pujiang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Boqi, he ranked twenty-eighth in birth order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zizhi (holder of an honorary title for longevity), his grandfather was Wenyou, his father was Mengjing, and his mother was née Dai; both parents were living, his elder brother was Yuanheng, his younger brothers were Yuanliang, Yuanping, Yuankang, Yuanqian, Yuantiao, and Yuane, and his wife was née Zhao; he placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Youwei, registered in Qianyang County, Yuanzhou Subprefecture, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xiyan, and he was first in birth order, aged forty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jiu; his grandfather, Yanzhang; and his father, Peng, a County Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Xiang, and his stepmother was née Tan. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Youdao, Youxian, Youshou, Youfan, and Younian. He married a woman née He. He placed ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Yan, registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Renhe County. An added-quota student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zixing, and he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ming, an unattached official of the seventh rank; his grandfather, Wenyuan; and his father, En, a provincial sacrificial official. His mother was née Yang. His parents and grandparents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ren, registered in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xiyin, and he was second in birth order, aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Qi; and his father, Zi'ai, a student of the Directorate of Education. His mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sheng, and his younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Chaobin, registered in Hui'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yuguan, and he was second in birth order, aged forty-two, born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yimin; his grandfather, Yongchu; and his father, Qiang. His mother was née Chen. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Shunqing. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née He. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Shike, registered in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zideng; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Ju, his father Jiusi, and his mother née Cao. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Shixian, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Shicong, Shichen, and Shiru. He married a woman née Ding. He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Youling, registered in Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Mengxi; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather was Jing, his father Xingwen, and his mother née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xialing, Shouling, Kangling, and Shiling; his younger brother was Changling. He married a woman née Xiong. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Sijian, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuye; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twentieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather Yin was a County Registrar; his father was Yunhu, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Siqi. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yixin, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenqi; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liangchou; his grandfather Yan was an annual tribute student who received the honorary title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his father Xingzhi was a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; and his mother, née Chen, received the title of Lady of Repose. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Dexin; his younger brothers were Shangxin and Enxin. He married a woman née Wu. He placed eleventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 100th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Shouzhi, courtesy name Zhenfu, was registered in a civilian household in Yanjin County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Biao, a Chief Clerk; his grandfather was Xiang, a tribute student; his father was Zi, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Diao. He ranked fourteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Sijie, courtesy name Yuanjing, was registered in a civilian household in Yizhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Changping Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, posthumously granted the title of Prefectural Vice Prefect; his grandfather was Weizong, an honorary official; and his father was Sheng, a Subprefectural Assistant Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Silan, Rubo, and Ruoqing, and his wife was née Wan. He ranked fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Minghan, courtesy name Weixian, was registered in a military household in Xiaoyi County, Fenzhou, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather was Zhifu, his father was Lei, and his mother was née Ren. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mingshi, Mingbian, Mingshi, and Mingyun, and his wife was née Qiao. He ranked fifty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Sanwei, courtesy name Rujing, was registered in a civilian household in Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the seventeenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather was Zong, his father was Xiang, his mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Tang. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Sande, Sanbian, and Sanpin, and his wife was née Ji. He ranked sixty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Zhichen, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in the family order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhongshan, was a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Jun, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, posthumously granted the same titles. His father, Dao, formerly held the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of War. His mother, née An, was ennobled as Lady (shuren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qinchen, Yinchen, Liangchen, Ruchen, and Yu [?]; his younger brothers were Xianchen, Chaochen, Chunchen, Jichen, Pinchen, Yiyi, and Shangren. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yuangong, courtesy name Zili, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twelfth in the family order and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ying, was a County School Instructor, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master of Palace Counsel and Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. His grandfather, Qi, was a Station Master, posthumously granted the same titles. His father, Zongqin, was a County Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Fan; his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Yuansu, was an Imperial University student; his younger brother, Yuanyi, was a Prefectural Clerk. He married a woman née Mao. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Yunyang, courtesy name Maocheng, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Changshu County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighteenth in the family order and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhixing, was honorifically granted the title County Magistrate; his grandfather, Yan, was an Assistant Prefect. His father's name is transcribed as 𨯤 [?], and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yunzhen, Yunxiu, and Yunhua. He married a woman née Lu. He placed ninety-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Jiugong, courtesy name Weixu, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangyuan County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in the family order and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather, Ren, held the designation Sacrificial Official (shengjiguan) [?]; his father was Shan, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiusi and Jiuqing; his younger brother was Jiuchou. He married a woman née Han. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

text:

===
林一新
貫福建漳州府漳浦縣軍籍　縣學增廣生
治詩經字躋夫行三年三十三八月初十日生
曾祖普玄〔壽官〕　祖振〔壽官〕　父鏛　母程氏

何鏜
貫浙江處州衛軍籍順天府宛平縣人　國子生
治詩經字振卿行五年三十二月初二日生
曾祖孟曇　祖允恭　父珙　母章氏
重慶下　兄鈁鏻鏊　弟鑰鋹鑌鎬鋌鈌銑鍵　娶陳氏
浙江鄉試第八十六名　會試第三十一名
punctuated:
宋文明〔貫山東東昌府臨清州民籍，山西洪洞縣人，國子生，治易經，字汝化，行一，年四十四，二月二十八日生〕。曾祖拯〔提學副使〕，祖讓，父天祥，母郭氏。永感下，弟文昇、文言、文選、文粹，娶梁氏，繼娶張氏。山東鄉試第三十一名，會試第七十八名。

劉應時〔貫山西平陽府洪洞縣軍籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字子易，行三，年二十六，八月初四日生〕。曾祖恭〔封文林郎兵馬司副指揮〕，祖榮〔通判，封奉直大夫刑部員外郎〕，父廷相〔貢士〕，母張氏。重慶下，弟應科、應材、應元、應嶽、應宿、應龍、應墀、應誥、應制，娶郭氏。山西鄉試第五十九名，會試第二百二十一名。

林一新〔貫福建漳州府漳浦縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字躋夫，行三，年三十三，八月初十日生〕。曾祖普玄〔壽官〕，祖振〔壽官〕，父黻，母程氏。具慶下，兄一初〔貢士〕、一陽〔貢士〕、功懋〔知府〕、策〔大理寺右評事〕、成綱〔貢士〕，娶吳氏。福建鄉試第四十七名，會試第九十五名。

何鏜〔貫浙江處州衛軍籍，順天府宛平縣人，國子生，治詩經，字振卿，行五，年三十，二月初二日生〕。曾祖孟曇，祖允恭，父珙，母章氏。重慶下，兄鈁、鉳、鋈，弟鑰、鋃、鑌、鎬、𨦣、銑、鍵，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第八十六名，會試第三名。
translation_en:
Song Wenming, registered in a civilian household in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a native of Hongdong County, Shanxi, and a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruhua, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, Deputy Surveillance Commissioner for Education; his grandfather was Rang; his father was Tianxiang; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Wensheng, Wenyan, Wenxuan, and Wencui. He married a woman née Liang and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yingshi was registered in a military household in Hongdong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyi, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gong, granted the titles Gentleman of Cultivated Learning and Vice Commander of a Ward-inspecting Office; his grandfather was Rong, an Assistant Prefect, granted the titles Grand Master for Straightforward Service and Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Tingxiang, a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His younger brothers were Yingke, Yingcai, Yingyuan, Yingyue, Yingxiu, Yinglong, Yingchi, Yinggao, and Yingzhi. He married a woman née Guo. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yixin was registered in a military household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was an expanded-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jifu, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Puxuan and his grandfather was Zhen, both holders of honorary official status for longevity; his father was Fu; and his mother was née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yichu and Yiyang, both tribute scholars; Gongmao, a Prefect; Ce, a Right Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; and Chenggang, a tribute scholar. He married a woman née Wu. He placed forty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Tang was registered in a military household of Chuzhou Guard, Zhejiang, and was a native of Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture, and a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhenqing, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Mengtan; his grandfather was Yungong; his father was Gong; and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His elder brothers were Fang, Bei (鉳) [?], and Wu; his younger brothers were Yue, Lang, Bin, Gao, 𨦣 [name reading uncertain], Xian, and Jian. He married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄

張西銘〔貫山東濟南府濱州軍籍州學生治書經字原仁行二年二十八八月三十日生〕
曾祖鑾祖淳父拱辰母胡氏
具慶下兄大化弟西嶽西崑娶王氏
山東鄉試第二十五名會試第六十七名

曾祖曉祖汝玉父文章母林氏

曾祖源　祖祐〔右恩例冠帶〕　父希周〔監生〕　母柯氏
嚴侍下　弟一夔　一貫　一中　一致　一新　娶童氏

李景華貫直隸順德府任縣民籍　縣學生
治詩經字德聚行一年二十五三月初二日生
曾祖銘　祖志皐　父璋〔壽官〕　母陳氏　繼母陳氏
具慶下　弟景茂　娶張氏
順天府鄉試第一百二十八名　會試第一百四十七名
punctuated:
張西銘〔貫山東濟南府濱州，軍籍，州學生，治書經，字原仁，行二，年二十八，八月三十日生〕。曾祖鑾，祖淳，父拱辰，母胡氏。具慶下，兄大化，弟西嶽、西崑，娶王氏。山東鄉試第二十五名，會試第六十七名。

宋曰仁〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字思表，行一，年三十七，八月初二日生〕。曾祖曉，祖汝玉，父文章，母林氏。永感下，弟孔、曰位、信、旦、偉、忠、孝、准，娶林氏。福建鄉試第三十八名，會試第一百九十三名。

李一元〔貫直隸池州府建德縣，匠籍，國子生，治春秋，字調卿，行一，年三十二，二月初八日生〕。曾祖源，祖祐〔恩例冠帶〕，父希周〔監生〕，母柯氏。嚴侍下，弟一夔、一貫、一中、一致、一新，娶童氏。應天府鄉試第三十三名，會試第二百十五名。

李景萃〔貫直隸順德府任縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字德聚，行一，年二十五，三月初二日生〕。曾祖銘，祖志皐，父璋〔壽官〕，母陳氏，繼母陳氏。具慶下，弟景茂，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十八名，會試第一百四十七名。
translation_en:
Zhang Ximing, registered in Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the department school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuanren. Second in birth order, he was twenty-eight years old, born on the thirtieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luan, his grandfather Chun, and his father Gongchen; his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dahua, and his younger brothers were Xiyue and Xikun. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Yueren, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Sibiao. First in birth order, he was thirty-seven years old, born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiao, his grandfather Ruyu, and his father Wenzhang; his mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Kong, Yuewei, Xin, Dan, Wei, Zhong, Xiao, and Zhun [division of names uncertain: 孔曰位信旦偉忠孝准]. His wife was née Lin. He placed thirty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yiyuan, registered in Jiande County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Diaoqing. First in birth order, he was thirty-two years old, born on the eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather You had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under provisions for imperial grace. His father Xizhou was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his mother was née Ke. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Yikui, Yiguan, Yizhong, Yizhi, and Yixin. His wife was née Tong. He placed thirty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jingcui, registered in Ren County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Deju. First in birth order, he was twenty-five years old, born on the second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Zhigao, and his father Zhang, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His mother and stepmother were both née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jingmao, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
張希賢〔貫山東兗州府濟寧州軍籍國子生治易經字尚友行三年三十七七月二十一日生〕

永感下兄希周希憲娶曹氏
山東鄉試第二十三名會試第二百十七名
汪烇〔貫浙江杭州府臨安縣民籍國子生治詩經字子光行五十三年三十五正月二十五日生〕
曾祖勇祖明父淑嫡母徐氏生母羅氏

===

治詩經字益甫行四年三十九月十七日生
曾祖子魁　祖集仁　父時律　母饒氏
具慶下　兄思誠　弟思謨　思訓　思讓　思諫　娶劉氏

曾祖安　祖榮　父秀〔訓導〕　母楊氏

應天府鄉試第一百二十四名　會試第二百四十五名
punctuated:
張希賢〔貫山東兗州府濟寧州，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字尚友，行三，年三十七，七月二十一日生〕。曾祖晟，祖滋，父瑀，母劉氏。永感下，兄希周、希憲，娶曹氏。山東鄉試第二十三名，會試第二百十七名。

汪烇〔貫浙江杭州府臨安縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子光，行五十三，年三十五，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖勇，祖明，父淑，嫡母徐氏，生母羅氏。嚴侍下，兄聰、燉，弟應徵、煙、黨，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第七十名，會試第一百三十七名。

萬思謙〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字益甫，行四，年三十一，九月十七日生〕。曾祖子魁，祖集仁，父時律，母饒氏。具慶下，兄思誠，弟思謨、思訓、思讓、思諫，娶劉氏。江西鄉試第七十四名，會試第二百四十一名。

李心學〔貫直隸鳳陽府臨淮縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字建中，行三，年二十八，四月初三日生〕。曾祖安，祖榮，父秀〔訓導〕，母楊氏。具慶下，兄潮、灌，弟性學、淳、浩、志學、清、洞、瀧、勉學，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十四名，會試第二百四十五名。
translation_en:
Zhang Xixian 張希賢, registered in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shangyou; he ranked third in family order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Zi, his father Yu, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xizhou and Xixian 希憲, and his wife was née Cao. He placed twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Quan 汪烇, registered in Lin’an County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a commoner household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziguang; he ranked fifty-third in family order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Ming, and his father Shu; his legal mother was née Xu and his birth mother née Luo. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Cong and Dun; his younger brothers were Yingzheng, Yan, and Dang. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Siqian 萬思謙, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a commoner household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yifu; he ranked fourth in family order, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zikui, his grandfather Jiren, his father Shilü, and his mother née Rao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sicheng; his younger brothers were Simo, Sixun, Sirang, and Sijian. His wife was née Liu. He placed seventy-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xinxue 李心學, registered in Linhuai County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a commoner household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jianzhong; he ranked third in family order, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Rong, his father Xiu〔Assistant Instructor〕, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chao and Guan; his younger brothers were Xingxue, Chun, Hao, Zhixue, Qing, Dong, Long, and Mianxue. His wife was née Chen. He placed 124th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王世貞〔貫直隸蘇州府太倉州軍籍，崑山縣人，州學附學生，治易經，字元美，行十九，年二十二，十一月初五日生〕。曾祖輅〔累贈通議大夫南京兵部右侍郎〕，祖倬〔通議大夫南京兵部右侍郎〕，父忞〔監察御史〕，母郁氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄世芳〔提學副使〕、世德〔官生〕、世業〔譯字生〕，弟世聞、世望、世懋，娶魏氏。應天府鄉試第五十八名，會試第八十二名。

江治〔貫江西南昌府進賢縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字順之，行五，年四十七，七月初三日生〕。曾祖啓明〔義官〕，祖正奇，父玠，母楊氏。永感下，兄洪，弟泗，娶吳氏。江西鄉試第二名，會試第一百五十五名。

朱天俸〔貫忠義後衛軍籍，直隸濬縣人，國子生，治書經，字子學，行三，年三十二，七月十一日生〕。曾祖紹，祖榮，父鑑，前母林氏，母林氏，繼母謝氏、張氏。嚴侍下，兄天爵，娶洪氏。順天府鄉試第七名，會試第一百九名。

胡朝臣〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣民籍，府學附學生，治易經，字汝鄰，行十三，年三十四，九月二十一日生〕。曾祖慶，祖謹〔壽官〕，父廷璋〔典史〕，母趙氏。嚴侍下，兄朝宗、朝元、朝冕、朝會、朝陽、朝著、朝京，弟朝佐、朝卿、朝相，娶董氏。浙江鄉試第十八名，會試第二百五十九名。
translation_en:
Wang Shizhen, registered in a military household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a native of Kunshan County and an supplementary student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuanmei. Nineteenth in birth order, he was twenty-two sui and was born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Lu was posthumously granted, through successive honors, the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing; his grandfather Zhuo held those titles; his father Min was an Investigating Censor; and his mother, née Yu, was granted the title Lady of the Seventh Rank. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shifang, an Education Intendant with the rank of Vice Commissioner; Shide, a student admitted by virtue of official family status; and Shiye, a student of written translation. His younger brothers were Shiwen, Shiwang, and Shimao. He married a woman née Wei. He placed fifty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Zhi was registered in a civilian household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shunzhi. Fifth in birth order, he was forty-seven sui and was born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Qiming held an honorary office awarded for public benefaction; his grandfather was Zhengqi; his father was Jie; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Hong, and his younger brother was Si. He married a woman née Wu. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Tianfeng was registered in a military household of the Zhongyi Rear Guard, was a native of Xun County in the directly administered region, and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zixue. Third in birth order, he was thirty-two sui and was born on the eleventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shao; his grandfather was Rong; and his father was Jian. His father's former wife was née Lin, his mother was also née Lin, and his stepmothers were née Xie and née Zhang. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Tianjue. He married a woman née Hong. He placed seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Chaochen was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a supplementary student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rulin. Thirteenth in birth order, he was thirty-four sui and was born on the twenty-first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather Jin held an honorary office awarded for longevity; his father Tingzhang was a County Clerk; and his mother was née Zhao. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Chaozong, Chaoyuan, Chaomian, Chaohui, Chaoyang, Chaozhu, and Chaojing; his younger brothers were Chaozuo, Chaoqing, and Chaoxiang. He married a woman née Dong. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.
