translation_en:
Wang Lianggui, registered in an artisan household in Ningjin County, Hejian Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shaosi; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Jin, was an Instructor; his father, Ping, was an Office Manager in a Regional Military Commission; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Liangcai, Liangshi, Liangqi, and Liangshi (良史). He married a woman née Zhan and subsequently a woman née Pan. He placed thirty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Wenmian, registered in a civilian household in Kaihua County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Kesheng; he ranked forty-seventh in birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Luan, was an Investigating Censor; his grandfather, Zu, was an Instructor; his father, Lian, was a School Instructor; and his mother was née Cheng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Wenpu, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, Wenshi, and Wentang; his younger brothers were Wenpeng, Wenlan, Wenhuang, Wenpan, and Wenyan. He married a woman née Fang. He placed sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yu, registered in a civilian household in Anju County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenfu; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang; his grandfather was Yizhu (億株) [?]; his father was You; and his mother was née Xiang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was En and his younger brother was Jie. He married a woman née He. He placed thirty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Xuan, registered in a military household in Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tianyi; he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather was Cong; his father was Zhen; his father's former wife was née Li; and his mother was née Xu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhang, Zan, and Han. He married a woman née Wang. He placed eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

金銑〔貫江西南昌府新建縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子良，行七，年二十九，六月二十八日生〕。曾祖玉，祖日榮，父應隆，母余氏。具慶下，弟鏜、鏞，娶李氏。江西鄉試第五十二名，會試第一百三十四名。

張思靜〔貫陝西西安府同州民籍，國子生，治書經，字伯安，行三，年三十，正月十二日生〕。曾祖琰〔貢士〕，祖績〔知縣〕，父敔，母楊氏。重慶下，兄思魯、思中〔貢士〕，弟思孝、思第、思衛、思誠、思睿、思明、思恭，娶翟氏。陝西鄉試第三名，會試第二百四十四名。
translation_en:
Jin Xian, registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ziliang; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Rirong, and his father Yinglong; his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tang and Yong, and his wife was née Li. He placed fifty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Tang, registered in an artisan household in Suqian County, Pizhou Subprefecture, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Deyang; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Jin, and his father Bi; his mother was née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Song. He placed one hundred sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Sijing, registered in a civilian household in Tongzhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Bo’an; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan, a tribute student; his grandfather was Ji, a district magistrate; and his father was Yu. His mother was née Yang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Silu and Sizhong, the latter a tribute student; his younger brothers were Sixiao, Sidi, Siwei, Sicheng, Sirui, Siming, and Sigong. His wife was née Zhai. He placed third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

高尚文〔貫直隸太平府當塗縣軍籍，縣學生，治春秋，字從周，行三，年二十八，十月二十四日生〕。曾祖源，祖永通，父嵩，母胡氏。具慶下，兄尚志、尚賢，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第二十四名，會試第二百二十八名。
translation_en:
Third class: 208 men, granted the status of graduates assimilated to metropolitan graduates (tong jinshi chushen).

Xiong Mianxue 熊勉學, courtesy name Maolun, was registered with the Ceremonial Guard Office of Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was a native of Dehua County, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers, was twenty-seven years old, and was born on the fourteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather was Ding, an honorary official (yiguan); his father was Xuan, a tribute student; and his mother was née Deng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Mianren and Miancheng, and his younger brother was Mianjia. His wife was née Kong. He placed seventy-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yisong 陳一松, courtesy name Zongyan, was registered in a military household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan; his grandfather was Yue; his father was Yuantao; and his mother was née Cai. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Yigan and Yibai. His wife was née Wu. He placed forty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Shangwen 高尚文, courtesy name Congzhou, was registered in a military household in Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked third among his brothers, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather was Yongtong; his father was Song; and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shangzhi and Shangxian. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

賀鏤〔貫江西吉安府永新縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字邦器，行一，年三十九，十月十二日生〕。曾祖叔正，祖攸，父廷曽，母左氏，繼母陳氏。具慶下，弟鉤、鈺、鈉、鉠，娶歐陽氏。江西鄉試第八十四名，會試第二百四十九名。

陶承學〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字子述，行八，年三十，正月十八日生〕。曾祖愫，祖試〔訓導〕，父廷奎〔歲貢生〕，母商氏。具慶下，兄大有〔刑部主事〕、惟學、大年〔南京兵部郎中〕，弟幼學、勉學、來學、時學、博學、求學、勤學、篤學，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第五十三名，會試第二百八十二名。

劉涇〔貫河南懷慶衛軍籍，直隸靖江縣人，國子生，治詩經，字叔清，行三，年三十八，三月十六日生〕。曾祖通，祖寛，父綱，母何氏，繼母倫氏。具慶下，兄漢、渭，弟溱、瀾、洧，娶戈氏。河南鄉試第四十一名，會試第二百七十名。

錢鯨〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字叔鳴，行五十五，年四十三，九月三十日生〕。曾祖鍰，祖瀚，父re，母馮氏。慈侍下，兄熜、燾，弟鯤、鮪、煌、爐、炫，娶孫氏。浙江鄉試第四名，會試第五十一名。
translation_en:
He Lou 賀鏤, registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bangqi; he ranked first in family birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuzheng, his grandfather You, and his father Tingzeng; his mother was née Zuo and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Gou, Yu, Na, and Yang, and his wife was née Ouyang. He placed eighty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Chengxue 陶承學, registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zishu; he ranked eighth in family birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Su, his grandfather Shi (Assistant Instructor), and his father Tingkui (annual tribute student); his mother was née Shang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dayou (Secretary in the Ministry of Justice), Weixue, and Danian (Director in the Nanjing Ministry of War); his younger brothers were Youxue, Mianxue, Laixue, Shixue, Boxue, Qiuxue, Qinxue, and Duxue. His wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jing 劉涇, registered in a military household of Huaiqing Guard, Henan, and a native of Jingjiang County in Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuqing; he ranked third in family birth order, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Kuan, and his father Gang; his mother was née He and his stepmother née Lun. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Han and Wei, and his younger brothers were Zhen, Lan, and Wei. His wife was née Ge. He placed forty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Jing 錢鯨, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuming; he ranked fifty-fifth in family birth order, was aged forty-three, and was born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather Han, and his father's name is transcribed as “re” [?]; his mother was née Feng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Cong and Tao, and his younger brothers were Kun, Wei, Huang, Lu, and Xuan. His wife was née Sun. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

樊獻科〔貫浙江處州府縉雲縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字文叔，行八十四，年三十，十二月十八日生〕。曾祖祿〔義官〕，祖鐸，父守〔訓導〕，前母施氏，母王氏。具慶下，兄獻忠，弟獻疇、獻綱，娶朱氏。浙江鄉試第三十四名，會試第十五名。
translation_en:
Yao Shixian 姚仕顯, registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanxue; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xiu, a prefectural Clerk; his grandfather was Weitao, a Granary Commissioner; his father was Shifu, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shizhao, Shizhuo, and Shikai, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed seventy-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Tingbiao 宋廷表, registered in a civilian household in Lingui County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jinzhi; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather was Jian, his father was Ru, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingce, Tingjin, and Tingyan, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed first in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Meiyi 楊美益, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yiqian; he ranked fifty-eighth in his family and was thirty-three years old, born on the eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ziren; his grandfather was Shouyang, an honorary official; his father was Maoge, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Bao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Meizhi and Meijue; his younger brothers were Meilu, Meijue [the name appears in both lists: ?], Meiqi, Meizhi, Meiyin, Meiheng, and Meiyu. His wife was née Chen. He placed forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Xianke 樊獻科, registered in a civilian household in Jinyun County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenshu; he ranked eighty-fourth in his family and was thirty years old, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Lu, an honorary official; his grandfather was Duo; and his father was Shou, an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wife was née Shi, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xianzhong, his younger brothers were Xianchou and Xiangang, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

謝江〔貫河南河南衛官籍，國子生，治易經，字仲川，行三，年三十九，十月十八日生〕。曾祖慶，祖旺〔壽官〕，父鑑，前母王氏，母李氏。慈侍下，兄俊、忠，弟淮，娶史氏，繼娶許氏。河南鄉試第七十二名，會試第二百二十六名。

孫永思〔貫山西平陽府蒲州民籍，州學生，治書經，字性孝，行三，年三十八，七月二十九日生〕。曾祖惟溫，祖暹，父𦙍，母李氏。慈侍下，兄邦畿、邦域，弟永恩，娶張氏。山西鄉試第二十四名，會試第一百九十六名。

王樵〔貫直隸鎮江府金壇縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字明逸，行九，年二十七，九月二十六日生〕。曾祖鎮，祖瀚〔贈兵部主事〕，父臬〔按察司副使〕，母于氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄默然、壽默〔監生〕、休默〔監生〕、丞采，弟維能、維熊、夢羔、夢魚，娶虞氏。應天府鄉試第六十七名，會試第二百二十四名。
translation_en:
Li Youzi, registered in a military household in Yingcheng County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuanshu; he ranked first in family order and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Qiong, a prefectural vice prefect; his grandfather was Ming, a county magistrate; his father was Shixiu, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Youpei, Youshu, Youzhi, Youfan, Youshi, and Youzeng. His wife was née Zhou. He placed seventy-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Jiang, registered in an officer household of Henan Guard, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongchuan; he ranked third in family order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather was Wang, an honorary official honored for longevity; his father was Jian; his father’s former wife was née Wang; and his mother was née Li. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Jun and Zhong, and his younger brother was Huai. His wife was née Shi, and his subsequent wife was née Xu. He placed seventy-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yongsi, registered in a civilian household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xingxiao; he ranked third in family order and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Weiwen; his grandfather was Xian; his father was Yin; and his mother was née Li. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Bangji and Bangyu, and his younger brother was Yong’en. His wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qiao, registered in a civilian household in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mingyi; he ranked ninth in family order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather was Han, posthumously appointed a secretary in the Ministry of War; his father was Nie, a surveillance vice commissioner; and his mother was née Yu, granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Moran, Shoumo (an Imperial University student), Xiumo (an Imperial University student), and Chengcai [?]; his younger brothers were Weineng, Weixiong, Menggao, and Mengyu. His wife was née Yu. He placed sixty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Zhongli, registered in a civilian household in Guichi County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Sili, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yixing, a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Puyuan; his father was Shouning; and his mother was née Tan. His father was living and his mother deceased; his younger brother was Zhonghui, and his wife was née Tan. He placed nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pang Jun, registered in a civilian household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mengzhang, he ranked twelfth in his family, and he was forty-five years old, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Zheng; his father was Chen, an Unranked Official; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Wu, Yun, Fu, Xue, Rui, Yue, Yanzhang, En, Xian, and Jing, and his younger brothers were Jie and Yi. His wife was née Yue. He placed forty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Qi, registered in a civilian household in Jiajiang County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Qianbin, he ranked first in his family, and he was forty-seven years old, born on the ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng, a Prefect; his grandfather was Jinglun; his father was Heng, a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased; his younger brother was Jiu. His wife was née Su, and his subsequent wives were née Mo and née Hu. He placed thirty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mi, registered in an artisan household in Nanpi County, Cangzhou Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zijing, he ranked third in his family, and he was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, a Salt Distribution Deputy Commissioner; his grandfather was Xiu, a Registrar; his father was Jizong; and his mother was née Bi. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Dang and Mo, and his younger brothers were Ren and Yan. His wife was née Ma. He placed seventy-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

張淵〔貫河南開封府陳州民籍，浙江鄞縣人，國子生，治易經，字惟本，行三十三，年四十，五月初八日生〕。曾祖旺，祖謙，父鎧，母童氏。永感下。兄洪；弟濬、淪〔監生〕。娶范氏。河南鄉試第六十四名，會試第四十九名。

張敦復〔貫浙江處州府麗水縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字叔中，行四，年三十四，八月十五日生〕。曾祖文炳，祖寧〔訓導〕，父欽〔教諭〕，母葉氏。永感下。兄敦厚、敦仁〔兵部主事〕、敦化。娶薄氏。浙江鄉試第三十五名，會試第二百四十八名。
translation_en:
Yang Shoulu, registered in a military household of Pengcheng Guard and originally from Changsha County, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yunde; he ranked fifth in family order and was aged thirty, born on the eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Zongsheng was posthumously granted, through successive honors, the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Justice. His grandfather Chun was granted the title Director in the Ministry of Revenue and subsequently received successive posthumous grants of the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Justice. His father Zhixue, Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Justice, was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the name Kanghui. His father's former wife, née Zhang, and his mother, née Chen, were each posthumously granted the title Lady. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shouyu, Shouqian (Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate), Shouyue (Prefect), and Shoumo; his younger brothers were Shourang (a government student), Shoupu, and Shoujie. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Benli, registered in a civilian household in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chongdao; he ranked 104th in family order and was aged thirty, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Yongxia, his father Zhi, and his mother a woman née Chen. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Shu and his younger brother Ge. He married a woman née Wu. He placed eighty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yuan, registered in a civilian household in Chenzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and originally from Yin County, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weiben; he ranked thirty-third in family order and was aged forty, born on the eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Qian, his father Kai, and his mother a woman née Tong. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Hong; his younger brothers were Jun and Lun (a National University student). He married a woman née Fan. He placed sixty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dunfu, registered in a civilian household in Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuzhong; he ranked fourth in family order and was aged thirty-four, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wenbing, his grandfather Ning (Assistant Instructor), his father Qin (Instructor), and his mother a woman née Ye. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dunhou, Dunren (Secretary in the Ministry of War), and Dunhua. He married a woman née Bo. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陸佐〔貫浙江衢州府龍游縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字子翼，行二十八，年二十九，十月初七日生〕。曾祖孔彰，祖孟圭〔義官〕，父杞，前母勞氏，母葉氏。嚴侍下，兄仁，弟俊，娶勞氏。浙江鄉試第八十四名，會試第五十七名。

彭範〔貫河南河南府陝州靈寶縣軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字克憲，行四，年三十四，正月二十四日生〕。曾祖滿，祖珪，父儀，母楊氏。具慶下，兄簡、符、籌，弟簪、箴、籍、策，娶張氏，繼娶趙氏。河南鄉試第三十一名，會試第九名。
translation_en:
Sun Shifang 孫世芳, courtesy name Kecheng, was registered in a military household of the Xuanfu Right Guard under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission and was a native of Andong County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Yu, and his father Jixian; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Dong. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shangli 王尚禮, courtesy name Xufu, was registered in a civilian household in Weinan County, Huazhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in his family, was aged forty, and was born on the eleventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiu, an honorary official honored for longevity; his grandfather was Mengchang; and his father was Zheng, a subprefectural assistant magistrate. His mother was née Li and his stepmother née Guo. Both parents were living. His wife was née Shi; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Zuo 陸佐, courtesy name Ziyi, was registered in a civilian household in Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An added student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked twenty-eighth in his family, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kongzhang, his grandfather Menggui, an honorary official recognized for public benefaction, and his father Qi. His father’s former wife was née Lao, and his mother was née Ye. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Ren and his younger brother Jun; his wife was née Lao. He placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Fan 彭範, courtesy name Kexian, was registered in a military household in Lingbao County, Shanzhou Subprefecture, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked fourth in his family, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Man, his grandfather Gui, and his father Yi; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jian, Fu, and Chou, and his younger brothers Zan, Zhen, Ji, and Ce. His wife was née Zhang; he subsequently married a woman née Zhao. He placed thirty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳善治〔貫四川重慶府巴縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字時化，行一，年三十二，四月初一日生〕。曾祖洪演，祖廷佐，父弟，母郭氏。具慶下，兄榮治、大治，弟盛治、嘉治、長治、安治、平治，娶莫氏。四川鄉試第十一名，會試第一百三十三名。
translation_en:
Gan Ru, registered in a military household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhengfu, he ranked fifth in family order, and he was twenty-five, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Xiushen, was an Administration Vice Commissioner, successively granted the posthumous titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Works; his grandfather, Ze, was successively granted the posthumous titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Junior Guardian concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Works; his father, Weilin, was a tribute scholar. His father's former wife and his mother were both née Liu, and his stepmother was née Huang. He had living grandparents and parents. His elder brothers were Su, formerly a prefectural Registrar, and Huo, a student admitted by virtue of official family status; his younger brothers were Qin, Yu, Jie, a student admitted by imperial grace, Yun, an Imperial University student, Cai, Quan, Ming, and Chun. His wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Yilong, registered in a civilian household in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Futu, he ranked forty-second in family order, and he was thirty-nine, born on the third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Gongfu, was posthumously granted the titles Gentleman for Rendering Service and garrison Registrar; his grandfather, Qing, was a garrison Registrar; his father, Xinglu, was formerly a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War. His mother, née Xu, held the title Lady. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Yilin. His wife was née Sun, and his subsequent wives were née Suo and née Xu. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhaoxiang, registered in a salt-producing household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yuantao, he ranked second in family order, and he was thirty-six, born on the twelfth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Fan, his grandfather was Guan, and his father, Shu, was a county Registrar. His mother was née Shi and his stepmother née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother, Jiaxiang, was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Dexiang, Zhongxiang, Dingxiang, Zhengxiang, Kaoxiang, Fengxiang, Yanxiang. His wife was née Chen, and his subsequent wife was née Quan. He placed 116th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shanzhi, registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shihua, he ranked first in family order, and he was thirty-two, born on the first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Hongyan, his grandfather was Tingzuo, his father was Di [?], and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rongzhi and Dazhi; his younger brothers were Shengzhi, Jiazhi, Changzhi, Anzhi, and Pingzhi. His wife was née Mo. He placed eleventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Yan, registered in a civilian household in Lingui County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Simo; he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather, Yu; his father, Ce, a county magistrate; and his mother, née Yuan. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xiang, Qi, Jing, and Gao, and he married a woman née Tu. He placed sixth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Lai, registered in a civilian household in Changshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added-quota student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shiyin; he ranked seventy-third in family order and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Guang; his grandfather, Si, held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness; his father, Lie, was an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Xu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Kui, and his younger brothers were Qin, Jian, and Fa. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Bi was registered in a civilian household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was originally from Yuyao County. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ruliang; he ranked second in family order and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Sui; his grandfather, Ming; his father, Han; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xian, and his younger brother was Nian; he married a woman née Zheng. He placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Keshu, registered in a civilian household in Hongya County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Weixiao; he ranked fourth in family order and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Silong; his grandfather, Fusen, was granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father, Peng, was a prefect. His father's principal wife, née Zhan, was granted the title of Lady for Service; his birth mother was née Yuan. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Kecheng, Keli, Kedi, Kesui, and Keshi; his younger brothers were Keda, Ketong, Keyao, Kexuan, Kejin, and Keyu. He married a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bai Dayong, registered in a military household in Weinan County, Huazhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Youquan; he ranked first in family birth order, was aged forty, and was born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xiu, his grandfather Jun, and his father Jimin; his mother was née Liang. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed thirty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Rulie, registered in a civilian household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he ranked forty-eighth in family birth order, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Jingmeng and grandfather Pang were both district magistrates; his father Shiqiang was a student of the Imperial University. His father’s former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Ni. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Yun; his younger brothers were Ruxiao, Ruxi, and Ruqian. He married a woman née Fan. He placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Dun, registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and a native of Changzhou County, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuhou; he ranked third in family birth order, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twentieth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Keqing, and his father Chen. His father’s former wives were née Wang, Pu, and Mao; his mother was née Wu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Zheng, and his younger brother Xiao. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Gu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Shiji, registered in a civilian household in Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Boyu; he ranked twenty-seventh in family birth order, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Duo was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Respectful Service and Minister for Proper Governance. His grandfather Pu was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his father Ji was an Investigating Censor. His father’s former wife, née Lü, was posthumously granted the title Lady for Courtesy; his mother, née Gong, was granted the same title. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. He married a woman née He and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

郝成性〔貫錦衣衛官籍，直隸江都縣人，國子生，治易經，字存甫，行三，年三十一，六月初六日生〕。曾祖欽，祖泰〔錦衣衛百戶〕，父理，前母方氏，母靳氏。具慶下，兄惠，弟應〔監生〕，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第一百十九名，會試第四十七名。

王健〔貫福建漳州府漳浦縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字于行，行一，年二十九，七月十五日生〕。曾祖勗，祖謐〔知縣〕，父璇〔知縣〕，母陳氏，繼母蘇氏。具慶下，弟侁、僑、俶、倬，娶林氏。福建鄉試第七十八名，會試第七十六名。
translation_en:
Li Yingshi, registered in an artisan household in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Jike; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-nine sui, born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gan, his grandfather Sheng, his father Hailiang, and his mother née Xi. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingzhen, Yingchun, and Yingyang; his wife was née Wang. He placed forty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao De, registered in a commoner household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingfu; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three sui, born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, an honorary official; his grandfather was Yu, his father Yijing, and his mother née Zheng. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His younger brothers were Fu and Kan; his wife was née Hu. He placed ninety-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hao Chengxing, registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and originally from Jiangdu County, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Cunfu; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-one sui, born on the sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin; his grandfather Tai was a Company Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard. His father was Li; his father's former wife was née Fang, and his mother was née Jin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hui; his younger brother Ying was a student of the Directorate of Education. His wife was née Li. He placed 119th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jian, registered in a commoner household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuxing; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-nine sui, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xu; his grandfather Mi and father Xuan were both District Magistrates. His mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Su. His father and stepmother were living. His younger brothers were Shen, Qiao, Chu, and Zhuo; his wife was née Lin. He placed seventy-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lü Kongliang, courtesy name Zixing, was registered in an artisan household in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the nineteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao; his grandfather, Ze, was a Post Station Master; his father, Xiang, was a Steward of Food; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kongjia, and his younger brother was Kongshan. He married a woman née Fang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ling, courtesy name Zicai, was registered in an artisan household in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ju, was an Assistant Subprefect and received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Xuan; his father was Tang; and his mother was née Hu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother, Zhong, was an Imperial University student, and his younger brother was Ying. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Hongyu, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Wu County. An additional student at the county government school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather was Ang; his father was Wen; and his mother was née Huangfu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shien and Shizhong, and his younger brother was Hongzhi. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Zou. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shikui, courtesy name Bochun, was registered in a civilian household in Shuangliu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tianzhong; his grandfather was Wenbi; his father was Chaofeng; and his mother was née Niu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Shichen. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Lian 林燫, registered in a scholarly household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhenheng; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the fifteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Yuanmei, was a prefect, successively granted posthumous titles culminating in Minister of Personnel at Nanjing, with the further posthumous titles of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Works. His grandfather, Han, was Minister of War at Nanjing, posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the name Wen’an. His father, Tingji, was an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy; his mother, née Li, held the title Lady. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan 炫, Assistant Director of the Office of Transmission at Nanjing; Yang 煬, Registrar of the Central Chief Military Commission at Nanjing; Lang 烺; Xuan 炫, an Imperial University student [the name 炫 is repeated in the transcription, possibly in error]; Yu 煜; and Yue 爚. His younger brothers were Qiao 喬 and Zhou 舟 [the reading and division of these two names are uncertain: ?], Jiong 炯, Tong 燑, Kui 煃, and Jing 燝. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qiu 李秋, registered in a civilian household in Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bocheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wenyou; his grandfather was Ao; his father, Gao, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhi 秩, a general, Ji 積, Zhi 稺, and Yu 稢. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Kexiang 徐可相, registered in a civilian household in Lingui County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Maozhong; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the nineteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Hao, was a county Registrar; and his father, Huai, was a department magistrate. His father’s former wife was née Long, and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brother was Kedong, and his younger brother was Kekai. He married a woman née Xiao. He placed fourth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Chengsi 徐承嗣, registered in a civilian household in Suining County, Tongchuan Department, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Kejing; he ranked third among his brothers and was forty-three years old, born on the nineteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Gang, was a prefect; his grandfather was Dabang; his father was Zhong; and his mother was née He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chengzong and Chengzu; his younger brothers were Chengshun, Chengxuan, Chengjiao, Chengxue, and Chengyan. He married a woman née Guo. He placed twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 305th in the Metropolitan Examination.

羅椿〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治《詩經》，字元齡，行一，年三十三，五月二十日生〕。曾祖克謙，祖軏，父觀，母沈氏。具慶下，弟松，娶徐氏，繼娶虞氏。浙江鄉試第六十九名，會試第一百五十六名。
translation_en:
Guo Yue, courtesy name Qizhi, was registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Zuo, and his father Lian; his father's former wife was née Huang and his mother née Zheng; both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Zhong and his younger brothers Feng and Ai; his wife was née Yang; he placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Laizheng, courtesy name Xianfu, was registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Linfen County, Shanxi; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked seventh in family order, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Neng, a general; his grandfather was Wu, a platoon commander entitled to wear official cap and sash; his father was Zhao, formerly Assistant Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, and his mother was née Yang; both parents were living; his elder brother Mengzheng was a department magistrate; he married a woman née Wei and subsequently a woman née Yang; he placed 115th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yunzhong, courtesy name Rushi, was registered in an officer household of the Rear Battalion of the Taiyuan Right Guard, Shanxi; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked second in family order, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Jing, his father Xian, and his mother née Qian; his father was living and his mother deceased; his elder brother was Chaoyang and his younger brothers Yunsheng, Chaodong, Yunde, Yungong, Yunzhi, and Chaofeng; his wife was née Zhang; he placed thirty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Chun, courtesy name Yuanling, was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household; he was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the twentieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Keqian, his grandfather Yue, his father Guan, and his mother née Shen; both parents were living; his younger brother was Song; he married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Yu; he placed sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhuang Yingzhen, registered in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xizhou; he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirtieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Ting’ai, his grandfather Yuanji, and his father Zhang; his mother was née He. His father was still living, and his mother had died. His elder brothers were Yinghong, Yingwen, and Yingzeng. He married a woman née Hong. He ranked twentieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bian Yi, registered in Xiajiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Dehong; he was ninth in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Huiming, his grandfather Jingxiang, and his father Chun; his mother was née Yin, and his stepmother née Yuan. Both parents had died. His elder brothers were Zhong and Zhi. He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Li. He ranked forty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Dongbai, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shuxiao; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Qian was an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather Hui received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His father Bi was a Prefect, advanced to the rank of Grand Master of the Second Class (Yazhong dafu); his mother, née Yu, received the title Lady of Respect. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Dongdu, Dongjiang, Dongye, Donghui, Donglin, Dongchun, Dongshi, and Dongchang. He married a woman née Ke. He ranked forty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zun, registered in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gonglu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twentieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhishan, his grandfather Qu, and his father Bi; his mother was née Shen, and his stepmother née Sun. His father had died, and his mother was still living. His younger brothers were Dao, Sui, and Mai. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Hu. He ranked sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Tingmei, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yuhe, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was forty-seven, born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zinan, his grandfather Jiehao, his father Bofeng, and his mother Lady Xiao; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Tingqing, a Police Chief, Tingzan, Tingliang, and Tingxiang; his younger brothers were Tingxu, Tingdao, Tingbing, Tinggao, and Tingbin, the last three being tribute students. He married Lady Hu and placed forty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Ruxian, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Yungong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ang, his grandfather Quan, his father Yingqian, and his mother Lady Xu; his parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Rubin, Ruzhen, and Ruji. He married Lady Zou and placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Kai, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ciyuan, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was thirty-four, born on the thirtieth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather Hao, his father Yuan, and his mother Lady Jiang; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Chen and Qing, the latter a tribute student, and his younger brother was Ti. He married Lady Xia and subsequently Lady Zhang; he placed forty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Ziyun, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Mingzhong, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-four, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Yuan, his father Bingwen, an Instructor at the Imperial University, and his mother Lady Yao; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Ziyuan; his younger brothers were Zixian, Zidui, Ziyao, Zichong, and Ziguang. He married Lady Zhou and placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

于業〔貫直隸鎭江府金壇縣，軍籍，縣學生，治禮記，字建公，行二，年三十，十月初十日生〕。曾祖盛〔贈通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，祖鎰〔知縣，封兵部郎中，贈通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，父泗，母王氏。慈侍下，兄棐〔監生〕，弟未〔監生〕、柬、集，娶高氏。應天府鄉試第三十一名，會試第二百二十二名。

黃季瑞〔貫福建福州府閩縣，民籍，府學增廣生，治春秋，字宗和，行三，年三十九，十二月十二日生〕。曾祖孜，祖珙，父源大〔知縣〕，嫡母金氏，生母趙氏。永感下，兄孟台、仲陽〔教授〕，娶阮氏，繼娶陳氏。福建鄉試第二十二名，會試第一百七十九名。

李天榮〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字仁卿，行四，年三十一，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖洪貴，祖大勲，父時俊，母周氏。慈侍下，弟天華、天憲，娶樊氏，繼娶喻氏。江西鄉試第四十一名，會試第二百六十二名。

曹禾〔貫浙江嘉興府平湖縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字世嘉，行二，年三十三，九月二十二日生〕。曾祖斌，祖瑜，父渭〔驛丞〕，母陳氏。具慶下，兄采，弟耒、桐、東，娶朱氏。浙江鄉試第七十四名，會試第七十一名。
translation_en:
Yu Ye, registered in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Jiangong; he ranked second among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Sheng was posthumously conferred the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Yi, a county magistrate, was honorarily conferred the title of Director in the Ministry of War and posthumously conferred the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father was Si, and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother Fei and younger brother Wei were Imperial University students; his other younger brothers were Jian and Ji. He married a woman née Gao. He placed thirty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Jirui, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the prefectural school, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zonghe; he ranked third among his brothers, was thirty-nine years old, and was born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zi, his grandfather Gong, and his father Yuanda, a county magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Jin, and his birth mother was née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mengtai and Zhongyang, the latter a prefectural school instructor. He married a woman née Ruan and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tianrong, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Renqing; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was thirty-one years old, and was born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Honggui, his grandfather Daxun, his father Shijun, and his mother née Zhou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Tianhua and Tianxian. He married a woman née Fan and subsequently a woman née Yu. He placed forty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao He, registered in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shijia; he ranked second among his brothers, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Yu, his father Wei, a stationmaster, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cai, and his younger brothers were Lei, Tong, and Dong. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed seventy-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃履旋〔貫福建福州府侯官縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字性之，行二，年三十四，五月初九日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖亨〔巡檢〕，父繼文，母彭氏。永感下，弟履謙、履端、履經，娶李氏，繼娶陳氏。福建鄉試第三十四名，會試第二百十六名。
translation_en:
Huangfu Huan, registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shiheng, and he ranked third in his family. He was thirty-eight years old, born on the seventeenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingbi; his grandfather was Jie, an honorary official; his father was Mu, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing; his younger brothers were Pan, a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi), Pang, Cheng, Han, Pei, Jin, Yi, Yue, Chao, and Zhan. He married a woman née Shen. He placed ninety-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Bochen, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wengong, and he ranked ninth in his family. He was thirty-two years old, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jilin; his grandfather was Qiling; his father was Chu, and his mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Boxiao, Boyan, an official attending provincial sacrifices, Boyun, and Boai. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fifty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Rudou, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yunwen, and he ranked twenty-ninth in his family. He was thirty-six years old, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tinglan; his grandfather was Yun; his father was Jing, and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Rudi, Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and Rushan, a County Vice Magistrate; his younger brothers were Rudeng, Rulun, a student of the Directorate of Education, Rujiang, and Ruhan. He married a woman née Mao. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Lüxuan, registered in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xingzhi, and he ranked second in his family. He was thirty-four years old, born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Heng, a Police Chief; his father was Jiwen, and his mother was née Peng. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Lüqian, Lüduan, and Lüjing. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yuan Guanghan, registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xianfu, he ranked second in family order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Wenyuan, his grandfather Xichu, and his father Kui, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Fu, and his father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Guangru, a Department Magistrate, Guangxiang, Guangbiao, and Guangpeng; his younger brother was Guangchen, and his wife was née Li. He placed thirteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Sigong, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rumao, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jingsong, his grandfather Yong’an, and his father Bo; his mother was née Fang, and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sixun and Silie, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Yuchen, registered in a civilian household in Changsha County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ziyi, he ranked third in family order, and he was aged forty, born on the second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Degui, and his father Ren, a Professor; his mother was née Xiang, and both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yaochen and Shunchen, his younger brother was Tangchen, and his wife was née Yang. He placed twenty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Bopeng, registered in a civilian household in Yiwu County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weixi, he ranked ninety-ninth in family order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Wengao, his grandfather Lan, and his father Qiong, an Instructor; his mother was née Cai and his stepmother née Jin, and he had both parents and a grandparent or grandparents living. His elder brothers were Boyuan and Bozhong; his younger brothers were Boshun, Boqian, Bohou, Bolu, and Bobian, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shen Huai, courtesy name Chengbo, was registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-six, born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Zhi, held an honorary longevity title; his father was Deming, and his mother was née Ni. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yi, Bo, Song, and Lan. His wife was née He. He placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yuyuan, courtesy name Yingqian, was registered in a military household of Lin'an Guard, Yunnan, and was a native of Jiangdu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Sen, his father Fu, and his mother née Ye. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Diaoyuan. His wife was née Zhang; he subsequently married a woman née Ren. He placed fifty-second in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Meizhong, courtesy name Daohua, was registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Wu County. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da, his grandfather Guang, his father Liexiu, and his mother née Cao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Huazhong, Yingzhong, and Yangzhong; his younger brothers were Maozhong, Yunzhong, Huazhong [?—listed among both elder and younger brothers], Weizhong, and Bingzhong. His wife was née Qian. He placed forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shouren, courtesy name Yu'an, was registered in a civilian household in Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Hui, his father Shi, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Huairen. His wife was née Tian. He placed nineteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather was Ang, an honorary official for longevity; his father was Jie; and his mother was née Shi. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Weihe, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed thirteenth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Lin, registered in a civilian household of Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a department school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shenzheng; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather was Cong; his father was Zongyi, a Departmental Assistant Judge; and his mother was née Song. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Xu, Dao 道, and Dao 導; his younger brother was Xuan; and his wife was née Gao. He placed 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yi, registered in a civilian household of Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Sizhan; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shouzong, a Professor; his grandfather was Ruyue; his father was Tang, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Wei. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Bao, his younger brother was Biao, and his wife was née Tang. He placed thirty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Guan, registered in a civilian household of Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weizheng; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Cong, a Vice Prefect; his grandfather was Ren; his father was Sishan, a Station Master; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Cai and Shou. His wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Mengzhang; his grandfather, Yuan, a Chief Office Clerk; and his father, Chong. His legal mothers were née Zhou and née Zhu, and his birth mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Qiao and Ju. His wife was née Wu. He ranked fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Wu [?], registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiyan; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Rongshan; his grandfather, Luan; his father, Shangjiong; his mother, née Zhou; and his stepmother, née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sheng, Jian, a tribute student, Guo, and Da. His wife was née He. He ranked twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Dongfan, registered in a civilian household in Jinxiang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenfu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Wen; his father, Nang [?]; and his mother, née Huang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Dongjing. His wife was née Li. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Rumo, registered in Jinghai County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shiyan. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pan, a Guard Registrar; his grandfather was Shao, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Bangqi, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rujian, Ruhou, Ruqi (a student of the Directorate of Education), Ruzhong, Rucai, and Rushen. He married a woman née Li and subsequently married women née Wang and née Qi. He ranked 106th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Weiju, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhifu. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiweng; his grandfather was Gongming; his father was Jingcai, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Weixue, and his younger brother was Weixing. He married a woman née Yuan. He ranked twenty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Ren, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jingfu. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather was Chou; his father was Yin, and his mother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Ru. He married a woman née Zou. He ranked 131st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yunlu, registered in Gaoping County, Zezhou Subprefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Bodeng. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jue; his grandfather was Zineng; his father was Lei, and his mother was née Fan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tiande and Yunteng. He married a woman née Guo. He ranked twelfth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Yuanbai, registered in Dazhou, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the departmental school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yongzhang. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Shiliang; his father was Gao, a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Tian. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yuandi, Yuanzheng, Yuankai, Yuansi, and Yuanjin. He married a woman née Tang. He placed fourteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chenghua, registered in Quwo County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shifu. He ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, a County Vice Magistrate, honorifically appointed Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works and successively granted the posthumous titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of War. His grandfather was Hao, Grand Master for Aid in Governance, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Rites, posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the name Zhuangjian. His father was Yong, Assistant Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture; his mother was née Xu, granted the title Lady of Respectfulness. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengguang, a student admitted by virtue of an official’s privilege, and Chengde, a student of the Directorate of Education. His younger brothers were Chengzhao and Chengci, both students of the Directorate of Education, and Chengchong. He married a woman née Fu and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xiuji, registered in Xincai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yijing. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zong; his grandfather was Bing; his father was Jie; and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brothers were Zhengji and Xingji. He married a woman née Ji and subsequently women née Dai and née Ma. He placed twenty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Tang, registered in Tunliu County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shiyong. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin; his grandfather was Yongqian; his father was Lun; and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brothers were Yu, Mo, Xian, Gao, Xun, and Zhao. He married a woman née Yin and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.
