陳學夔〔貫廣西慶遠府宜山縣，民籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字汝諧，行一，年二十九，四月十四日生〕。曾祖謙，祖廣惠〔義官〕，父策〔推官〕，母李氏。慈侍下，弟學益，娶宋氏。廣西鄉試第三十名，會試第一百二十四名。

岳粹〔貫山東東昌府冠縣，民籍，國子生，治《書經》，字純甫，行一，年三十五，十月十二日生〕。曾祖祥，祖隆〔壽官〕，父恂，母苗氏。慈侍下，弟秔，娶吳氏。山東鄉試第五十八名，會試第一百四十九名。
translation_en:
Gao Yue, courtesy name Wenhua, was registered in a civilian household in Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the department school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in birth order and was aged forty, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather, Fu, was a county magistrate; and his father, Gong, was an instructor. His father's principal wife was née Yu, and his birth mother was née Luo. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were He, Zhu, and Xi, and his younger brother was Qiao. He married a woman née Cai. He placed ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Shengfang, courtesy name Shiwu, was registered in a military household in Qi County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather, Wei, was commissioner of a Tax Office and was posthumously granted the title of county magistrate; his grandfather, Rui, was vice commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission. His father was Shixian, and his mother was née Chen; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shaofang and Jifang, and his younger brothers were Lianfang, Jifang, Zuanfang, Mianfang, and Weifang. He married a woman née Wu. He placed twenty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xuekui, courtesy name Ruxie, was registered in a civilian household in Yishan County, Qingyuan Prefecture, Guangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather, Guanghui, held an honorary title for charitable contributions; and his father, Ce, was a prefectural judge. His mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Xueyi, and he married a woman née Song. He placed thirtieth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yue Cui, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in a civilian household in Guan County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather, Long, held an honorary title for longevity; and his father was Xun. His mother was née Miao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Jing, and he married a woman née Wu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

屈諫〔貫山西潞安府長治縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字正父，行十一，年三十三，八月初二日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖端，父俊〔壽官〕，母張氏。慈侍下，兄誠、謹、鎧、珣、龍、環、展、方直、廷美，娶宋氏。山西鄉試第二十五名，會試第二百八十五名。

李价〔貫廣東廣州府番禺縣，軍籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字少藩，行一，年二十五，十一月二十九日生〕。曾祖政，祖科，父士鸞，母陳氏。重慶下，弟材、柄、樞、楹、機、模、楨、杜，娶衛氏。廣東鄉試第七名，會試第一百五十九名。
translation_en:
Zhang Jiafu, registered in Anding County, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yizhen, and he ranked second in family order. He was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Wensheng; his father, E, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother, née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiaxing, and his younger brothers were Jiazhao, Jiaheng, and Jiaji. He married a woman née Nan. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Xiang, registered in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Lüxiang, and he ranked forty-seventh in family order. He was thirty-four years old, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather, Xuan; his father, Ren; and his mother, née Wu. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Chu, and his younger brother was Xi. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qu Jian, registered in Changzhi County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zhengfu, and he ranked eleventh in family order. He was thirty-three years old, born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Duan; his father, Jun, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; and his mother, née Zhang. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Cheng, Jin, Kai, Xun, Long, Huan, Zhan, Fangzhi, and Tingmei. He married a woman née Song. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jie, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was an added student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shaofan, and he ranked first in family order. He was twenty-five years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather, Ke; his father, Shiluan; and his mother, née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Cai, Bing, Shu, Ying, Ji, Mo, Zhen, and Du. He married a woman née Wei. He placed seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Hong 羅鴻, courtesy name Tingyou, was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a student of the Panyu County school. He specialized in the Book of Rites, was first in birth order, and was twenty-eight sui old, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Weizheng; his grandfather, Shan, was a County Magistrate; his father, Xian, was a tribute student; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were E, Luan, and Peng, and his wife was née Li. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bin 李彬, courtesy name Guohua, was registered in a military household of the Taizhou Guard Battalion in the Metropolitan Region and was a native of Youxi County, Fujian. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. First in birth order, he was thirty-two sui old, born on the third day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather, Da; his father, Chao; and his mother, née Fan. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Xing, and his wife was née Feng. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Shidan 殷士儋, courtesy name Zhengfu, was registered in a civilian household in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, and was a native of Wuding Subprefecture. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Rites. First in birth order, he was twenty-six sui old, born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather, Heng, was an Adjudicator; his grandfather, Jun, was a tribute student; his father was Rulin; and his mother was née Guo. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His wife was née Zhai. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Daokun 汪道昆, courtesy name Yuqing, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. He was an added-quota student of the prefectural school and specialized in the Book of Rites. First in birth order, he was twenty-three sui old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather, Xuanyi; his father, Liangbin; and his mother, née Hu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Daotan, Daoguan, and Daohui. His first wife was née Wu, and his subsequent wife was also née Wu. He placed ninetieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Chongwen, registered in a civilian household in Gaoping County, Zezhou, Shanxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuanzhi, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was twenty-six years old, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuang; his grandfather, Yun; and his father, Tao, an annual tribute student. His father's former wives were Lady Cheng and Lady Yuan, and his mother was Lady Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chongdao and Chongde, and his younger brother was Chongru. He married Lady Zhang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Can, registered in a military household in Dongguang County, Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Huifu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongheng, a Registrar; his grandfather, Yuan, a Professor; and his father, Song. His mother was Lady Zhang, and his stepmother was Lady Fan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Huan, and his younger brothers were Wei, Yao, Ye, Zhao, Lian, Jiong, Zhuo, and Huang. He married Lady Mu. He placed 135th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li You, registered in an official household in Qingping Guard, Guizhou, and originating from Chong'an County, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jifu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather, Chun, an Instructor; and his father, Kui, a Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice. His mother was Lady Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zuo, a District Magistrate. He married Lady Bai. He placed sixth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Qing, registered in an artisan household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyang, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was thirty-six years old, born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, a Professor posthumously granted the title of Prefect; his grandfather, Siyuan, a Prefect; and his father, Jin. His mother was Lady Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Cheng, Hong, Ying, Pan, and Hun. He married Lady Jin. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

鄭真〔貫山東濟寧衛，軍籍，湖廣黃岡縣人，國子生，治易經，字惟誠，行二，年四十一，九月初八日生〕。曾祖興，祖通〔封南京戶部主事〕，父文炳〔知府〕，母王氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，兄直，娶周氏，繼娶孫氏。山東鄉試第七十二名，會試第一百六十七名。

丘岳〔貫湖廣黃州府黃岡縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字子瞻，行五，年二十九，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖端文，祖大鵬，父尚忠，母熊氏。慈侍下，兄山、坤、均、坦，弟增、坊，娶黃氏。湖廣鄉試第四十一名，會試第一百七十四名。

translation_en:
Huang Deng 黃燈, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuandeng; he ranked sixth among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, a prefect; his grandfather was Dou; his father was Gaoqing; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi, Dian (a tribute scholar), Cheng, Yi, and Tan. His wife was née Gan. He placed thirtieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Zhen 鄭真, registered in Jining Guard, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a native of Huanggang County, Huguang. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weicheng; he ranked second among his brothers, was forty-one years old, and was born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather was Tong, granted the title of secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his father was Wenbing, a prefect; and his mother was née Wang, granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Zhi. His wife was née Zhou; he subsequently married a woman née Sun. He placed seventy-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Yue 丘岳, registered in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zizhan; he ranked fifth among his brothers, was twenty-nine years old, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duanwen; his grandfather was Dapeng; his father was Shangzhong; and his mother was née Xiong. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Shan, Kun, Jun, and Tan; his younger brothers were Zeng and Fang. His wife was née Huang. He placed forty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Jin 段錦, registered in En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Meizhong; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Xing; his father was Wengao; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His wife was née Zheng; he subsequently married another woman née Zheng. He placed twenty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qiu Wei, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shizhang; he ranked third among his brothers, was twenty years old, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Xian, his father Shan, and his mother née Liu. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Jing; his younger brothers were Zu, Shen, Gang, and Yue. His wife was née Ding. He placed fifty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Bingren, registered in a military household of Guizhou Guard in Guizhou and originally from Daye County, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyuan; he ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the twentieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Zeng, his father Heng (a department magistrate), and his mother née Hao. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Bingyi and Bingli. His wife was née Tang. He placed twelfth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Que, registered in a military household of Jiangyin Guard under Nanjing and originally from Tianchang County in the directly administered region, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanzhi; he ranked third among his brothers, was twenty-six years old, and was born on the eighteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benxiang, his grandfather Xu, his father Heng, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gan; his younger brothers were Que [?], Wen, and Heng. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Weishan, registered in a military household in Xincai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Poufu; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was He, his grandfather Di (an honorary official for longevity), his father Hong, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

嚴侍下　弟席　廣　廉　厚　音　廩　襄　娶朱氏
福建鄉試第八名　會試第四名
punctuated:
鄭銘〔貫福建福州府閩縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治春秋，字警吾，行三，年三十七，十一月初六日生〕。曾祖普，祖壽，父德全，嫡母林氏、楊氏，生母林氏。慈侍下，娶林氏，繼娶黃氏、陳氏。福建鄉試第六十七名，會試第八十八名。

楊巍〔貫山東濟南府武定州海豐縣人，縣學生，治易經，字伯謙，行二，年三十一，五月十四日生〕。曾祖麟〔義官〕，祖斌〔義官〕，父光祖〔陰陽官〕，母安氏。具慶下，兄崇，弟巖，娶陳氏。山東鄉試第四十八名，會試第一百八名。

祝天保〔貫直隸順德府唐山縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字惟忠，行一，年三十四，八月二十三日生〕。曾祖榮，祖賓〔壽官〕，父明〔義官〕，前母郭氏，母李氏。永感下，弟天祐、天眷、天祚，娶許氏。順天府鄉試第一百二名，會試第一百九十五名。

陳言〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，府學生，治書經，字宜昌，行一，年四十一，七月三十日生〕。曾祖德誠〔壽官〕，祖必清〔壽官〕，父一通，母黃氏。嚴侍下，弟席、廣、廡、厚、音、廩、襄，娶朱氏。福建鄉試第八名，會試第四名。
translation_en:
Zheng Ming, registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Jingwu; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu, his grandfather Shou, and his father Dequan. His legal mothers were née Lin and née Yang; his birth mother was née Lin. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. He married a woman née Lin, then successively women née Huang and née Chen. He placed sixty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Wei, a native of Haifeng County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Boqian; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Lin and grandfather Bin each held an honorary official title for philanthropy. His father Guangzu was an official of the School of Yin and Yang; his mother was née An. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chong, and his younger brother Yan. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Tianbao, registered in a civilian household in Tangshan County, Shunde Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weizhong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather Bin held an honorary official title for longevity, and his father Ming held an honorary official title for philanthropy. His father's former wife was née Guo, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Tianyou, Tianjuan, and Tianzuo. He married a woman née Xu. He placed 102nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yan, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yichang; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the thirtieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Decheng and grandfather Biqing each held an honorary official title for longevity. His father was Yitong, and his mother was née Huang. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His younger brothers were Xi, Guang, Wu, Hou, Yin, Lin, and Xiang. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

李如桂〔貫山西潞安府長治縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字希賓，行一，年二十八，九月初六日生〕。曾祖翥〔知縣〕，祖玹〔縣丞，贈監察御史〕，父延昌〔七品散官〕，前母趙氏，母章氏。具慶下，弟如楠、如松，娶王氏，繼娶宋氏、閻氏。山西鄉試第二十二名，會試第二百三十六名。

丘預達〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，匠籍，縣學生，治書經，字若孚，行五，年四十，八月十七日生〕。曾祖希高，祖朝輔，父璞，母許氏。永感下，兄預馨、預學、預進、預彰，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第八十一名，會試第九十六名。

吳俊〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字子魯，行五，年三十八，正月初六日生〕。曾祖文深，祖瑜，父廷寅，母張氏。具慶下，兄倬，弟偉，娶何氏。浙江鄉試第七十四名，會試第一百五十四名。

狄斯彬〔貫應天府溧陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字文中，行六，年四十三，十二月初八日生〕。曾祖竭，祖欽〔贈南京工部郎中〕，父津，母葛氏，繼母楊氏。永感下，弟斯本、斯東，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第六十一名，會試第十二名。
translation_en:
Li Rugui, registered in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xibin, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhu, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Xuan, a District Vice Magistrate posthumously awarded the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Yanchang, a holder of seventh-rank prestige office; his father’s former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Runan and Rusong; he married a woman née Wang and subsequently women née Song and née Yan. He placed twenty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Yuda, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an artisan household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruofu, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged forty, born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xigao, his grandfather was Chaofu, his father was Pu, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Yuxin, Yuxue, Yujin, and Yuzhang; he married a woman née Zheng. He placed eighty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Jun, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zilu, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenshen, his grandfather was Yu, his father was Tingyin, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Zhuo and his younger brother was Wei; he married a woman née He. He placed seventy-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Di Sibin, registered in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenzhong, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was aged forty-three, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather was Qin, posthumously awarded the title of Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works; his father was Jin, his mother was née Ge, and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased; his younger brothers were Siben and Sidong; he married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳觀衡〔貫山東兖州府東平州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字季平，行三，年三十，五月二十一日生〕。曾祖忠，祖校，父善道〔省祭官〕，母于氏。具慶下，兄觀順、觀瀾，娶張氏。山東鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百三十一名。

李敏德〔貫山西潞安府長治縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字伯脩，行二，年三十一，四月二十七日生〕。曾祖貴〔贈錦衣衛經歷〕，祖紀〔運使〕，父汝佑〔儀賓〕，母臨汾縣主。具慶下，兄敏政，弟敏求，娶王氏。山西鄉試第十三名，會試第一百四十二名。
translation_en:
Zhang Zhu, courtesy name Ruren, was from Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and registered in a military household. An added-quota student at the county school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked eighth in family order and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiu, an Honorary Official for Philanthropy; his grandfather was Zhan; his father was Dongyang, granted the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; and his mother, née Ma, was granted the title of Lady of Tranquility. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hang, Liangfu, Liangbi, Liangzuo, Biao (a Prefect), Duo, and Cui; his younger brother was Ge. He married a woman née Liu. He placed forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tianfu, courtesy name Fuheng, was from Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. He ranked fourteenth in family order and was aged thirty-five, born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gong; his grandfather was Zongsheng, a titular official of the seventh rank; his father was Zhao; and his mother was née Zhao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Tianqu, a Department Magistrate, and Tiande. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Guanheng, courtesy name Jiping, was from Dongping Department, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked third in family order and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather was Xiao; his father was Shandao, a Provincial Sacrificial Official; and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guanshun and Guanlan. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Minde, courtesy name Boxiu, was from Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Classic of Documents. He ranked second in family order and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, posthumously granted the title of Registrar in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; his grandfather was Ji, a Salt Distribution Commissioner; his father was Ruyou, a Ceremonial Consort; and his mother was the County Princess of Linfen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Minzheng and his younger brother Minqiu. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Minjing, of Shanyin County, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zizhuang. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiuling, his grandfather Zan, and his father Mian, a student of the Directorate of Education. His father's former wives were Lady Gao and Lady Liu; his mother was Lady Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Minwang and his younger brother Minxin; he married Lady Ba. He placed forty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Hengjia, of Chaoyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuanhui. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty-eight, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qianchao, his grandfather Zhonggang, his father Zhe, and his mother Lady Cheng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Hengqu, Hengbang, and Hengdao; he married Lady Chen. He placed thirteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chence, of Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shidong. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Gong, an Instructor; his father was Jiao, and his mother Lady Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chenshan and his younger brother Chenfan; he married Lady He. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Liang, of Qingliu County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tingcai. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yonghe, his grandfather Jin, his father Xiwen, and his mother Lady Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xiang; he married Lady Chen. He placed sixty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sui Mingcai, registered in Zi County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zheqing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was forty-four years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather was Shangbin, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Chaoyang; his legal mother was née Huang, and his birth mother was née Xiong. His parents were deceased. His elder brother, Tingcai, was a Director of Food Services. He married a woman née Tian. He placed sixty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Jing, registered in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruming, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was thirty-three years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Daoheng; his grandfather was Song; his father was Jun, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Yi, was a District Magistrate, and his younger brother was Wei. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Xun belonged to the banner register of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zizhong, ranked first among his brothers, and was forty-one years old, born on the tenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather was Qing; his father was Qin; and his mother was née Zhao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Chu. He placed 125th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Wenhan, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhangqing, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was forty years old, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Kan, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Zhang; his father was Quan, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Wenzhi. He married a woman née Lin. He placed fifty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Yi 徐鷁, courtesy name Mingchuan, was registered in a salt-producing household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. Second in birth order, he was aged forty-one and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Zongsi, his father Yu, and his mother née Tang; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was He and his younger brother Peng. He married née Yu. He placed forty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Kuo 章适, courtesy name Jingnan, was registered in a civilian household in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Pang, his father Zhi (a tribute scholar, gongshi), and his mother née Xu; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Hu, and his younger brothers were Shu (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Mai, Qian, Hou, and Bian [the last three names are doubtful in the transcription]. He married née Ling. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yue Qiya 樂其雅, courtesy name Bisuo, was registered in a military household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Fengming, his father Jia, and his mother née Liu; both parents were living. His elder brother was Qiwen, and his younger brothers were Qimo and Qixian. He married née Yang and subsequently married née Kong and née Xu. He placed seventeenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wanji 張萬紀, courtesy name Shunqing, was registered in a military household of Lintao Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Zhouzhi County. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Rui, his father Huai, and his mother née Wu; both parents were living. His younger brother was Wanlu. He married née Jiang and subsequently married née Yang. He placed forty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Hai, registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rurong, and he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shu, Office Manager in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Bing, Registrar in the Office of Transmission; his father was Zhong, and his mother was née Yan. His father was still living, and his mother was deceased. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked 108th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Yinglin, registered in Jiande County, Chizhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shirui, and he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Changqing; his grandfather was Sheng, an Assistant Instructor; and his father was Yichang. His father’s former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Wei. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His younger brother was Yingqi. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Yang. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jiamo, registered in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shixian, and he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather was Hengxian, who held an honorary title for longevity; his father was Wen, and his mother was née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Jiaxun and Jiamou. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked seventeenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Shi, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Chunfu, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ping; his grandfather was Bo, an Instructor in a subprefectural Confucian school; his father was Guorong, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Mo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jie; his younger brothers were Cai, Xian (a sacrificial attendant [?]), Xuan, Nian, and Wei. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently women née Wu and née Yao. He ranked seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qin Liang, courtesy name Zicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yongfu, officially honored for filial piety; his grandfather was Tang, Office Manager in the Nanjing Censorate; his father was Han, and his mother was née Yin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cai, an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were He, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Fen, Can, Jie, Fei, Nan, and Muqu [?]. His wife was née Chen. He placed ninety-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Fei, courtesy name Wenhui, was registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixth in family birth order and was aged forty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jiyang; his grandfather was Shunmo; his father was Mian, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Nie, and his stepmother was née Gao. His mother alone survived. His younger brother was Gong, and his wife was née Yang. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Peng, courtesy name Runan, was registered in a civilian household in Zaoqiang County, Jizhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family birth order and was aged twenty-six, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather was Congshan; his father was Ze, and his mother was née He. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zhi, Lu, Zi, and E, and his wife was née Lu. He placed fifteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Yingqian, courtesy name Jiqing, was registered in a military household of Wuqing Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked ninety-third in family birth order and was aged thirty, born on the ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Fan, a seventh-rank prestige official; his grandfather was Yimo, posthumously appointed a Guard Registrar; his father was Yunyang, a Subprefectural Vice Magistrate; and his mother was née Wei, granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father alone survived. His elder brothers were Yingchun, Yingshi, a Subprefectural Magistrate, Yingqi, Yingbi, an Imperial University student, Yingqian, a Guard Registrar, Yingkui, and Yingxuan; his younger brothers were Yingji and Yingyi. His wife was née Ge. He placed 120th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Xiao, courtesy name Dongbai, was registered in a civilian household in Jixi County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. He was an additional student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Documents. Second in family order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the twenty-first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian’an; his grandfather, Sheng; and his father, Tingchu. His father’s former wife was née Hong, and his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ming, and his younger brothers were Shi, Dan, Gao, Chang, and Bing. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Tang, courtesy name Zhongsheng, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a prefectural school student and specialized in the Book of Documents. Thirty-eighth in family order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunzhong; his grandfather, Kui, an Assistant Instructor; and his father, Fengshan. His mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jian and Quan. His wife was née Mao. He placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shi, courtesy name Shiyin, was registered in a military household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. Sixth in family order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zi; his grandfather, Kun; and his father, Tianmin. His mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Hou, Chu, Ji, Feng, and Fang. His wife was née Pu. He placed 112th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Limin, courtesy name Shanfu, was registered in a civilian household in Dongguang County, Jing Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Second in family order, he was thirty-nine years old and was born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Xian, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan) [?]; and his father, Gang, who held the honorary title of Longevity Official. His mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Aimin, and his younger brothers were Baomin, Yumin, Jimin, and Zhimin. His wife was née Li; he subsequently married a woman née Yang. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

沈晃〔貫直隸鎮江府丹徒縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字克昭，行十一，年四十四，十一月十八日生〕。曾祖彤，祖毅，父瑀〔壽官〕，前母林氏，母汪氏。永感下，兄魯〔訓導〕、鼎、鼐、昱、昂、杲、昇、昆、勗、顯、景，娶馮氏。應天府鄉試第四十三名，會試第十九名。
translation_en:
Liu Lusheng: registered in En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xikong; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Jin, was a County Chief Clerk; his father, Gao, was a Registrar. His mother was née Ma, and his stepmothers were née Guo and née Fang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Luosheng, a Subprefect, Guansheng, Minsheng, and Yansheng. He married a woman née Sun and subsequently a woman née Shang. He placed forty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Sancai: registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household, and originally from Deqing County; a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Sican; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather, Jingxian, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his father was Long, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sanyuan, Sanwei, and Sanxing; his younger brothers were Sanxi and Sangang. He married a woman née Jia. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yun: registered in Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household; a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiuqing; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Chang; his father was Zhongyu, and his mother was née Zhu. His mother was deceased, and he attended his surviving father. His younger brothers were Zhuang, a Sacrificial Attendant, Hui, Jian, and Zhen. He married a woman née Ren. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Huang: registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, in a military household; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Kezhao; he ranked eleventh in birth order and was aged forty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Yi; his father, Yu, held an honorary title for longevity. His father's former wife was née Lin, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Lu, an Assistant Instructor, Ding, Nai, Yu, Ang, Gao, Sheng, Kun, Xu, Xian, and Jing. He married a woman née Feng. He placed forty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Gang, courtesy name Zhenfu, was registered in a military household in Cao County, Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather was Jian, a sacrificial official; his father was Zhen; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ji, and his younger brothers were Jiong and Xiu. He married a woman née Zheng. He ranked twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Renyong, courtesy name Ruqin, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Kunshan County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-seven, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xun, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Hui, a titular official of the seventh rank; his father was Shiyu; and his mother was née Xiang, officially honored as a chaste widow. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Sanxi, a subprefect; Sanjie, a prefect; Sangu and Sanpin, both Imperial University students; and Sanchong. He married a woman née Qian. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Dayou, courtesy name Shisheng, was registered in an official household of Haining Guard, Zhejiang, and was a native of Haiyan County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Gong, grandfather Jian, and father Yong were all guard commanders. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Shen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Dabang, a guard commander, and Dazheng; his younger brother was Dahua. He married a woman née Ma. He ranked twentieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zongmao, courtesy name Shiyu, was registered in a military household in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Dashao, posthumously appointed a bureau secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his father was Qiao, a prefect; and his mother was née Hao, invested with the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zongtai, Zongfan, Zongyu, an Imperial University student, Zongyan, Zongzhu, Zongzhen, Zongyi, and Zongyin. He married a woman née Shi. He ranked twenty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Pu, registered in Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yuanye, and he ranked second among his brothers. His age appears to be thirty-four [?; the transcription contains an extra 月], and he was born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Lun was posthumously granted the title of Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather Ding received the same title by honorary grant. His father was Yu; his mother was née Yao, and his stepmother née Yu. His father was living, but his mother had died. His elder brothers were Jie, Qiu, Zhen, 𤣱 [reading uncertain], Xun, Qiong, and Zhang; his younger brothers were Xuan and Ji. He married a woman née Shen. He placed sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Geng Suiqing, registered in Hua County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zicheng, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Biao, his grandfather Run, and his father Teng; his mother was née Guo, and his stepmothers were née Zhu and née He. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Suiguo and Suichao, the latter a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year; his younger brothers were Suixiang, Suixing, Suizuo, Suijian, Suiyong, Suixiao, and Suiti. He married a woman née Liu. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Lu, registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ziyin, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-three years old, born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Ji, and his father Jian; his mother was née Jin, and his stepmother née Wu. His parents and grandparents had all died. His younger brother was Fu. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Shuyang, registered in Gaochun County, Yingtian Prefecture, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Jianfu, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Yi, and his father Lie; his mother was née Yuan, and his stepmother née Wang. His mother was living, but his father had died. His younger brothers were Shuhe, Shuren, and Shuyi. He married a woman née Huang. He placed twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Mian 張冕, courtesy name Zhuangfu, was from Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and belonged to a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Fu was a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather Wang was a tribute student; his father was Yuanying; his mother was née Zeng, and his stepmother née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ang, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Shaode 沈紹德, courtesy name Chunfu, was from Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen; his grandfather Xuan held the honorary title of Official for Public Benefaction; his father was Yuancheng; his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother née Shao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shaodai, and his wife was née Gu. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yanzuo 徐衍祚, courtesy name Zihou, was from Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and belonged to a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Chun was a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Lu; his father was Fuchen, and his mother née Feng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yanshi, his younger brothers were Yanru and Yanshi, and his wife was née Gu. He ranked forty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Dashao 朱大韶, courtesy name Xiangxuan, was from Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and belonged to a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xuan was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, advanced to the prestige titles of Grand Master for Court Discussion (zhongyi dafu) and Director for Assisting Governance (zanzhi yin); his grandfather Xian was a Registrar in the Nanjing Tiance Guard; his father Liangfeng was an Imperial University student, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dazhang and Daying, and his wife was née Lu. He ranked second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Shangzhi, registered in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yida; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the seventeenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bowen, his grandfather Gang, his father Di, and his mother née He. His parents and grandparents were living. His wife was née Yang. He placed fifty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Chengfang, registered in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yingyu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rongguang, his grandfather Zuan, his father An, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chunfang, Tianfang, Ruifang, and Xiangfang. His wife was née Lin. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bu Dayou, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Qianfu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather Zhou held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness. His father Zongluo was a student of the Imperial University and received successive posthumous grants of the titles Grand Master for Forthright Service and Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father’s former wife was née Zhou; his mother, née He, received successive grants of the title Senior Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Datong was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his younger brothers were Daguan and Dashun. His wife was née Huai. He placed forty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Zhong, registered in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zili; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Tai held the honorary title of Longevity Official; his grandfather Ang was a Ceremonial Escort, a consort of an imperial clanswoman; his father Fengyi was a Prefect, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Nan and his younger brother Xi. His wife was née Li. He placed ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

王三接〔貫山西平陽府洪洞縣，匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字晉甫，行二，年四十，八月十七日生〕。曾祖從宣，祖俊〔壽官〕，父相〔知縣〕，前母張氏、陳氏，母孔氏。慈侍下，兄三德、三槐、三聘，弟三省、三益，娶李氏。山西鄉試第四名，會試第二百七十六名。
translation_en:
Zheng Qi, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Ruwen. Second in birth order, he was aged forty-nine and was born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zan, a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Weiren; his father was Tingxuan; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fang, Yi, and Xiu. He married a woman née Song. He ranked fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Shiju, registered in Xianning County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruxian. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ang, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; his grandfather was Bingcong, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Yu, a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Qian. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Shiru, and his younger brothers were Shifan and Shixian. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xianfang, registered in Pu Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was originally from Jianli County, Huguang. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bocheng. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the twenty-third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanzhong; his grandfather was Hai; his father was Jian; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chunfang, Zhongsheng, Tongfang, and Jideng. He married a woman née Sheng and subsequently a woman née Ren. He ranked fourteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Sanjie, registered in Hongtong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jinfu. Second in birth order, he was aged forty and was born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congxuan; his grandfather was Jun, an honorary official recognized for longevity; and his father was Xiang, a County Magistrate. His father's former wives were née Zhang and née Chen, and his mother was née Kong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Sande, Sanhuai, and Sanpin, and his younger brothers were Sanxing and Sanyi. He married a woman née Li. He ranked fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳瓚〔貫直隸河間府獻縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字敬夫，行二，年三十七，十二月二十九日生〕。曾祖英，祖思義，父大川，母劉氏。具慶下，兄瑄，弟現、璜，娶李氏，繼娶郭氏、韓氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十三名，會試第二百三十八名。

楊鑰〔貫雲南鶴慶府劔川州，民籍，州學生，治詩經，字啓之，行四，年三十三，三月二十五日生〕。曾祖春，祖芳，父元，嫡母郭氏，生母楊氏。永感下，兄志永、鎧、鐸，娶郭氏。雲南鄉試第二十八名，會試第二百三十五名。

張芹〔貫山西汾州孝義縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字獻之，行八，年三十一，七月初七日生〕。曾祖九隆〔義官〕，祖翃〔義官〕，父大綱〔州吏目〕，母趙氏。具慶下，兄芝、冕〔按察司副使〕、芟〔貢士〕、蕃、文，弟芳，娶閻氏。山西鄉試第二十三名，會試第九十二名。

喻顯科〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字時晉，行一，年三十七，九月二十二日生〕。曾祖武成，祖公豪〔壽官〕，父忠節，母涂氏。具慶下，兄魁〔省祭官〕、顯民，弟顯職、顯秩、顯程、顯稱，娶熊氏，繼娶龔氏。江西鄉試第五十七名，會試第八十五名。
translation_en:
Chen Zan 陳瓚, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Siyi, his father Dachuan, and his mother née Liu; both parents were living. His elder brother was Xuan, and his younger brothers were Xian and Huang. He married a woman née Li, then successively women née Guo and Han. He placed 123rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yue 楊鑰, courtesy name Qizhi, was registered in Jianchuan Subprefecture, Heqing Prefecture, Yunnan, in a civilian household. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Fang, and his father Yuan; his legal mother was née Guo and his birth mother née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhiyong, Kai, and Duo. He married a woman née Guo. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qin 張芹, courtesy name Xianzhi, was registered in Xiaoyi County, Fenzhou Subprefecture, Shanxi, in a military household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked eighth in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Jiulong and grandfather Hong each held the honorary title of Official of Righteousness; his father Dagang was a subprefectural Clerk, and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi, Mian (Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission), Shan (a tribute scholar), Fan, and Wen; his younger brother was Fang. He married a woman née Yan. He placed twenty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Xianke 喻顯科, courtesy name Shijin, was registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wucheng, his grandfather Gonghao held the honorary title of Longevity Official, his father was Zhongjie, and his mother was née Tu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kui (a provincial sacrificial official [?]) and Xianmin; his younger brothers were Xianzhi, Xianzhi, Xiancheng, and Xiancheng (顯職、顯秩、顯程、顯稱 respectively). He married a woman née Xiong and subsequently a woman née Gong. He placed fifty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yin Bingyang, courtesy name Ziyin, was registered in a civilian household in Ji County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Zhang, served as an Unranked Service Official; and his father was Wentai. His mother was née Li, and his stepmothers were née Dong and née An. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Binghui and Bingxin. He married a woman née Luo. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Tianjue, courtesy name Zixiu, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangyuan County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the seventeenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Cong, served as a prefectural Clerk; his grandfather, Ru, as a Daoist Instructor; and his father, Liangxiang, as a Station Master. His mother was née Hao, and his stepmother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tianxu, Tianzhi, Tianmin, Tianlun, Tianyou, Tianzhang, and Tianqu. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Huai’ai, courtesy name Yuemin, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked twenty-second in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the fifth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Tinghua, his grandfather Tang, and his father Jing. His father's principal wife was née Zhu, and his birth mother was née Xia. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Huaixin, and his younger brothers were Huaide, Huaizhi, Huaizhong, and Huaizuo. He married a woman née Fan and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jing, courtesy name Zizheng, was registered in a military household of the Yunnan Left Guard in Yunnan and was a native of Lulong County in the Metropolitan Region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Wen, his grandfather Ming, and his father Jin; his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Gang. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-first in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Miao Minxue, registered in an artisan household in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yiqin; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather, Ze; his father, Bicheng, a Sacrificial Attendant; and his mother, née Liu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Minzheng and Minde. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhi, registered in a military household of Jiyang Guard and a native of Qidong County, Shandong, was a Shuntian prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziren; he ranked fifth in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Youyu; his grandfather, Quan; his father, Xiu; his mother, née Wei; and his stepmothers, née Jin and née Lü. His father was deceased, and he attended a surviving mother. His elder brothers were Luan, Feng, Qi, and Lin. He married a woman née Cheng and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed seventy-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Guangzu, registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Pinghu County, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yusheng; he ranked tenth in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Chang, a District Magistrate who received successive posthumous promotions to Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His grandfather was Song, Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments in Nanjing, posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His father was Gao, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guangyu, Guangzuo (a tribute scholar), Guangru, Guangbi (a student admitted by virtue of family official status), and Guangzhai. He married a woman née Tao. He placed 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xunmao, registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jishi; he ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Bing; his grandfather, Jian; his father, De; and his mother, née Zhang. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Jiamao, Duanmao, and Yingmao. He married a woman née Shen. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Xi, registered in Jize County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dechun, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was aged twenty-four, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Zhongliang, his father Lei, and his mother née Li; both parents were living. His elder brother was Yi, and his wife was née Dai. He placed 107th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Zhengmao, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yangshi, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenqing, his grandfather Fu, his father Huang, his mother née Wu, and his stepmother née Cheng; his parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zhengfang, Zhenghua, Zhengshi, and Zhengli, and his wife was née Zhuang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Min, registered in Yuci County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dunfu, he ranked first in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenqi, his grandfather Fengliang, his father Qi, and his mother née Zhao; his parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Cong, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fortieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lou Zhen, registered in Yiwu County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zi'an, he ranked seventy-third in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenhua, his grandfather Qiu, his father Quan, his mother née Jin, and his stepmother née Wang; his father alone was living. His elder brothers were Luan, Yue, and Duo, and his wife was née Jin. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Yingjie, registered in a civilian household in Wei County, Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zihe, he ranked first in family birth order, and he was apparently twenty-five years old [?; the transcription reads 二五], born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen, his grandfather Ke, his father Run, and his mother née Han; both parents were living, his wife was née Wang, and he placed fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Zhihe, registered in a civilian household in Pingyuan County, Dezhou Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Shunfu, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was forty years old, born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Jian, his father Guan, and his mother née Zhou; his mother alone was living, his elder brother was Zhizhong, his first wife was née Zhu and his subsequent wife née Ma, and he placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yu, registered in a civilian household in Changyuan County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Xiaozheng, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng, his grandfather Cong (a Professor, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor), his father Sheng, his father's former wife née Zheng, and his mother née Qi; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Kai and his younger brother Shi, his wife was née Yang, and he placed sixtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Shan, registered in a civilian household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Tingpei, he ranked twenty-sixth in family birth order, and he was forty years old, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luxing, his grandfather Can, his father Shi, and his mother née Li; his father alone was living, his first wife was née Li and his subsequent wife née Lu, and he placed seventy-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫裒〔貫貴州清平衛官籍，直隸如皋縣人，國子生，治書經，字益之，行七，年二十六，五月初五日生〕。曾祖鐸，祖瀚〔府同知，進階中議大夫〕，父重〔知縣〕，母宋氏。重慶下，兄衣〔知縣〕、衮〔監生〕、卞、雍、襄、褒〔貢士〕，娶王氏。貴州鄉試第八名，會試第二百八十八名。
