何琚〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字佩甫，行二，年三十五，十一月二十四日生〕。曾祖祜〔州同知〕，祖德仁，父聰，母梁氏。慈侍下，兄琦，娶顧氏。福建鄉試第三十名，會試第二百九十七名。
translation_en:
Li Shi, courtesy name Yixing, was registered in a military household in Jiangjin County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi’ang; his grandfather, Lin; his father, Tingchun, a District Magistrate; and his mother, née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yan, Fang, Jiao, Zhi, and Xu. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Luo. He placed third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Pou, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered in an official household in Qingping Guard, Guizhou, and was originally from Rugao County in Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was seventh in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the fifth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather, Han, an Associate Prefect promoted to the prestige title Grand Master for Deliberation; his father, Zhong, a District Magistrate; and his mother, née Song. His parents and members of the grandparental generation were living. His elder brothers were Yi, a District Magistrate; Gun, an Imperial University student; Bian; Yong; Xiang; and Bao, a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Wang. He placed eighth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Heng, courtesy name Shouzhun, was registered in a civilian household in Shulu County, Qizhou, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Zan, granted the title Investigating Censor; his father, Yun, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Wei, granted the title Lady (ruren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Qu, and his younger brother was Wei. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Ju, courtesy name Peifu, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Hu, a Subprefectural Vice Magistrate; his grandfather, Deren; his father, Cong; and his mother, née Liang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Qi. He married a woman née Gu. He placed thirtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en: Lü Yin 呂廕 was registered in Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in the civilian registration category. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Chengzhi, and he was the eldest among his brothers, aged forty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Siying; his grandfather, Yong; and his father, Yue, a Vice Battalion Commander in the Right Battalion of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. His mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hui, a student of the Imperial University, Geng, and Yong. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently married another woman née Zhang. He ranked fifty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

不得而辭焉者唐

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:

子之傳至孟軻而
止孟子則以堯舜
禹湯文王之為君
===
皐陶伊尹萊朱太
公望散宜生之為
臣各有聞知見知
之殊其詳畧同異
果何義歟其授受

translation_en: …Han Yu maintained that the transmission from Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, King Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius ended with Meng Ke (Mencius). Mencius, however, distinguished among the rulers Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, and King Wen and the ministers Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Lai Zhu, Taigong Wang, and San Yisheng, according to whether they knew through hearing or through seeing. What, indeed, is the significance of the differences and similarities in the detail and brevity of these accounts? As for their handing down and receiving of the Way…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
之微有可指歟宋
儒謂周敦頤程顥
兄弟朱熹四子為
得孔孟不傳之緒
而直接夫自古帝
===
王之統道果若是
班歟其講求著述
之功果可與行道
者並歟抑門人尊
尚師說遞相稱謂

punctuated: 之微，有可指歟？宋儒謂周敦頤、程顥兄弟、朱熹四子為得孔孟不傳之緒，而直接夫自古帝王之統，道果若是班歟？其講求著述之功，果可與行道者並歟？抑門人尊尚師說，遞相稱謂
translation_en: …can the subtleties of this transmission be identified? Song Confucians held that the four masters—Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao and his brother, and Zhu Xi—had recovered the thread of teaching from Confucius and Mencius whose transmission had been broken, and had directly continued the succession of the emperors and kings of antiquity. Is the Way indeed ordered thus [?]? Can their achievements in inquiry and writing truly rank alongside those of men who put the Way into practice? Or did their disciples exalt their teachers’ doctrines and pass on these claims from one generation to the next…

text:

宋而下雖不能比
隆唐虞三代之盛
其間英君誼辟撫

From the Han, Tang, and Song onward, although these dynasties could not rival the flourishing rule of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties, among their rulers were outstanding and righteous sovereigns who governed the world and ordered all things, whose virtue and beneficence extended throughout the Four Seas, and whose achievements shone between Heaven and Earth. They cannot all be dismissed as insignificant. Could it truly be that none was worthy to carry on the transmission of the Way among great sovereigns? Reverently considering Our …

text:
太祖高皇帝體堯舜
授受之要而允執
厥中論人心虛靈
之機而操存弗二
我
===
成祖文皇帝言帝王
之治一本於道又
言六經之道明則
天地聖人之心可
見至治之功可成

translation_en: …Emperor Taizu Gao embodied the essential principle transmitted from Yao to Shun and faithfully held fast to the Mean; he discussed the subtle workings of the human mind in its emptiness and spiritual awareness, and preserved it with undivided constancy. Our Emperor Chengzu Wen said: “The government of emperors and kings is rooted entirely in the Way.” He also said: “When the Way of the Six Classics is made clear, the heart of Heaven, Earth, and the sages can be discerned, and the achievement of perfect government can be realized.”

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
斯言也真有以上
繼皇王道統之正
下開萬世太平之
基迨我
列聖克篤前業所以
===
開天常叙人紀者
歷百八十餘年于
兹朕纘紹
祖宗鴻緒登踐寶阼
惟敬惟一叙彞倫

translation_en: These words truly serve to carry forward the orthodox succession of the Way transmitted by the emperors and kings of old, and to lay the foundations of supreme peace for ten thousand generations to come. Our successive sage emperors have steadfastly advanced the achievements of their predecessors, manifesting Heaven’s enduring norms and ordering human relationships for more than one hundred and eighty years down to the present. I have continued the grand legacy of my ancestors and ascended the imperial throne, maintaining reverence and singleness of purpose, setting the constant human relationships in order…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
惇典禮祈
天命拯民窮思弘化
理以成叅贊繼立
之功者宵旰孳孳
不遑寧處茲欲遠
===
紹二帝三王大道
之統近法我
祖宗
列聖心學之傳舎是
又何所致力而可
alt_text:
惇典禮所
天命撫民窮思弘化
理以成參贊繼立
之功者宵旰孳孳
不違寧處玆欲遠
===
紹二帝三王大道
之統近法我
祖宗
列聖心學之傳舍是
又何所致力而可
punctuated: 惇典禮，祈天命，拯民窮，思弘化理，以成叅贊繼立之功者，宵旰孳孳，不遑寧處。茲欲遠紹二帝三王大道之統，近法我祖宗列聖心學之傳，舎是，又何所致力而可？
translation_en: …to uphold the canonical rites, pray for Heaven’s mandate, and rescue the people from distress. Intent on extending moral transformation and good governance, and thereby accomplishing the work of assisting [Heaven and Earth] and carrying forward and establishing [their work][?], I labor diligently from before dawn until late in the day, with no leisure to rest. Now I wish, looking to distant antiquity, to continue the succession of the Great Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and, looking to the more recent past, to emulate the learning of the mind transmitted by our ancestral founders and successive sage emperors. Apart from this, toward what else could I properly direct my efforts?

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
夫自堯舜禹文之
後孔孟以来上下
千數百年間道統
之傳歸諸臣下又
盡出于宋儒一時
===
之論此朕所深疑
也子大夫學先王
之道審於名實之
歸宜悉心以對毋
隱毋泛朕將注覽

translation_en: Now, after Yao, Shun, Yu, and King Wen, from Confucius and Mencius onward, over a span of more than a thousand years, the transmission of the succession to the Way devolved upon subjects. Yet this account derives entirely from the discussions of Confucian scholars of the Song dynasty at that particular time. This is something about which I have profound doubts. You gentlemen have studied the Way of the former kings and carefully examined how names accord with realities. You should devote your whole minds to your replies, concealing nothing and avoiding vague generalities. I shall read them attentively…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
臣李春芳
臣對臣聞帝王之治本於道道立而後化以
之弘帝王之道本於心心純而後道以之會
心也者統夫道者也心有弗純則存諸中者
無貞純精一之懿其於道也為小成道也者
弘夫治者也道有弗粹則發諸外者無正大
光明之業其於治也為小康小成不足以語
天德小康不足以語王道斯豈帝王之所以
繼天立極者哉故必本之心也渾乎天理而
有以裕内聖之基而後敷之治也若乎天道
===
而有以熈外王之業天德王道其極一也然
其本則係之學焉而已矣學以純心心以會
道道以出治治以格天其在當時也則帝王
之治法以立其在萬世也則帝王之心法以
傳斯其道統之所由肇乎循之而治唐虞三
代是也得其似而理漢唐宋是也至於有宋
諸儒則亦講明斯學以翼乎聖道而已矣烏
可以與帝王並歟洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
成祖文皇帝體天弘道因心出治以上繼皇王道

諸儒則亦講明斯學以翼乎聖道而已矣烏
可以與帝王並歟洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
成祖文皇帝體天弘道因心出治以上繼皇王道
punctuated:
臣李春芳。
臣對：臣聞帝王之治本於道，道立而後化以之弘；帝王之道本於心，心純而後道以之會。心也者，統夫道者也。心有弗純，則存諸中者無貞純精一之懿，其於道也為小成。道也者，弘夫治者也。道有弗粹，則發諸外者無正大光明之業，其於治也為小康。小成不足以語天德，小康不足以語王道，斯豈帝王之所以繼天立極者哉？故必本之心也，渾乎天理，而有以裕内聖之基；而後敷之治也，若乎天道，而有以熈外王之業。天德王道，其極一也。然其本則係之學焉而已矣。學以純心，心以會道，道以出治，治以格天。其在當時也，則帝王之治法以立；其在萬世也，則帝王之心法以傳。斯其道統之所由肇乎？循之而治，唐虞三代是也；得其似而理，漢唐宋是也。至於有宋諸儒，則亦講明斯學，以翼乎聖道而已矣，烏可以與帝王並歟？洪惟我太祖高皇帝、成祖文皇帝，體天弘道，因心出治，以上繼皇王道
translation_en:
Your servant, Li Chunfang.
Your servant replies: I have heard that the government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way. Only when the Way is established can its transforming influence spread. The Way of emperors and kings is rooted in the mind. Only when the mind is pure can the Way be comprehended in its entirety. The mind is what unifies the Way. If the mind lacks purity, what is preserved within will lack the excellence of steadfast purity, refinement, and singleness; its attainment of the Way will be only partial. The Way is what extends good government. If the Way lacks purity, what manifests outwardly will lack the achievements of uprightness, greatness, radiance, and clarity; government will attain only modest peace. Partial attainment is insufficient to speak of Heaven’s virtue, and modest peace is insufficient to speak of the Kingly Way. Could these be the means by which emperors and kings carry on Heaven’s work and establish the supreme standard? Thus one must first ground oneself in the mind, wholly united with Heaven’s principle, thereby enriching the foundation of inward sagehood. Only then can one extend this into government, conforming to Heaven’s Way and thereby bringing lustre to the work of outward kingship. Heaven’s virtue and the Kingly Way are one in their ultimate realization. Yet their root lies solely in learning. Learning purifies the mind; the mind comprehends the Way; the Way brings forth government; and government reaches Heaven. In their own time, the methods of government of emperors and kings are thereby established; for the myriad generations to come, their teaching of the mind is thereby transmitted. Is this not the origin of the succession of the Way? Those who followed it and achieved good government were the rulers of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Those who attained a semblance of it and brought order were the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song. As for the Confucian scholars of the Song, they merely expounded and clarified this learning to support the Way of the sages. How could they be placed alongside emperors and kings? Reverently considering our Taizu, the Gao Emperor, and Chengzu, the Wen Emperor: they embodied Heaven and extended the Way, bringing forth government from their minds, thereby carrying forward from antiquity the Way of the august sovereigns and kings …

陛下則又
神聖縱于天光明緝乎學而治之所溥四達不
悖薰蒸透徹融液周遍二帝三王道統之傳
遠紹而無間

于
萬幾之暇進臣等于
廷俯賜
===

以仰裨

聖化蓋亦有年其于我

矣敢不敬陳以對揚

矣敢不敬陳以對揚
休命乎臣嘗聞之天地未判道在天地天地既判
道在聖人是聖人者道之宗也又嘗聞諸書
punctuated:
統之正，下開萬世太平之基。而我陛下則又神聖縱于天，光明緝乎學，而治之所溥，四達不悖，薰蒸透徹，融液周遍。二帝三王道統之傳，遠紹而無間；二祖列聖心學之邃，近述而彌光。粹乎無以尚矣！乃猶于萬幾之暇，進臣等于廷，俯賜清問，且曰：「宵旰孳孳，不遑寧處。」臣有以仰窺陛下望道未見之心矣。
臣草茅疵賤，何所知識，可以仰裨聖學之萬一？雖然，涵濡聖化，蓋亦有年。其于我祖宗治道之盛，及我陛下心學之精，亦嘗佩服涵泳，有以少窺其涯涘矣。敢不敬陳，以對揚休命乎？
臣嘗聞之：天地未判，道在天地；天地既判，道在聖人。是聖人者，道之宗也。又嘗聞諸《書》
translation_en:
…the orthodox succession of the Way, and laid the foundation for great peace for ten thousand generations to come. Your Majesty, moreover, possesses divine sagacity bestowed by Heaven and a luminous understanding cultivated through learning. Your government’s beneficence reaches in all four directions without deviation; its transforming influence penetrates everywhere, suffusing and permeating all. You continue without interruption the distant transmission of the Way from the Two Emperors and Three Kings; you carry forward and further illuminate the profound learning of the mind of the two imperial founders and the successive sage emperors. Such purity admits of nothing higher! Yet even in the intervals between your myriad affairs, you summoned us, your servants, to court and graciously bestowed your august questions upon us. You further declared: “From before dawn until late at night, I labor diligently, with no leisure to rest.” Through this, your servant can glimpse Your Majesty’s resolve to seek the Way as though you had yet to behold it.
Your servant is an obscure man of humble station and many faults. What knowledge or understanding could I possess that might contribute even the smallest part to your sagely learning? Nevertheless, I have been steeped in your sagely transforming influence for years. I have reverently taken to heart and pondered both the flourishing arts of government of our imperial ancestors and the refinement of Your Majesty’s learning of the mind, and have thus gained some slight glimpse of their scope. How could I dare fail to set forth my thoughts respectfully, in response to and celebration of your gracious command?
Your servant has heard it said: before Heaven and Earth separated, the Way resided in Heaven and Earth; once Heaven and Earth had separated, the Way resided in the sages. Thus the sages are the fountainhead of the Way. I have also heard in the Book of Documents…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
曰惟天地萬物父母惟人萬物之靈亶聰明
作元后元后作民父母是元后者人之主也
然則道在天下安得不屬之聖人又安得不
屬之大君也哉是故三代而上位稱其德達
而在上者莫匪聖神而道統之傳有自來矣
請因
聖問而條陳之唐虞以往書契未立逖哉無以稽
矣故韓愈孟軻之所稱率自堯舜而始愈謂
堯以是傳之舜舜以是傳之禹禹以是傳之
湯湯以是傳之文武周公孔子是立功立言
===
雖異以言乎道統則均也軻謂由堯舜至於
湯五百有餘歲若禹皐陶則見而知之若湯
則聞而知之由湯至於文王五百有餘歲若
伊尹萊朱則見而知之若文王則聞而知之
由文王至於孔子五百有餘歲若太公望散
宜生則見而知之若孔子則聞而知之是見
知聞知雖殊以言乎道統則一也然觀孔子
有志三代之英而自傷其未逮伊尹樂堯舜
之道於畝畝而必以吾身親見為幸則託之
空言者豈若見之行事哉此二帝三王之道

之道於畎畝而必以吾身親見爲幸則託之
空言者豈若見之行事哉此二帝三王之道
punctuated:
曰：「惟天地萬物父母，惟人萬物之靈。亶聰明，作元后；元后作民父母。」是元后者，人之主也。然則道在天下，安得不屬之聖人，又安得不屬之大君也哉？是故三代而上，位稱其德，達而在上者莫匪聖神，而道統之傳有自來矣。
請因聖問而條陳之。唐虞以往，書契未立，逖哉，無以稽矣。故韓愈、孟軻之所稱，率自堯舜而始。愈謂：「堯以是傳之舜，舜以是傳之禹，禹以是傳之湯，湯以是傳之文武周公孔子。」是立功立言雖異，以言乎道統則均也。軻謂：「由堯舜至於湯，五百有餘歲。若禹、皐陶，則見而知之；若湯，則聞而知之。由湯至於文王，五百有餘歲。若伊尹、萊朱，則見而知之；若文王，則聞而知之。由文王至於孔子，五百有餘歲。若太公望、散宜生，則見而知之；若孔子，則聞而知之。」是見知聞知雖殊，以言乎道統則一也。然觀孔子有志三代之英，而自傷其未逮；伊尹樂堯舜之道於畝畝，而必以吾身親見為幸，則託之空言者，豈若見之行事哉？此二帝三王之道
translation_en:
…reads: “Heaven and Earth are the parents of all things; humankind is the most spiritually endowed of all things. One truly possessed of keen discernment becomes the sovereign; the sovereign becomes the parent of the people.” Thus the sovereign is the ruler of humankind. Since the Way exists throughout the world, how could its charge fail to fall to the sage, and how could it fail to fall to the great ruler? Hence, in the Three Dynasties and earlier, rank matched virtue: those who attained high position were invariably sagely and divinely wise. The transmission of the orthodox succession of the Way therefore has a long history.
Allow me to set this forth point by point in response to Your Majesty’s sagely question. Before the age of Tang and Yu, written records had not yet been established. Those times are so remote that there is no means of examining them. Thus the accounts of Han Yu and Meng Ke generally begin with Yao and Shun. Han Yu said: “Yao transmitted this to Shun; Shun transmitted it to Yu; Yu transmitted it to Tang; Tang transmitted it to Kings Wen and Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius.” Thus, although establishing meritorious achievements differs from establishing enduring teachings, they are equivalent in terms of the orthodox succession of the Way. Meng Ke said: “From Yao and Shun to Tang was more than five hundred years. Those such as Yu and Gao Yao knew their Way through seeing them; Tang knew it through hearing of them. From Tang to King Wen was more than five hundred years. Those such as Yi Yin and Lai Zhu knew his Way through seeing him; King Wen knew it through hearing of him. From King Wen to Confucius was more than five hundred years. Those such as Taigong Wang and San Yisheng knew his Way through seeing him; Confucius knew it through hearing of him.” Thus, although knowing through seeing differs from knowing through hearing, they are one in terms of the orthodox succession of the Way. Yet consider how Confucius aspired to the excellence of the Three Dynasties and lamented that he had not lived to witness it; and how Yi Yin delighted in the Way of Yao and Shun while working in the fields [?], yet regarded personally witnessing its realization as his good fortune. How, then, could entrusting it to mere words compare with manifesting it in deeds? This Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
所以為獨盛而道統之傳非帝王莫之能當
也何也夫所謂道者非徒以其蘊之心也以
其本之心而宣之化也是故以之經天則陰
陽宣節天道其清乎以之緯地則山川靜翕
地道其寧乎以之總民物之紀則百姓太和
萬類咸若民物其熙乎道猷章而道妙流焉
實政乂而實心昭焉體用一源者也微帝王
其孰能與于此哉然求其要則心焉盡之矣
究其功則學焉盡之矣何也非道無以弘天
下之治非心無以會天下之道而學也者所
===
以純心以體道凝道以出治者也大哉學乎
斯固帝王之所不可忽者乎是故格于上下
堯之道盛矣然求其所以為學者則曰欽明
允恭其所以事其心者何如其至也重華協
帝舜之道盛矣然求其所以為學者則曰濬
哲溫恭其所以事其心者何如其至也三代
有道之長禹湯文武之道亦云盛矣然求其
所以為學者則曰勤儉曰執中曰緝熙執兢
其所以事其心者何如其至也則夫治之所
成黎民於變也四方風動也文命誕敷也萬

所以為獨盛，而道統之傳非帝王莫之能當也。何也？夫所謂道者，非徒以其蘊之心也，以其本之心而宣之化也。是故以之經天，則陰陽宣節，天道其清乎；以之緯地，則山川靜翕，地道其寧乎；以之總民物之紀，則百姓太和，萬類咸若，民物其熙乎。道猷章而道妙流焉，實政乂而實心昭焉，體用一源者也。微帝王，其孰能與于此哉？然求其要，則心焉盡之矣；究其功，則學焉盡之矣。何也？非道無以弘天下之治，非心無以會天下之道，而學也者，所以純心以體道、凝道以出治者也。大哉學乎！斯固帝王之所不可忽者乎！

translation_en:
…is why it flourished uniquely, and why none but emperors and kings could shoulder the transmission of the succession of the Way. Why is this? What is called the Way is not merely something stored within the heart; it is rooted in the heart and made manifest in transforming influence. Thus, when employed to order Heaven, yin and yang unfold in their proper rhythms: how clear Heaven’s course becomes! When employed to regulate Earth, mountains and rivers rest in harmony: how tranquil Earth’s course becomes! When employed to unite the guiding principles governing people and things, the hundred surnames enjoy supreme harmony and all kinds of beings follow their proper course: how flourishing people and things become! The guiding principles of the Way become manifest, and its subtle workings flow forth; genuine governance brings order, and the sincere heart shines forth. Substance and function have a single source. Without emperors and kings, who could participate in this? Yet if we seek its essential point, it is wholly encompassed in the heart; if we investigate the effort required, it is wholly encompassed in learning. Why? Without the Way, there is no means to extend good government throughout the realm; without the heart, there is no means to comprehend the Way throughout the realm. Learning is the means by which one purifies the heart to embody the Way, and firmly establishes the Way to bring forth good government. How great is learning! Surely it is something emperors and kings must never neglect!
Thus, reaching above and below, Yao’s Way flourished. Yet when we seek what constituted his learning, we find the words “reverent, discerning, truly respectful.” How consummate was his care for his heart! With his redoubled brilliance matching that of the emperor, Shun’s Way flourished. Yet when we seek what constituted his learning, we find the words “profoundly wise, gentle, and respectful.” How consummate was his care for his heart! As for the enduring rule of the Three Dynasties that possessed the Way, the Way of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu may likewise be said to have flourished. Yet when we seek what constituted their learning, we find “diligence and frugality,” “holding fast to the Mean,” and “continuing in brightness and maintaining vigilance.” How consummate was their care for their hearts! As for the achievements of their government: the common people were transformed; the four quarters stirred as if moved by the wind; civilizing instruction spread far and wide; the myriad…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
邦惟懷也燕及皇天會朝清明也唐虞三代
之化巍乎其不可及者謂不本於此哉德至
此而後謂之天德道至此而後謂之王道若
夫皐陶伊尹諸臣贊翊之功固不可泯而其
宅中圖大以恢弘化理建中建極以丕昭道
猷者則豈諸臣所得而專之哉故易曰地道
也妻道也臣道也地道無成而代有終也此
之謂也三代而降享國長久者莫如漢唐宋
其間英君誼辟撫世宰物德澤加于四海功
烈著諸天地者亦不可少誠有如
===
聖制所云者是故漢之除秦苛也深得弔民之理
以至七制嗣興風俗淳美矣唐之靖隋亂也
迅收底定之功以至三宗迭出海宇乂安矣
宋振五季之衰也愛養民力出生靈于塗炭
之苦而好文守成之主又繩繩相繼焉不可
謂其盡畔于道也向使盡畔于道則不足以
總一四海整齊萬民矣又安能歷數百年而
巍然民上以握神器乎後之尚論猶不能無
憾焉者以其學之未純焉耳學苟未純則蘊
之心者不足以語帝王精一之傳敷之治者

宅中圖大以恢弘化理建中建極以丕昭道
猷者則豈諸臣所得而專之哉故易曰地道
也妻道也臣道也地道無成而代有終也此
之謂也三代而降享國長久者莫如漢唐宋
其間英君誼辟撫世宰物德澤加于四海功
烈著諸天地者亦不可少誠有如
===
聖制所云者是故漢之除秦苛也深得帚民之理
以至七制嗣興風俗淳美矣唐之靖隋亂也
汛掃底定之功以至三宗迭出海宇乂安矣
宋振五季之衰也愛養民力出生靈于塗炭
之苦而好文守成之主又繩繩相繼焉不可
謂其盡畔于道也向使盡畔于道則不足以
總一四海整齊萬民矣又安能歷數百年而
巍然民上以握神器乎後之尚論猶不能無
憾焉者以其學之未純焉耳學苟弗純則藴
之心者不足以語帝王精一之傳敷之治者

邦惟懷也，燕及皇天、會朝清明也。唐虞三代之化，巍乎其不可及者，謂不本於此哉？德至此而後謂之天德，道至此而後謂之王道。若夫皐陶、伊尹諸臣贊翊之功，固不可泯；而其宅中圖大，以恢弘化理，建中建極，以丕昭道猷者，則豈諸臣所得而專之哉？故《易》曰：「地道也，妻道也，臣道也。地道無成，而代有終也。」此之謂也。

三代而降，享國長久者莫如漢、唐、宋。其間英君誼辟，撫世宰物，德澤加于四海，功烈著諸天地者，亦不可少，誠有如聖制所云者。是故漢之除秦苛也，深得弔民之理，以至七制嗣興，風俗淳美矣。唐之靖隋亂也，迅收底定之功，以至三宗迭出，海宇乂安矣。宋振五季之衰也，愛養民力，出生靈于塗炭之苦，而好文守成之主，又繩繩相繼焉。不可謂其盡畔于道也。向使盡畔于道，則不足以總一四海、整齊萬民矣，又安能歷數百年而巍然民上，以握神器乎？後之尚論猶不能無憾焉者，以其學之未純焉耳。學苟未純，則蘊之心者不足以語帝王精一之傳，敷之治者
translation_en:
…states cherished allegiance; peace extended even to August Heaven, and the morning assembly was clear and bright. Could anyone say that the transforming influence of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, so lofty as to be beyond attainment, was not rooted in this? Only when virtue reaches this point may it be called Heavenly Virtue; only when the Way reaches this point may it be called the Kingly Way. The contributions of ministers such as Gao Yao and Yi Yin in assisting their rulers certainly cannot be effaced. Yet dwelling in the center and planning for greatness so as to extend moral transformation and good government, establishing the mean and the supreme standard so as to manifest the principles of the Way—how could these be matters over which the ministers alone had authority? Thus the Book of Changes says: “It is the way of earth, the way of a wife, and the way of a minister. The way of earth claims no achievement of its own, but brings things to completion on another’s behalf.” This is what it means.

After the Three Dynasties, none enjoyed dynastic rule as enduring as the Han, Tang, and Song. Among their rulers were no few outstanding sovereigns and righteous monarchs who governed the world and directed its affairs, whose beneficence reached all within the Four Seas, and whose achievements shone between Heaven and Earth. It was indeed as Your Majesty’s decree states. Thus, when the Han abolished the harshness of Qin, it profoundly fulfilled the principle of bringing solace to the people. Seven successive reigns followed, and customs became honest and good. When the Tang pacified the disorders of Sui, it swiftly achieved the restoration of settled rule. Three emperors bearing the temple designation zong arose in succession, and the realm enjoyed order and peace. When the Song reversed the decline of the Five Dynasties, it cherished and nurtured the people’s strength and delivered the populace from desperate suffering; rulers who prized cultural learning and preserved their inherited achievements then followed in an unbroken succession. One cannot say that they wholly departed from the Way. Had they wholly departed from it, they could not have united all within the Four Seas and brought order to the myriad people. How, then, could they have remained loftily above the people for several hundred years, holding the sacred vessel of sovereign authority? That later generations, in judging them, still cannot be without regret is solely because their learning was not yet pure. If learning is not pure, what is nurtured in the heart cannot measure up to the emperors’ and kings’ transmission of refinement and singleness of mind; what is expressed in government…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
不足以語雍熙太和之盛斯豈天德王道之
極哉夫惟道化衰于上而後講學倡于下此
宋之四子所由興也以周敦頤言之學以主
靜為宗以一為要而究其極于明通公溥不
由師傳黙契道體者也以程顥兄弟言之涵
養則曰用敬進學則曰致知而又欲以大公
順應學天地之常寬和嚴毅殊途同歸者也
以朱熹言之以講學為入門以踐履為實地
博極羣書而會通於心集諸儒之大成者也
此四子之學之大較也是其學固亦遠宗乎
===
周孔而授之以政則亦伊傅之儔耳夫即為
伊傅也猶不可與帝王並況無伊傅之業乎
何也道在天下惟帝王為能行故道統在天
下惟帝王為能傳而臣之賢者能者則効用
仰成于下者也輙欲接續帝王道統之傳不
亦僭乎故四子者謂之有功於斯道可也以
之直接帝王之道統不可也何也不觀之天
乎方萬物之生也日以晅之雨以潤之風以
鼓之雷以動之夫天穆然深爾確然靜爾然
頌生物之功者必舉而歸之于天而日雨風

不足以語雍熙太和之盛，斯豈天德王道之極哉？夫惟道化衰于上，而後講學倡于下，此宋之四子所由興也。以周敦頤言之，學以主靜為宗，以一為要，而究其極于明通公溥，不由師傳，黙契道體者也。以程顥兄弟言之，涵養則曰用敬，進學則曰致知，而又欲以大公順應，學天地之常，寬和嚴毅，殊途同歸者也。以朱熹言之，以講學為入門，以踐履為實地，博極羣書而會通於心，集諸儒之大成者也。此四子之學之大較也。是其學固亦遠宗乎周孔，而授之以政，則亦伊傅之儔耳。

夫即為伊傅也，猶不可與帝王並，況無伊傅之業乎？何也？道在天下，惟帝王為能行，故道統在天下，惟帝王為能傳，而臣之賢者能者，則効用仰成于下者也。輙欲接續帝王道統之傳，不亦僭乎？故四子者，謂之有功於斯道可也，以之直接帝王之道統不可也。何也？不觀之天乎？方萬物之生也，日以晅之，雨以潤之，風以鼓之，雷以動之。夫天穆然深爾，確然靜爾，然頌生物之功者，必舉而歸之于天，而日雨風
translation_en:
…is insufficient to speak of the flourishing of concord, prosperity, and supreme harmony. How could this be the pinnacle of Heaven’s virtue and the kingly Way? Only when transformation through the Way declined among those above did the exposition of learning arise among those below. This was why the four masters of the Song emerged. In Zhou Dunyi’s case, his learning took making stillness central as its guiding principle and unity as its essential point, reaching its culmination in illumination, thorough understanding, impartiality, and all-embracing breadth. Without receiving a teacher’s transmission, he tacitly apprehended the substance of the Way. In the case of Cheng Hao and his brother, they spoke of employing reverent attentiveness for self-cultivation and extending knowledge for advancing in learning. They further sought, through complete impartiality and responsiveness to things, to emulate the constancy of Heaven and Earth. One was generous and harmonious, the other stern and resolute; by different paths they reached the same destination. In Zhu Xi’s case, he took the exposition of learning as the gateway and practical conduct as the firm ground. He ranged extensively through the books and comprehended their interconnections in his mind, bringing the learning of the various Confucian scholars to its fullest synthesis. Such is the broad outline of these four masters’ learning. Their learning indeed looked back to Zhou Gong and Kongzi as its models; had they been entrusted with government, they would merely have been peers of Yi Yin and Fu Yue.

Even Yi Yin and Fu Yue could not be placed on a level with emperors and kings; how much less those who lacked their achievements! Why is this? Of all under Heaven, only emperors and kings can put the Way into practice. Thus, of all under Heaven, only emperors and kings can transmit the succession of the Way. Worthy and capable ministers render service below and look upward for its fulfillment. Would it not be presumptuous for them forthwith to seek to continue the emperors’ and kings’ transmission of the Way? Thus, it is permissible to say that the four masters rendered meritorious service to this Way, but impermissible to regard them as directly inheriting the emperors’ and kings’ succession of the Way. Why? Have you not observed Heaven? When the myriad things come into being, the sun warms them, the rain moistens them, the wind stirs them, and thunder rouses them. Heaven itself is solemn and profound, steadfast and still. Yet those who praise the achievement of bringing things to life invariably attribute it entirely to Heaven, while the sun, rain, and wind…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
雷不得而有其功何也太和之充盎天實司
之而日雨風雷效其動而已矣可與天道並
乎知日雨風雷不可與天道並則知臣不可
與君道並矣知臣不可與君道並則知四子
者不可與帝王並矣而後之推尊者若黄幹
則叙堯舜禹湯文武周公孔孟而直以周子
繼孔孟不傳之緒二程得統于周子先師朱
子得統于二程而撮其要旨于居敬窮理致
知克己四者而謂千聖萬賢所以傳道而教
人者不越于此至于真德秀則曰孔孟之道
===
至周子而復明周子之道至二程而益明二
程之道至朱子而大明吳澄則曰周子始有
以接孟子之傳于千載之下二程則師于周
子而傳其學後又有朱子集周程之大成是
皆得夫道統之傳者也夫德秀以為道至周
程朱子而大明則誠有之若黄幹吳澄遂以
四子為直接皇王道統之傳于千載之下逓
相稱述其論蔓衍波流直至于今學者尊之
而莫敢違信之而莫或疑抑孰知其失之過
乎故四子講明著述之功不可謂其無裨于

雷不得而有其功，何也？太和之充盎，天實司之，而日雨風雷效其動而已矣，可與天道並乎？知日雨風雷不可與天道並，則知臣不可與君道並矣；知臣不可與君道並，則知四子者不可與帝王並矣。
而後之推尊者，若黄幹，則叙堯舜禹湯文武周公孔孟，而直以周子繼孔孟不傳之緒，二程得統于周子，先師朱子得統于二程，而撮其要旨于居敬、窮理、致知、克己四者，而謂千聖萬賢所以傳道而教人者不越于此。至于真德秀，則曰：「孔孟之道，至周子而復明；周子之道，至二程而益明；二程之道，至朱子而大明。」吳澄則曰：「周子始有以接孟子之傳于千載之下，二程則師于周子而傳其學，後又有朱子集周程之大成，是皆得夫道統之傳者也。」
夫德秀以為道至周程朱子而大明，則誠有之。若黄幹、吳澄遂以四子為直接皇王道統之傳于千載之下，逓相稱述，其論蔓衍波流，直至于今，學者尊之而莫敢違，信之而莫或疑，抑孰知其失之過乎？故四子講明著述之功，不可謂其無裨于
translation_en:
…thunder cannot claim the credit. Why is this? Heaven truly governs the fullness of Supreme Harmony; sun, rain, wind, and thunder merely carry out its activity. Can they stand alongside the Way of Heaven? Once we understand that sun, rain, wind, and thunder cannot stand alongside the Way of Heaven, we understand that a minister cannot stand alongside his ruler in the Way. Once we understand that a minister cannot stand alongside his ruler in the Way, we understand that the Four Masters cannot stand alongside emperors and kings.
Among those who subsequently exalted them, Huang Gan recounted the succession of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius, and directly made Master Zhou the successor to the lineage left without transmission after Confucius and Mencius. The two Cheng masters received this succession from Master Zhou, and his late teacher, Master Zhu, received it from the two Cheng masters. He distilled its essentials into four practices: abiding in reverence, investigating principle, extending knowledge, and overcoming the self. He maintained that the means by which all sages and worthies transmitted the Way and taught others did not extend beyond these. As for Zhen Dexiu, he said: “The Way of Confucius and Mencius became clear again with Master Zhou; the Way of Master Zhou became clearer still with the two Cheng masters; and the Way of the two Cheng masters became fully clear with Master Zhu.” Wu Cheng said: “Only with Master Zhou was there someone able to take up the transmission from Mencius a thousand years later. The two Cheng masters took Master Zhou as their teacher and transmitted his learning. Later, Master Zhu brought the teachings of Zhou and Cheng to their culmination. All these received the transmission of the succession of the Way.”
Now, Dexiu’s view that the Way became fully clear through Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhu is indeed well founded. But Huang Gan and Wu Cheng went so far as to regard the Four Masters as directly taking up the transmission of the emperors’ and kings’ succession of the Way a thousand years later. These claims were repeated and praised in turn; their argument spread and flowed onward down to the present. Scholars revere it and none dares dissent; they believe it and none doubts it. Yet who recognizes that its error lies in going too far? Thus, the Four Masters’ achievements in elucidation and writing cannot be said to have brought no benefit to…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
道而直以為逺續道統之傳與帝王並論焉
是誠門人推尊之過恐亦非四子之心也是
故由唐虞而三代由三代而漢唐宋其帝王
道統之傳端不可誣若秦之于漢六朝之于
唐五代之于宋則皆帝王之驅除烏足以與
斯道哉至于胡元則又我
國朝之驅除若漢之秦唐之六朝宋之五代也
道統之在天下不其淪胥以沒乎幸而
皇天厭亂我
太祖高皇帝挺生淮甸廓清海宇我
===

有以逺追唐虞三代之盛而超軼漢唐宋之
上矣然其所以致治者則莫非本於道其所
以體道者則莫非本於心其所以存心以體

translation_en:
…the Way; yet to claim outright that they continued the transmission of the succession to the Way across the intervening ages, and to rank them alongside emperors and kings, is indeed excessive exaltation by their disciples. I fear it was not the intention of the four masters themselves. Thus, from Tang and Yu to the Three Dynasties, and from the Three Dynasties to the Han, Tang, and Song, the transmission of the succession to the Way among emperors and kings is certainly undeniable. As for the Qin in relation to the Han, the Six Dynasties in relation to the Tang, and the Five Dynasties in relation to the Song, they merely cleared the ground for the emperors and kings who followed. How could they qualify to participate in this Way? As for the barbarian Yuan, it likewise cleared the ground for our dynasty, just as the Qin did for the Han, the Six Dynasties for the Tang, and the Five Dynasties for the Song. Had not the succession to the Way in the world sunk into general oblivion? Fortunately, August Heaven grew weary of disorder. Our Emperor Taizu Gao arose in the Huai region and swept clean all within the seas. Our Emperor Chengzu Wen was born thereafter, richly endowed, and grandly continued that magnificent legacy. The flourishing of their government and transforming influence truly matched the distant splendor of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, and surpassed the Han, Tang, and Song. Yet everything by which they achieved good government was rooted in the Way; everything by which they embodied the Way was rooted in the mind. And in preserving the mind to embody the Way, and embodying the Way to bring forth good government, what did not have learning as its foundation?
As Your Majesty’s composition states: “Emperor Taizu Gao embodied the essentials of the transmission from Yao to Shun and sincerely held fast to the Mean. He discussed the workings of the human mind in its receptive clarity and spiritual responsiveness, and held fast to and preserved it without wavering. Our Emperor Chengzu Wen said that the government of emperors and kings is rooted entirely in the Way. He also said that when the Way of the Six Classics is made clear, the mind of Heaven and Earth can be perceived, and the achievements of perfect government can be realized. Emperors and kings …

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
相傳之要端在是也然臣嘗求我
二祖聖學之精則存心一錄與夫聖學心法尤其
至要者歟存心錄凡歷代帝王祭祀有感于
災祥者備載以垂訓而于敬天之怒無敢戲
豫者尤致意焉聖學心法凡有關於君臣父
子之道者詳述以迪後而于敬天法祖用人
理財者尤申重焉則我
二祖之所以為學者具見于二書而精純貞一心
即二帝三王之心太和咸熙治即二帝三王
之治天德王道巍然煥然又奚惑哉此
===
列聖之所以克篤前業開天常敘人紀歷百八十
餘年而
皇圖鞏固者信皆有得於是也恭惟
陛下以聰明聖智之資懋精一執中之學心之所
裕者與天地合其德治之所成者與皇王匹
其休肆今大化流行百姓太和德浹于中夏
威行于蠻貊至治馨香達于上下而休徵畢
集千古所未有也臣何幸躬逢其盛哉臣嘗
竊窺
陛下之所以臻此者信本於學而學之精實典要

punctuated:
相傳之要端在是也。然臣嘗求我二祖聖學之精，則《存心》一錄與夫《聖學心法》，尤其至要者歟！《存心錄》凡歷代帝王祭祀有感于災祥者，備載以垂訓，而于敬天之怒、無敢戲豫者，尤致意焉。《聖學心法》凡有關於君臣父子之道者，詳述以迪後，而于敬天法祖、用人理財者，尤申重焉。則我二祖之所以為學者，具見于二書，而精純貞一，心即二帝三王之心；太和咸熙，治即二帝三王之治。天德王道，巍然煥然，又奚惑哉！此列聖之所以克篤前業、開天常、敘人紀，歷百八十餘年而皇圖鞏固者，信皆有得於是也。
恭惟陛下以聰明聖智之資，懋精一執中之學，心之所裕者，與天地合其德；治之所成者，與皇王匹其休。肆今大化流行，百姓太和，德浹于中夏，威行于蠻貊，至治馨香，達于上下，而休徵畢集，千古所未有也。臣何幸躬逢其盛哉！臣嘗竊窺陛下之所以臻此者，信本於學，而學之精實典要
translation_en:
…the essential principles transmitted from one ruler to the next lie precisely here. Yet when your servant has sought the essence of the sagely learning of our two ancestral emperors, surely the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu) and the Mind-Method of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) are its most essential expressions! The Record of Preserving the Mind fully records instances in which emperors of successive ages, in performing sacrifices, responded to calamities and auspicious signs, thereby bequeathing instruction. It gives particular attention to revering Heaven’s wrath and daring not indulge in frivolity or pleasure. The Mind-Method of Sagely Learning sets forth in detail everything concerning the Way governing ruler and minister, father and son, to guide later generations. It places particular emphasis on revering Heaven, emulating the ancestors, employing men, and managing finances. Thus, the learning of our two ancestral emperors is fully manifest in these two books. Refined, pure, steadfast, and undivided, their minds were the very minds of the Two Emperors and Three Kings; in supreme harmony and universal flourishing, their government was the very government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. Heavenly virtue and the Kingly Way stand lofty and radiant: what further doubt can there be? That successive sage rulers have been able to consolidate their predecessors’ achievements, unfold Heaven’s constant principles, and order human relationships, so that the imperial realm has remained secure for more than one hundred and eighty years, surely owes entirely to their grasp of these teachings.
I reverently consider how Your Majesty, endowed with keen perception and sagely wisdom, diligently pursues the learning of refinement, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the Mean. The abundance within your mind accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth; the accomplishments of your government rival the splendor of the august sovereigns and kings of antiquity. Thus today your great transforming influence spreads everywhere, and the common people enjoy supreme harmony. Your virtue permeates the central lands, and your might extends among the Man and Mo peoples. The fragrance of perfect government reaches above and below, and auspicious signs gather in their entirety—something never before seen throughout the ages. How fortunate your servant is to witness this flourishing age in person! Your servant has ventured to discern how Your Majesty has attained this: it is surely rooted in learning. And as for the refined substance and essential guiding principles of that learning …

text:
則又莫過於
敬一之一箴而彝倫之叙典禮之敦所由出也
臣請得而颺言之其曰人有此心萬理咸備
體而行之惟德是據蓋言道本於心也其曰
匪一弗純匪敬弗聚畏天勤民弗遑寧處蓋
言學以體道也其曰敬怠純駁應驗頓殊徵
諸天人如鼓答桴蓋言治以徵學也其曰郊
則恭誠廟嚴孝趨肅于明廷慎于閒居反躬
以實踐也其曰天親民懷永延厥慶光前垂
後綿衍蕃盛考祥以視履也語其目則析之

餘斯其學即二帝三王之學心即二帝三王

之盛德以裕達之為王道而富有之大業以

而且未易以名言矣復何所稱述以為

…then nothing surpasses the Admonition on Reverence and Oneness (Jingyi); from it proceed the proper ordering of the enduring human relationships and the strengthening of canonical rites. Your servant begs leave to proclaim its meaning.

It says: “Human beings possess this mind, in which all principles are fully present. Embody them and put them into practice, relying solely upon virtue.” This means that the Way is rooted in the mind. It says: “Without oneness there is no purity; without reverence there is no concentration. Stand in awe of Heaven and labor for the people, with no leisure to rest at ease.” This means that learning serves to embody the Way. It says: “Reverence and negligence, purity and admixture—their corresponding effects differ utterly. Test them against Heaven and humankind: they respond as a drum responds to its beater.” This means that governance serves to verify learning. It says: “At the suburban sacrifice, be respectful and sincere; in the ancestral temple, proceed solemnly and filially. Be reverent in the illustrious court and circumspect in private.” This is to examine oneself and put these teachings into practice. It says: “Heaven draws near and the people cherish you; your blessings are perpetually prolonged. Bring glory to those before and leave a legacy to those after; may prosperity spread and multiply without end.” This is to examine auspicious signs as a means of assessing one’s conduct.

Consider its particular teachings: it distinguishes them with the utmost precision and without confusion. Investigate its purport: it unites them in their fullest breadth, leaving nothing out. Such learning is the learning of the Two Emperors and Three Kings; such a mind is their mind. The consummate governance thereby achieved adds luster, in the nearer past, to the tradition of the Two Founding Ancestors and the succession of sage emperors, and, in the distant past, rises to the flourishing heights of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Truly, it embodies trustworthiness and brings harmony to fruition, attaining a unity whose workings cannot be fathomed. Preserved within, it is the virtue of Heaven, enriching the abundant virtue that renews itself daily; extended outward, it is the Kingly Way, making flourish the great undertaking that embraces all things. Can one say that the transmission of the Way among emperors and kings does not reside here? Your servant wishes to describe its grandeur, yet finds it difficult even to express in words. title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
日月得天而能久照四時變化而能久成聖
人久於其道而天下化成我
陛下之自箴也亦曰終如其始又曰日新不已故
學必緝熈而後底於純治必永貞而後底於
化
陛下之學亦既純矣天下之化亦既洽矣然
端拱穆清之上一日二日事有萬幾有一之弗
得其宜非純也此勅天之命惟幾惟康堯舜
所為兢兢也四海九州之遠剛柔異性輕重
異宜有一之弗得其所非洽也此一夫不獲
===
時予之辜堯舜所為拳拳也學之純者不使
其或間化之洽者不使其或漓夫然後常敬
常一而道久化成其在兹矣非我
陛下所當致力者乎其要則在求之心而已矣
太祖高皇帝嘗諭輔臣曰防閑此身使不妄動自
謂已能若防閑此心使不妄動尚難能也
成祖文皇帝嘗諭解縉曰心能靜虛事來則應事
去如明鏡止水自然純是天理是
二祖之學誠不外于心而得之也臣願
陛下毅然以道自任上法乎

punctuated:
日月得天而能久照，四時變化而能久成，聖人久於其道而天下化成。」我陛下之自箴也，亦曰：「終如其始。」又曰：「日新不已。」故學必緝熈而後底於純，治必永貞而後底於化。
陛下之學亦既純矣，天下之化亦既洽矣。然端拱穆清之上，一日二日，事有萬幾，有一之弗得其宜，非純也。此「勅天之命，惟幾惟康」，堯舜所為兢兢也。四海九州之遠，剛柔異性，輕重異宜，有一之弗得其所，非洽也。此「一夫不獲，時予之辜」，堯舜所為拳拳也。學之純者，不使其或間；化之洽者，不使其或漓。夫然後常敬常一，而道久化成，其在兹矣。非我陛下所當致力者乎？其要則在求之心而已矣。
太祖高皇帝嘗諭輔臣曰：「防閑此身，使不妄動，自謂已能；若防閑此心，使不妄動，尚難能也。」成祖文皇帝嘗諭解縉曰：「心能靜虛，事來則應，事去如明鏡止水，自然純是天理。」是二祖之學，誠不外于心而得之也。臣願陛下毅然以道自任，上法乎
translation_en:
…“The sun and moon obtain their place in Heaven and so can shine enduringly; the four seasons change and transform and so can bring things to completion enduringly; the sage endures in his Way, and the world is transformed and brought to perfection.” In Your Majesty’s admonitions to yourself, you likewise say, “At the end, be as at the beginning,” and also, “Renew yourself daily without cease.” Thus learning must be continuously cultivated and illuminated before it attains purity, and government must remain steadfastly correct before it achieves transformation.
Your Majesty’s learning has already attained purity, and the transforming influence of your rule has already spread throughout the realm. Yet, as you sit with folded hands in the august serenity of the throne, in the course of a day or two affairs present myriad subtle beginnings. If even one is not handled fittingly, this is not purity. This is the concern expressed in “Attend reverently to Heaven’s mandate, mindful of subtle beginnings and of repose [?],” which made Yao and Shun so vigilant. Throughout the distant reaches of the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, people differ in their firm or yielding dispositions, and circumstances call for different degrees of severity or leniency. If even one person fails to find his proper place, your transforming influence has not reached everywhere. This is the concern expressed in “If a single man does not obtain his due, this is my fault,” which so earnestly occupied Yao and Shun. Allow no interruption in the purity of your learning, and no dilution of the pervasive influence of your transformation. Only then will you remain constantly reverent and single-minded: herein lies enduring in the Way and bringing transformation to completion. Is this not what Your Majesty should strive for? Its essential point lies simply in seeking it within the mind.
Emperor Taizu Gao once instructed his assisting ministers: “To guard and restrain this body so that it does not act recklessly—I consider myself already capable of this. But to guard and restrain this mind so that it does not stir recklessly is still difficult.” Emperor Chengzu Wen once instructed Xie Jin: “If the mind can be tranquil and empty, it responds when affairs arise; when affairs pass, it is like a bright mirror or still water, naturally consisting purely of Heaven’s principle.” The learning of these two ancestral emperors was indeed attained within the mind, without seeking outside it. Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would resolutely take the Way as your own responsibility and model yourself upon…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
二祖反求諸一心養之于念慮未萌之先以存其
寂然不動之體察之于幾務既興之際以妙
其感而遂通之用俾其湛而虛也神而明也
與太虛同其空洞焉日月同其照臨焉四時
同其運行焉萬物同其冲和焉則一心既正
萬化以行敬不期敬而自爾其常敬一不期

二祖，反求諸一心，養之于念慮未萌之先，以存其寂然不動之體；察之于幾務既興之際，以妙其感而遂通之用。俾其湛而虛也，神而明也，與太虛同其空洞焉，日月同其照臨焉，四時同其運行焉，萬物同其冲和焉。則一心既正，萬化以行。敬不期敬而自爾其常敬，一不期一而自爾其常一，天德益以立，王道益以溥矣。帝王道統之傳，不其益光也哉？至于用人必當，而臯夔稷契之在列；行政必允，而禮樂刑政之覃敷，則又此心之妙用，而我陛下之餘事也，何敢以瀆聖聽哉？
陛下倘能鑒臣之愚，而於所謂敬一者，貞之于久，而會之於心，則道統之傳亘古今而獨盛矣。斯文幸甚！宗社幸甚！臣何任祈籲隕越之至！臣謹對。
translation_en:
…the two founding ancestors, and seek within the single mind. Nurture it before thoughts and deliberations have begun to stir, thereby preserving its substance, still and unmoving; examine it when the affairs of government arise, thereby perfecting its function of responding to stimuli and penetrating all things. Let it be limpid and empty, numinous and luminous, sharing the openness of the Great Void, the illumination of the sun and moon, the movement of the four seasons, and the balanced harmony of the myriad things. Once this single mind is rectified, all transformations will proceed. Reverence will remain constant of itself, without deliberately striving for reverence; unity will remain constant of itself, without deliberately striving for unity. Heavenly virtue will become ever more firmly established, and the kingly Way ever more widespread. Will not the transmission of the emperors’ and kings’ succession to the Way shine ever more brightly? As for invariably appointing the right men, so that men like Gao Yao, Kui, Ji, and Xie stand among the officials, and invariably governing fittingly, so that rites, music, punishments, and administration extend everywhere—these are further wondrous functions of this mind, and matters of secondary concern for Your Majesty. How would I dare trouble Your sagely hearing with them?
If Your Majesty can consider your servant’s humble views and, in what is called reverence and unity, remain steadfast over time and bring them together within the mind, then the transmission of the succession to the Way will flourish beyond anything seen throughout past and present. What good fortune for this cultural tradition! What good fortune for the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain! Your servant cannot contain his utmost supplication and trembling apprehension. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
臣張春
臣對臣聞帝王之御世也有君道以臨天下
必有師道以淑天下君道以臨之則天下成
一統之治而內聖之用彰師道以淑之則天
下宗一本之教而外王之體立是故兼君師
之任者必會體用而並全總治教之能者必
合內外而交盛要之治本於道道生於心心
純於敬敬主於一而已矣此自古帝王一脉
相承而無後先之間一理相授而無彼此之
殊為治統之所歸者必為道統之所屬者也
===
苟有治而無教則為有用而無體天下豈有
無體之用哉此其治也必不達有教而無治
則為有體而無用天下豈有無用之體哉此
其教也必不尊無惑乎道統竟莫之底麗也
已

廷而以道統為問甚盛心也顧臣草茅微生章
句末學雖仰誦
陛下敬一之訓有年而無所自得也何足以對揚
休命之萬一乎然慨自隆古君臣密勿相與論

punctuated:
臣張春。
臣對：臣聞帝王之御世也，有君道以臨天下，必有師道以淑天下。君道以臨之，則天下成一統之治，而內聖之用彰；師道以淑之，則天下宗一本之教，而外王之體立。是故兼君師之任者，必會體用而並全；總治教之能者，必合內外而交盛。要之，治本於道，道生於心，心純於敬，敬主於一而已矣。此自古帝王一脉相承，而無後先之間；一理相授，而無彼此之殊。為治統之所歸者，必為道統之所屬者也。苟有治而無教，則為有用而無體，天下豈有無體之用哉？此其治也必不達。有教而無治，則為有體而無用，天下豈有無用之體哉？此其教也必不尊。無惑乎道統竟莫之底麗也已！
陛下策士於廷，而以道統為問，甚盛心也！顧臣草茅微生，章句末學，雖仰誦陛下敬一之訓有年，而無所自得也，何足以對揚休命之萬一乎？然慨自隆古君臣密勿相與論
translation_en:
Your servant Zhang Chun.
Your servant replies: I have heard that when emperors and kings govern the world, if they possess the Way of the ruler by which to preside over all under Heaven, they must also possess the Way of the teacher by which to improve all under Heaven. When they preside through the Way of the ruler, all under Heaven attain unified government, and the functioning of inner sagehood becomes manifest; when they improve the people through the Way of the teacher, all under Heaven honor a teaching rooted in a single source, and the substance of outer kingship is established. Thus those who bear the responsibilities of both ruler and teacher must unite substance and function and perfect both; those who command the capacities for both government and teaching must join the inner and the outer and bring both to flourishing. In essence, government is rooted in the Way; the Way arises from the heart; the heart is purified through reverence; and reverence centers upon oneness. That is all. Since antiquity, emperors and kings have transmitted this in a single line, with no division between earlier and later generations, handing down a single principle with no difference between one and another. Whoever inherits the succession of governance must also inherit the succession of the Way. If there is government without teaching, there is function without substance. How could there be function without substance in the world? Such government will surely fail to achieve its ends. If there is teaching without government, there is substance without function. How could there be substance without function in the world? Such teaching will surely fail to command respect. No wonder the succession of the Way ultimately finds no one in whom to reside!
Your Majesty examines scholars with policy questions at court and has made the succession of the Way the subject of your inquiry: how exalted your purpose is! Yet I am an insignificant man from the countryside, a shallow student of textual explication. Although for years I have reverently recited Your Majesty’s instructions on reverence and oneness, I have attained no understanding of my own. How could I adequately respond to and extol even the ten-thousandth part of your gracious command? Yet I reflect with sorrow that, in high antiquity, rulers and ministers worked diligently together in discussion …

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
道至於叔季之世寥寥數千載蔑無聞矣幸
天篤生
陛下以斯道為已任幸
陛下俯進臣等以斯道為首詢自
陛下於臣言之為試臣之始自臣於
陛下言之為告
君之始而乃不遑他及遠諏帝王之大法近述
祖宗之鴻猷旁求列辟之治以至諸儒之學發至
精之義欲聞至當之論誠千載一時難得之
遇也臣豈敢隱默不宣以欺
===
陛下又豈敢泛引不根以欺吾心哉臣嘗讀書曰
天佑下民作之君作之師言治必有教也又
曰惟皇上帝降衷於下民若有恒性克綏厥
猷惟后言教之在君也故嘗以為君也者以
受天之命言也師也者以立民之命言也必
有其位斯謂受天命而克荷司牧之責必有
其德斯謂立民命而無忝曆數之膺知乎此
而後知道統之所歸矣嗟夫道豈易言哉臣
聞之立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔與
剛立人之道曰仁與義三才一道也伏羲氏

translation_en:
…the Way; by the latter ages of decline, scarcely anything of this had been heard for several thousand years. Fortunately, Heaven brought forth Your Majesty, who takes this Way as his own responsibility. Fortunately, Your Majesty has graciously summoned us, your servants, and made this Way the first subject of inquiry. From Your Majesty’s standpoint in relation to your servant, this marks the beginning of examining me; from your servant’s standpoint in relation to Your Majesty, it marks the beginning of addressing my sovereign. Yet, allowing no time for other matters, you inquire into the great principles of the emperors and kings of distant antiquity, recount the grand designs of your more recent imperial ancestors, and seek widely into the governance of successive rulers and even the learning of the Confucian scholars. You bring forth the most refined meanings and wish to hear the most fitting arguments. Truly, this is a rare encounter, occurring but once in a thousand years. How could your servant dare remain silent and conceal what he knows, thereby deceiving Your Majesty? And how could I dare offer sweeping, unfounded citations, thereby deceiving my own heart?

Your servant has read in the Book of Documents: “Heaven assists the common people, providing them with rulers and providing them with teachers.” This means that governance must include instruction. It also says: “August Heaven Above bestowed an innate moral nature upon the common people. In accordance with their constant nature, it is the sovereign alone who can bring them securely to follow their proper course.” This means that responsibility for instruction rests with the ruler. Thus I have long considered that ‘ruler’ refers to receiving Heaven’s mandate, while ‘teacher’ refers to establishing the people’s moral destiny. Only one who occupies the requisite position can be said to receive Heaven’s mandate and be capable of bearing responsibility for shepherding the people. Only one who possesses the requisite virtue can be said to establish the people’s moral destiny and be worthy of receiving the allotted succession to rule. Only after understanding this can one know where the transmission of the Way properly rests.

Alas! How could the Way be easy to speak of? Your servant has heard: “The Way established for Heaven is called yin and yang; the Way established for Earth is called yielding and firmness; the Way established for humanity is called benevolence and righteousness.” The Three Powers share a single Way. Fuxi…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
之王天下也仰觀俯察以發揮其道於八卦
矣而無文字可考也故曰道統之傳自堯舜
始蓋堯懼夫陰陽剛柔仁義之不恊於一也
而貫之以中舜又懼夫危微之幾中難於執
也而申之以精一自是而談道者有所本學
道者有所宗矣然古昔盛時道之所在位亦
在焉位之所在道亦在焉是以堯授舜以天
下而傳堯之道者即舜也舜授禹以天下而
傳舜之道者即禹也至若湯能改夏之命而
不能不纘禹之舊服文武能改殷之命而不
===
能不率湯之舊章凡以道一而已矣是道也
即受天之命以立民之命者也不公之於天
下不足以見大為富有之業不垂之於萬世
不足以見久為日新之德故惟天下之大人
而後能居天下之大位居天下之大位而後
能行天下之大道行天下之大道而後能繼
天下之大統由今觀之堯舜禹湯文武之德
曰欽明曰濬哲曰勤儉曰寬仁曰敬止為德
不同而同本於心也堯舜禹湯文武之治曰
恊和曰風動曰誕敷曰允殖曰永清為治不

punctuated:
之王天下也，仰觀俯察，以發揮其道於八卦矣，而無文字可考也。故曰：「道統之傳自堯舜始。」蓋堯懼夫陰陽剛柔仁義之不恊於一也，而貫之以中；舜又懼夫危微之幾，中難於執也，而申之以精一。自是而談道者有所本，學道者有所宗矣。然古昔盛時，道之所在，位亦在焉；位之所在，道亦在焉。是以堯授舜以天下，而傳堯之道者即舜也；舜授禹以天下，而傳舜之道者即禹也。至若湯能改夏之命，而不能不纘禹之舊服；文武能改殷之命，而不能不率湯之舊章。凡以道一而已矣。
是道也，即受天之命以立民之命者也。不公之於天下，不足以見大為富有之業；不垂之於萬世，不足以見久為日新之德。故惟天下之大人，而後能居天下之大位；居天下之大位，而後能行天下之大道；行天下之大道，而後能繼天下之大統。由今觀之，堯舜禹湯文武之德，曰欽明，曰濬哲，曰勤儉，曰寬仁，曰敬止，為德不同，而同本於心也。堯舜禹湯文武之治，曰恊和，曰風動，曰誕敷，曰允殖，曰永清，為治不
translation_en:
…when Fuxi ruled all under Heaven, he looked upward and examined what lay below, thereby expounding the Way through the Eight Trigrams. Yet no written records survive for examination. Thus it is said: “The transmission of the succession of the Way begins with Yao and Shun.” Yao feared that yin and yang, softness and firmness, benevolence and righteousness might fail to accord as one, and so he united them through the Mean. Shun further feared that, amid the subtle stirrings of the precarious human mind and the barely perceptible mind of the Way, the Mean would be difficult to hold fast to; he therefore elaborated upon this with the injunction to be discerning and single-minded. From then onward, those who discussed the Way had a foundation, and those who studied it had a guiding authority. In the flourishing ages of antiquity, however, wherever the Way resided, sovereign authority also resided; wherever sovereign authority resided, the Way also resided. Thus Yao entrusted all under Heaven to Shun, and it was Shun who transmitted Yao’s Way. Shun entrusted all under Heaven to Yu, and it was Yu who transmitted Shun’s Way. As for Tang, although he could replace the Xia mandate, he could not but continue Yu’s established undertakings. Although Kings Wen and Wu could replace the Yin mandate, they could not but follow Tang’s established institutions. This was solely because the Way is one.
This Way is precisely that by which one receives Heaven’s mandate and establishes the people’s allotted life. Unless it is shared with all under Heaven, one cannot manifest the undertaking whose greatness consists in abundant possession; unless it is handed down through ten thousand generations, one cannot manifest the virtue whose endurance consists in daily renewal. Thus only a great person in the realm can occupy the realm’s great position. Only after occupying that great position can he put into practice the realm’s great Way; only after putting that great Way into practice can he continue the realm’s great succession. Viewed from the present, the virtues of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu were described as reverence and enlightenment, profound wisdom, diligence and frugality, magnanimity and benevolence, and abiding in reverence. Their virtues differed, yet all were rooted in the heart. Their governance was described as bringing harmonious accord, transforming people as the wind moves them, broadly disseminating instruction, fostering true flourishing, and securing lasting peace. In their governance, they were not…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
同而同本於道也道本於心則廓之萬化者
一此理之根柢治本於道則根之一心者一
此化之流行故博厚以載物高明以覆物悠
久以成物而言大業者必歸焉為天地立心
為生民立命為萬世開太平而言盛德者必
歸焉是則無負君師之任兼體治教之能堯
舜禹湯文武功德獨隆誠如
聖制所謂道統屬之有不得而辭焉者矣乃若韓
愈繼以周公孔子而有止於孟軻之論孟子
繼以皐陶伊尹萊朱太公望散宜生而有見
===
知聞知之說豈下而為臣者亦可與道統之
傳歟臣請言其故矣周公制作禮樂有以備
帝王之所未備孔子刪述六經有以成帝王
之所未成紀綱法度之懿八百年守之而不
敢失性與天道之微七十子學之而不能殫
開物成務功在萬世後有作者莫之與京故
周公孔子必與道統者不可以臣道詘也伊
呂諸臣遭際聖世固有幸而見知於當時而
不為先亦有幸而聞知於異世而不為後嘉
猷之贊彝憲之守竭忠効勞社稷之俊也有

敢失性與天道之徽七十子學之而不能彈
開物成務功在萬世後有作者莫之與京故
周公孔子必與道統者不可以臣道詘也伊
呂諸臣遭際聖世固有幸而見知於當時而
不爲先亦有幸而聞知於異世而不爲後嘉
猷之賛彝憲之守竭忠効勞社稷之俊也有
punctuated:
同而同本於道也。道本於心，則廓之萬化者，一此理之根柢；治本於道，則根之一心者，一此化之流行。故博厚以載物，高明以覆物，悠久以成物，而言大業者必歸焉；為天地立心，為生民立命，為萬世開太平，而言盛德者必歸焉。是則無負君師之任，兼體治教之能。堯舜禹湯文武功德獨隆，誠如聖制所謂道統屬之，有不得而辭焉者矣。
乃若韓愈繼以周公孔子，而有止於孟軻之論；孟子繼以皐陶伊尹萊朱太公望散宜生，而有見知聞知之說，豈下而為臣者亦可與道統之傳歟？臣請言其故矣。周公制作禮樂，有以備帝王之所未備；孔子刪述六經，有以成帝王之所未成。紀綱法度之懿，八百年守之而不敢失；性與天道之微，七十子學之而不能殫。開物成務，功在萬世，後有作者，莫之與京。故周公孔子必與道統者，不可以臣道詘也。伊呂諸臣遭際聖世，固有幸而見知於當時而不為先，亦有幸而聞知於異世而不為後。嘉猷之贊，彝憲之守，竭忠効勞，社稷之俊也。有
translation_en:
…differ, yet all are rooted in the Way. The Way is rooted in the mind: when expanded into the myriad transformations, its root remains this single principle. Government is rooted in the Way: when grounded in the single mind, its transforming influence flows from this unity. Thus, broad and substantial, they bear all things; lofty and luminous, they shelter all things; enduring, they bring all things to completion. Those who speak of great achievements must turn to them. They establish a mind for Heaven and Earth, establish a destiny for the people, and inaugurate supreme peace for ten thousand generations. Those who speak of flourishing virtue must turn to them. In this way they fulfill the responsibility of ruler and teacher, embodying the capacity both to govern and to instruct. The achievements and virtues of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu were uniquely exalted. Truly, as Your Majesty’s imperial composition declares, the succession of the Way devolved upon them, and they could not decline it.
Now Han Yu continued this succession with Zhou Gong and Kongzi, arguing that it ended with Meng Ke; Mengzi continued it with Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Lai Zhu, Taigong Wang, and San Yisheng, speaking of knowing through seeing and knowing through hearing. Could those occupying the subordinate position of minister also participate in transmitting the succession of the Way? Your servant begs leave to explain why. Zhou Gong instituted rites and music, thereby supplying what the sage emperors and kings had not yet supplied. Kongzi edited and transmitted the Six Classics, thereby completing what the sage emperors and kings had not yet completed. The excellence of their governing principles, laws, and institutions was preserved for eight hundred years without anyone daring to depart from it; the subtleties of human nature and the Way of Heaven were studied by the seventy disciples, yet they could not exhaust them. They disclosed the nature of things and brought undertakings to completion, benefiting ten thousand generations. None who arose after them could equal them. Thus Zhou Gong and Kongzi must be included in the succession of the Way: their standing cannot be diminished on account of their position as ministers. Yi Yin, Lü Shang, and the other ministers encountered an age of sage rule. Some indeed had the good fortune to know the Way through seeing in their own time, yet were not thereby ahead; others had the good fortune to know it through hearing in another age, yet were not thereby behind. Assisting with excellent counsels, upholding established statutes, and exhausting their loyalty in devoted service, they were outstanding servants of the state. There is…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
君以主於其上斯統之不可以旁及矣孟子
以其同與聞乎道也故旁及諸臣而不以為
嫌韓愈欲附已於立言者故直推孟以繼周
孔而不懼其僭若以臣君師治教受命立命
之說律之二子安得無遺論哉何則道之在
天下固無時而可息無人而不得而統之在
人有得承與不得焉耳孟韓之後遂有薄漢
唐宋人主治世之功而崇周程朱四臣講論
之學推許其功直儕帝道是豈歷代人主果
俱不足以承藉天命而諸儒者顧足以迓續
===
治統與臣請得而言之周敦頤程顥程頤朱
熹四子者固世之名儒也學于古訓深究淵
源真將遡虞廷之授受孔門之問答而得其
指歸矣觀其圖書作而千古之疑以訂傳義
明而羣聖之秘以發其他所著述微而鬼神
性命顯而禮樂刑政大而綱常倫理小而事
物細微莫不備具誠於斯道為有鉅功蓋訓
詁興於漢矣今則平正通達而穿鑿之弊以
革詞章盛於唐矣今則根極要妙而浮靡之
習以袪四子者豈三代以下世儒俗學可比

punctuated:
君以主於其上，斯統之不可以旁及矣。孟子以其同與聞乎道也，故旁及諸臣而不以為嫌。韓愈欲附已於立言者，故直推孟以繼周孔，而不懼其僭。若以臣君師、治教、受命立命之說律之，二子安得無遺論哉？何則？道之在天下，固無時而可息，無人而不得；而統之在人，有得承與不得焉耳。孟韓之後，遂有薄漢唐宋人主治世之功，而崇周程朱四臣講論之學，推許其功，直儕帝道。是豈歷代人主果俱不足以承藉天命，而諸儒者顧足以迓續治統與？

臣請得而言之。周敦頤、程顥、程頤、朱熹四子者，固世之名儒也。學于古訓，深究淵源，真將遡虞廷之授受、孔門之問答，而得其指歸矣。觀其圖書作，而千古之疑以訂；傳義明，而羣聖之秘以發。其他所著述，微而鬼神性命，顯而禮樂刑政，大而綱常倫理，小而事物細微，莫不備具，誠於斯道為有鉅功。蓋訓詁興於漢矣，今則平正通達，而穿鑿之弊以革；詞章盛於唐矣，今則根極要妙，而浮靡之習以袪。四子者，豈三代以下世儒俗學可比
translation_en:
…a ruler presides above them; this succession therefore cannot extend laterally to include them. Mengzi, considering that they too had come to know the Way, extended it laterally to include these ministers and saw no impropriety in doing so. Han Yu wished to associate himself with those who established enduring teachings, and therefore directly advanced Mengzi as the successor to Zhou Gong and Kongzi, without fearing that this was presumptuous. If we judge these two thinkers by the distinctions between minister, ruler, and teacher [?], between governing and teaching, and between receiving Heaven’s mandate and establishing one’s allotted destiny, how could their arguments be without omissions? Why is this so? The Way in the world can never cease to operate, and no person is incapable of attaining it. As for its succession among human beings, however, some are entitled to inherit it and others are not. After Mengzi and Han Yu, there arose those who disparaged the achievements of the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song in governing the world, while exalting the scholarship expounded by the four ministers Zhou, the two Chengs, and Zhu. They praised these men’s achievements as directly equal to the Way of the sovereigns. Could it really be that the rulers of successive dynasties were all unworthy to receive and uphold Heaven’s mandate, while these Confucian scholars alone were worthy to receive and continue the succession of governance?

Your servant begs leave to explain. The four masters—Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, and Zhu Xi—were certainly renowned Confucian scholars of their age. They studied the ancient teachings and investigated their sources profoundly, truly seeking to trace back the transmission at Shun’s court and the questions and answers in Kongzi’s school, and to grasp their essential meaning. Consider how, through the production of their diagrams and writings, doubts of a thousand ages were resolved; through the elucidation of their commentaries and explanations, the hidden meanings of the many sages were disclosed. Their other writings comprehensively addressed everything: the unseen matters of spirits, human nature, and destiny; the visible institutions of ritual, music, punishments, and government; the great principles of social relationships and ethical order; and the smallest details of affairs and things. They truly rendered immense service to this Way. Philological exegesis arose under the Han; through their work it became balanced, sound, and thoroughly intelligible, and the faults of strained interpretation were eliminated. Literary composition flourished under the Tang; through their work it became rooted in the deepest essentials and subtleties, and habits of superficial ornamentation were dispelled. How could these four masters be compared with the conventional scholars and commonplace learning of the ages after the Three Dynasties…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
倫耶雖然視周公之制作孔子之刪述則亦
有間矣故嘗謂使四子親炙仲尼之門當居
顔閔之亞得堯舜禹湯文武之君而事之固
亦伊呂之儔精思力踐允矣述者之賢而窮
神知化未可遽躋作者之聖乃欲借周孔而
直附之於帝王之統恐非四子之本意矣由
其門人知師之可尊而不知統之不可僭始
於宗信所學而成於張大其說後之儒者承
訛踵舛直據以為確論耳抑孰知道非自相
發明之謂也必立民之命而後謂之大道統
===
非私相推許之謂也必受天之命而後謂之
大統三代而下漢唐宋諸君亦嘗受命而興
膺有撫世宰物之責者當天心之厭亂世變
之已窮英主者起而開一代之治此其時三
綱賴以不淪九法賴以不斁鬼神賴之以享
祀蒼生賴之以出水火於衽席夫固有道以
行乎其間也是故寬仁豁達者有帝王之度
仁義既効者有帝王之功恭儉仁厚者有帝
王之體偉畧雄謨追湯武以上為不足風醇
俗厚視成康以下為有餘之數君者豈可槩

punctuated:
倫耶？雖然，視周公之制作、孔子之刪述，則亦有間矣。故嘗謂，使四子親炙仲尼之門，當居顔閔之亞；得堯舜禹湯文武之君而事之，固亦伊呂之儔。精思力踐，允矣述者之賢；而窮神知化，未可遽躋作者之聖。乃欲借周孔而直附之於帝王之統，恐非四子之本意矣。由其門人知師之可尊，而不知統之不可僭，始於宗信所學，而成於張大其說，後之儒者承訛踵舛，直據以為確論耳。抑孰知道非自相發明之謂也，必立民之命而後謂之大道；統非私相推許之謂也，必受天之命而後謂之大統。
三代而下，漢唐宋諸君亦嘗受命而興，膺有撫世宰物之責者。當天心之厭亂、世變之已窮，英主者起而開一代之治。此其時，三綱賴以不淪，九法賴以不斁，鬼神賴之以享祀，蒼生賴之以出水火於衽席，夫固有道以行乎其間也。是故寬仁豁達者有帝王之度，仁義既効者有帝王之功，恭儉仁厚者有帝王之體。偉畧雄謨，追湯武以上為不足；風醇俗厚，視成康以下為有餘之數君者，豈可槩
translation_en:
…be ranked alongside them? Even so, measured against the institutions established by the Duke of Zhou and the editing and transmission undertaken by Confucius, they still fall short. Thus I have often said that, had these four masters received instruction personally at the school of Zhongni, they would have ranked immediately below Yan Hui and Min Sun; had they found rulers such as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, or Wu to serve, they would surely have been peers of Yi Yin and Lü Shang. Through profound reflection and earnest practice, they assuredly attained the worthiness of transmitters; yet in fathoming the numinous and understanding transformation, they cannot hastily be raised to the sagehood of originators. To invoke the Duke of Zhou and Confucius in order to attach them directly to the succession of emperors and kings was, I fear, not the original intention of the four masters. Their disciples knew that their teachers deserved reverence, but did not know that this succession could not be usurped. What began as devotion to and trust in their learning ended in exaggeration of their teachings. Later scholars perpetuated these errors and repeated these mistakes, simply taking them as established judgments. Yet who understands that the Way does not mean merely elucidating teachings among themselves? Only after securing the livelihood of the people may it be called the Great Way. Nor does succession mean privately endorsing one another: only after receiving Heaven’s mandate may it be called the Great Succession.
After the Three Dynasties, various rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song likewise rose upon receiving the mandate and assumed responsibility for bringing peace to the world and governing its affairs. When Heaven had grown weary of disorder and worldly upheavals had reached their limit, heroic rulers arose to inaugurate an era of good government. At such times, the Three Bonds depended on them to avoid collapse, the Nine Laws depended on them to avoid decay, the spirits depended on them to receive sacrifices, and the common people depended on them to escape fire and flood and attain the comfort of sleeping mats. Surely the Way was indeed at work among them. Thus those who were magnanimous, humane, and open-minded possessed the bearing of emperors and kings; those whose humanity and righteousness produced results possessed the achievements of emperors and kings; and those who were reverent, frugal, humane, and generous possessed the essential character of emperors and kings. These several rulers, whose grand strategies and mighty plans made even comparison with Tang and Wu and earlier rulers insufficient to do them justice, and whose wholesome social mores and substantial customs more than matched those of rulers from Cheng and Kang onward—how could they indiscriminately be…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
少哉然而資質之美僅符其近似學問之疎
未止諸至善其於堯舜禹湯文武道統之傳
猶有遺恨矣夫以數君德澤加於四海功烈
著諸天地而所養未粹猶不可當帝王之統
乃儒者以講學窮理著書立言之微勞而可
遽若是班耶大賢如四子且不可而況不及
於四子者乎故臣竊譬斯道之統猶之木之
本水之源也標枝條幹不可不謂之木而猶
為本之支流波衍派不可不謂之水而猶為
源之委是故體用並全內外交盛者得道之
===
本源者也數君有行道之責而全體未純四
子有體道之功而大用莫究此臣所謂有用
而無體治必不達有體而無用教必不尊均
非統之所可寄者矣要之正學之興自有其
時大統之歸不為無待天啓我
明
祖宗
列聖相授守一道而我
皇上益光大而中興之有以遠紹帝王之統而陋
漢唐宋於不為者豈偶然哉洪惟我

punctuated:
少哉？然而資質之美，僅符其近似；學問之疎，未止諸至善。其於堯舜禹湯文武道統之傳，猶有遺恨矣。夫以數君德澤加於四海，功烈著諸天地，而所養未粹，猶不可當帝王之統，乃儒者以講學窮理、著書立言之微勞，而可遽若是班耶？大賢如四子且不可，而況不及於四子者乎？故臣竊譬斯道之統，猶之木之本、水之源也。標枝條幹，不可不謂之木，而猶為本之支；流波衍派，不可不謂之水，而猶為源之委。是故體用並全、內外交盛者，得道之本源者也。數君有行道之責，而全體未純；四子有體道之功，而大用莫究。此臣所謂有用而無體，治必不達；有體而無用，教必不尊，均非統之所可寄者矣。
要之，正學之興，自有其時；大統之歸，不為無待。天啓我明，祖宗列聖相授，守一道，而我皇上益光大而中興之，有以遠紹帝王之統，而陋漢唐宋於不為者，豈偶然哉？洪惟我
translation_en:
…be held in slight regard? Yet the excellence of their natural endowments amounted only to an approximation, while the inadequacy of their learning kept them from resting in the highest good. In their transmission of the succession to the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, something still remained to be regretted. These several rulers extended their beneficence throughout the realm, and their achievements shone between Heaven and Earth; yet because what they had cultivated within themselves was not wholly pure, they still could not qualify as successors in the line of true emperors and kings. How, then, could Confucian scholars, with their modest labors of expounding learning, investigating principles, writing books, and setting forth doctrines, immediately be placed in such ranks? Even great worthies such as the Four Masters could not qualify, much less those who fall short of them.
Thus your servant ventures to compare this succession to the Way to the root of a tree or the source of a stream. The treetops, branches, shoots, and trunk must all be called parts of the tree, yet they remain offshoots of its root. Flowing waves and branching currents must all be called water, yet they remain the downstream extensions of its source. Hence those in whom substance and function are both complete, and inward cultivation and outward accomplishment alike flourish, have grasped the root and source of the Way. Those several rulers bore responsibility for putting the Way into practice, yet its substance was not wholly pure in them. The Four Masters achieved much in embodying the Way, yet could not fully realize its great function. This is what your servant means by saying that where there is function without substance, government necessarily fails to attain its ends; where there is substance without function, teaching necessarily fails to command reverence. Neither can be entrusted with the succession.
In sum, the flourishing of correct learning has its appointed time, and the great succession finds its rightful recipient only when the requisite conditions arise. Heaven opened the way for our Ming dynasty. Our founding and ancestral sovereigns, a succession of sage rulers, transmitted it to one another, preserving a single Way. Our Emperor has further magnified it and brought about its revival. 聖制述其要曰體堯舜授受之要而允執厥中論

道明則天地聖人之心可見至治之功可成

translation_en:
…Emperor Gao, Taizu, first laid the foundations, and the influence of this Way began to spread. As his imperial writings set forth its essentials: “Embody the essentials of the transmission from Yao to Shun, and faithfully hold fast to the Mean; examine the workings of the human mind in its emptiness and spiritual responsiveness, and preserve it with undivided attention.” This is what is meant. Our Emperor Wen, Chengzu, subsequently succeeded to the throne, and the transmission of this Way became still more firmly established. As his imperial writings declare: “The government of emperors and kings is rooted entirely in the Way.” They also state: “When the Way of the Six Classics is made clear, the minds of Heaven, Earth, and the sages can be discerned, and the achievements of perfect government can be realized.” This is what is meant. Although our two founding ancestors pacified the realm through military achievements, their pure essence was profound and all-embracing, and their brilliance shone forth. Meanings that classical scholars and learned men could not fathom in a lifetime became authoritative standards as soon as these emperors gave them utterance. Whether in instructions to their families, edicts to their officials, decisions on affairs of state, or moments of leisure within the palace, every word they expressed embodied the subtle profundities of the learning of the mind. There was thus good reason that they carried forward the orthodox transmission of the Way from the emperors and kings of antiquity and laid the foundations for peace throughout ten thousand generations.
The succeeding sage emperors perpetuated these blessings and furthered these accomplishments, bequeathing abundance and extending their legacy down to the present, more than 180 years later. Ah, how magnificent! Then Your Majesty came to inherit this great foundation. Diligent in moral transformation and government, you survey the distant past with lofty vision and ponder it with solemn depth. You recognize that what enabled the Two Emperors and Three Kings to govern the realm was this Way and this mind; and what enabled our imperial ancestors and succeeding sage emperors to govern the realm was likewise this Way and this mind. As for preserving the mind…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
要惟敬惟一而已矣力而行之日新月盛于
是攄發
宸衷製箴垂訓頒示學校覃被遐荒今者
聖諭家習戶曉師以為教弟子以為學先王之道
大明於天下矣此我
皇上以聰明睿智之資緝熈光明之學妙契道之
大原自得千載不傳之緒者也
踐祚以來紀綱振肅禮樂明備神人和洽海宇
寧謐得非根之心而廓之化盛德大業不可
尚者乎頃歲又於
===
===
文華殿左祀伏羲以下至周公孔子十一聖尊
以師稱著之祀典孟氏而下無取焉是蓋涵
養熟而見道益明閱歷深而履道靡懈真知
夫大道之師外數聖不可以他及而天命之
歸在今日不容以自諉者矣
大聖人之作為何其度越尋常萬萬也哉而猶不
自滿假有若望道未見者焉不曰敬一已知
之矣乃曰舍是又何所致力而可臣誠不知
舍是將何所致力也臣願
陛下無舍是而已蓋昔者堯之世極治矣堯不自

punctuated:
要，惟敬惟一而已矣。力而行之，日新月盛。于是攄發宸衷，製箴垂訓，頒示學校，覃被遐荒。今者聖諭家習戶曉，師以為教，弟子以為學，先王之道大明於天下矣。此我皇上以聰明睿智之資，緝熈光明之學，妙契道之大原，自得千載不傳之緒者也。踐祚以來，紀綱振肅，禮樂明備，神人和洽，海宇寧謐，得非根之心而廓之化，盛德大業不可尚者乎？頃歲又於文華殿左祀伏羲以下至周公、孔子十一聖，尊以師稱，著之祀典，孟氏而下無取焉。是蓋涵養熟而見道益明，閱歷深而履道靡懈，真知夫大道之師，外數聖不可以他及，而天命之歸在今日不容以自諉者矣。
大聖人之作為，何其度越尋常萬萬也哉！而猶不自滿假，有若望道未見者焉。不曰：「敬一已知之矣。」乃曰：「舍是又何所致力而可？」臣誠不知舍是將何所致力也。臣願陛下無舍是而已。蓋昔者堯之世極治矣，堯不自
translation_en:
…the essential requirement is simply reverence and single-mindedness. Through strenuous practice, progress is renewed daily and flourishes monthly. Thus Your Majesty expressed your imperial thoughts, composed an admonition to bequeath instruction, and distributed it to the schools, extending its influence to the distant frontiers. Now the sacred instruction is studied in every family and understood in every household; teachers use it to teach, and disciples use it to learn. The Way of the former kings has become brilliantly manifest throughout the realm. This is how our Emperor, endowed with intelligence and sagely wisdom, has cultivated ever more luminous learning, wondrously apprehended the great source of the Way, and personally recovered the thread of a transmission interrupted for a thousand years. Since ascending the throne, you have restored discipline to the governing order, clarified and perfected rites and music, brought spirits and people into harmony, and secured peace throughout the realm. Is this not a transformation rooted in the heart and extended outward, a flourishing virtue and great achievement that cannot be surpassed? In recent years, moreover, to the left of the Hall of Literary Brilliance, you have offered sacrifices to eleven sages, from Fu Xi down to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, honored them with the designation of teacher, and entered them in the sacrificial canon. None from Mengzi onward was included. Surely this shows that, as your self-cultivation has matured, your perception of the Way has become ever clearer, and as your experience has deepened, your practice of the Way has remained unflagging. You truly understand that no others can rank alongside those few sages as teachers of the Great Way, and that, now that Heaven’s Mandate has devolved upon you, you cannot disclaim its responsibility.
How immeasurably the actions of the great sage surpass the ordinary! Yet you remain without complacency, as though gazing toward the Way without yet having seen it. You do not say, “I already understand reverence and single-mindedness,” but instead say, “Apart from this, to what else could I properly devote my efforts?” Your servant truly does not know to what else one could devote one’s efforts apart from this. Your servant wishes only that Your Majesty never abandon it. For in antiquity, the age of Yao attained the utmost order, yet Yao did not himself…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
知也而問之在朝在野焉禹之德至盛矣禹
不自知也而且設鼛鐸鞀鐘焉臣有以知
陛下之心即堯問在朝在野之心也即禹設鼛鐸
鞀鐘之心也臣等何幸躬逢
聖人在
天子之位君子聞大道之要小人蒙至治之澤而
唐虞三代之盛復見於
今日哉臣於終篇竊有感夫
聖制以審於名實之歸望臣等也夫名實之辨世
運之否泰民命之休戚風俗之隆汙所繇繫
===
者也而可以不審哉臣故為之說曰人臣議
道於下則有道學之名而無其實人君倡道
於上則有道學之實而無其名唐虞三代之
盛未聞有其名而可封之俗比屋皆然干城
腹心武夫且爾實勝故也
陛下建中立極倡之於上而天下遵道遵義無敢
議之於下有實而無其名此臣所謂唐虞三
代之盛復見於
今日者也雖然審天下之名實易審一心之名
實難道也者在天為實理在人為實心所貴

臣故為之說曰：「人臣議道於下，則有道學之名而無其實；人君倡道於上，則有道學之實而無其名。」唐虞三代之盛，未聞有其名，而可封之俗，比屋皆然；干城腹心，武夫且爾，實勝故也。陛下建中立極，倡之於上，而天下遵道遵義，無敢議之於下，有實而無其名，此臣所謂唐虞三代之盛復見於今日者也。

雖然，審天下之名實易，審一心之名實難。道也者，在天為實理，在人為實心。所貴
translation_en:
…know it himself, and so he questioned those at court and those outside it. Yu’s virtue was supremely flourishing, yet Yu did not recognize this himself and moreover set out a large drum, a clapper bell, a hand drum, and a bell. Your servant thus knows that Your Majesty’s heart is the very heart with which Yao questioned those at court and outside it, the very heart with which Yu set out those instruments. How fortunate we, your servants, are to encounter in our own lifetimes a sage occupying the Son of Heaven’s throne! Gentlemen hear the essentials of the Great Way, ordinary people receive the blessings of perfect government, and the flourishing age of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties appears again today! As I bring this essay to a close, I am deeply moved by the expectation expressed in Your Majesty’s composition that we examine where name and reality ultimately lead. For the distinction between name and reality is what determines whether the age declines or prospers, whether the people suffer or flourish, and whether customs are elevated or debased. How could it go unexamined?

Your servant therefore offers this explanation: “When ministers discuss the Way below, there is the name of Learning of the Way, but not its reality; when the ruler promotes the Way above, there is the reality of Learning of the Way, but not its name.” In the flourishing age of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, this name was unheard of, yet customs were such that every household had people worthy of enfeoffment. Even warriors were shields and ramparts, trusted confidants of their lord. This was because reality prevailed. Your Majesty establishes the Mean and sets the supreme standard, promoting the Way from above, while all under Heaven follow the Way and righteousness, none daring to debate it below. There is the reality without the name: this is what your servant means by saying that the flourishing age of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties appears again today.

Nevertheless, examining name and reality throughout the realm is easy; examining name and reality within one’s own heart is difficult. The Way, in Heaven, is real principle; in human beings, it is a sincere heart. What is valued…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
於求道者以實心體夫實理以實理見諸實
事以實事崇其實德而審此心之實否則在
於謹獨而已人所不知己所獨知天下之真
知也一念之發而為敬天為勤民為法祖果
肫肫然為己而法歟則實矣少有為人之心
斯未免雜之以名也閑邪而存誠領惡而全
好夫是之謂知審知審則擬議而變化成淵
泉而道義出以之用人邪正不淆以之行政
是非莫眩而天下臻實效矣是故必審一心
之名實而後能審天下之名實也要之
===
陛下敬一之訓至矣盡矣復何以加之循名責實
得

臣謹對

punctuated: 於求道者，以實心體夫實理，以實理見諸實事，以實事崇其實德，而審此心之實否，則在於謹獨而已。人所不知，己所獨知，天下之真知也。一念之發，而為敬天、為勤民、為法祖，果肫肫然為己而法歟？則實矣。少有為人之心，斯未免雜之以名也。閑邪而存誠，領惡而全好，夫是之謂知審。知審則擬議而變化成，淵泉而道義出。以之用人，邪正不淆；以之行政，是非莫眩，而天下臻實效矣。是故必審一心之名實，而後能審天下之名實也。要之，陛下敬一之訓，至矣，盡矣，復何以加之？循名責實，得陛下為之嚴師，務實勝而不務名勝，臣等敢不勉自砥礪，以期無負今日千載一時之遇哉？臣不勝戰慄隕越之至，臣謹對。
translation_en:
…in seeking the Way is to apprehend true principle with a sincere heart, manifest true principle in actual deeds, and through actual deeds enhance one's genuine virtue. To discern whether this heart is sincere depends solely on vigilance when alone. What others do not know, but one alone knows oneself, is the world's true knowledge. When a thought arises—to revere Heaven, to labor for the people, or to emulate the ancestors—does it truly proceed with wholehearted sincerity, for one's own cultivation and emulation [?]? If so, it is genuine. If there is even the slightest intention of acting for others to see, concern for reputation inevitably becomes mixed with it. Guarding against perversity and preserving sincerity, restraining evil [?] and keeping goodness intact: this is what is meant by knowing how to discern. With such discernment, deliberation brings transformations to completion, and the Way and righteousness issue forth as from a deep spring. Employ people on this basis, and the wicked and upright will not be confused; conduct government on this basis, and right and wrong will not be obscured. All under Heaven will thus attain substantive results. One must therefore discern name and substance within one's own heart before one can discern name and substance throughout the realm.

In sum, Your Majesty's instruction to maintain reverent single-mindedness is perfect and exhaustive. What more could be added? In requiring substance to match name, we have Your Majesty as our stern teacher. Striving for preeminence in substance rather than reputation, how could we, your servants, dare not diligently discipline ourselves, hoping not to prove unworthy of today's opportunity, encountered but once in a thousand years? Your servant is overwhelmed by trembling and fear of failure. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
臣胡正蒙
臣對臣聞帝王任君師之責以臨御天下也
有治法以永萬世無疆之業有心法以續千
載不傳之統何謂治法敬天勤民盡倫盡制
以成參贊繼立之功者也何謂心法存心體
道惟敬惟一以懋緝煕光明之學者也有是
治法而後帝王之道以行有是心法而後帝
王之道以明道行於天下則有以盡祈天永
命之實致四海雍煕之化而萬世之大業在
是矣道明於天下則有以闡精義至理之存
