臣胡正蒙。

臣對：臣聞帝王任君師之責以臨御天下也，有治法以永萬世無疆之業，有心法以續千載不傳之統。何謂治法？敬天勤民，盡倫盡制，以成參贊繼立之功者也。何謂心法？存心體道，惟敬惟一，以懋緝煕光明之學者也。有是治法，而後帝王之道以行；有是心法，而後帝王之道以明。道行於天下，則有以盡祈天永命之實，致四海雍煕之化，而萬世之大業在是矣。道明於天下，則有以闡精義至理之存，發千古淵源之秘，而羣聖之至德在是矣。茍治法不弘，則無以行道，而君天下之責有未盡；心法不啓，則無以明道，而師天下之責有未全，皆不可以與於道統之傳也。是故二帝三王，職任君師，道隆德業，治法心法兼舉以無遺，有實有名，相符而不謬。此其道統之傳，歷世無間，而千載之下，必有在於我太祖高皇帝、成祖文皇帝，以至於皇上之大聖乎！恭惟
translation_en:
Your servant, Hu Zhengmeng.

Your servant replies: I have heard that emperors and kings, in assuming the responsibilities of ruler and teacher to govern all under Heaven, possess methods of governance by which to perpetuate their boundless enterprise for ten thousand generations, and a teaching of the mind by which to renew the succession that had gone untransmitted for a thousand years. What are methods of governance? Revering Heaven, diligently caring for the people, fully fulfilling human relationships and institutional provisions, and thereby accomplishing the work of assisting Heaven and Earth and carrying forward and establishing their work. What is the teaching of the mind? Preserving the mind and embodying the Way, maintaining reverence and unity of purpose, and thereby diligently pursuing the learning that continually advances toward illumination. Only with these methods of governance can the Way of emperors and kings be put into practice; only with this teaching of the mind can their Way be made manifest. When the Way is practiced throughout all under Heaven, there are means to fulfill in substance the prayer to Heaven for an enduring mandate and to bring about harmonious and flourishing transformation within the Four Seas. Herein lies the great enterprise of ten thousand generations. When the Way is made manifest throughout all under Heaven, there are means to elucidate subtle meanings and ultimate principles and to disclose the hidden depths of their age-old source. Herein lies the consummate virtue of all the sages.

If methods of governance are not extended, there is no means to practice the Way, and the responsibility of ruling all under Heaven remains unfulfilled. If the teaching of the mind is not opened up, there is no means to make the Way manifest, and the responsibility of teaching all under Heaven remains incomplete. In either case, one cannot participate in transmitting the succession of the Way. Thus the Two Emperors and Three Kings discharged the duties of ruler and teacher; their Way exalted their virtue and achievements. They applied both methods of governance and the teaching of the mind, leaving nothing neglected. They possessed both substance and name, which corresponded without discrepancy. The succession of the Way was thus transmitted through successive ages without interruption. A thousand years later, must it not reside in the great sageliness of our Emperor Taizu Gao, Emperor Chengzu Wen, and, down to the present, His Majesty? I reverently reflect that …

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝陛下亶聰明睿智之資紹豐亨熈洽之運居
堯舜禹湯文武之位有堯舜禹湯文武之德
臨御以来敬
天法
祖峻德塞於宇宙敘倫惇典鴻業冒於海隅德業
之盛比隆於二帝三王而陋漢唐宋於下風
矣比者
萬幾之暇進臣等於
廷詢以帝王道統之傳臣在學校嘗莊誦
敬一箴五箴註而涵濡於道化久矣敢不對揚
===
明詔於萬一乎臣聞天生萬民慮其無所主也故
作之君以主之惟皇降衷慮其不自覺也故
作之師以覺之於是乎有繼天立極之聖人
中天地以為三綱五常之主任行道之責以
君天下而恢弘化理彌綸參贊之事其身之
矣任明道之責以師天下而發揮精蘊教誨
啓迪之事其身之矣惟其君天下也故有敘
倫惇典以建治法於無疆而道行焉惟其師
天下也故有垂世立教以昭心法於不替而
道明焉行道明道非有二途作君作師實惟

臣聞天生萬民，慮其無所主也，故作之君以主之；惟皇降衷，慮其不自覺也，故作之師以覺之。於是乎有繼天立極之聖人，中天地以為三綱五常之主。任行道之責以君天下，而恢弘化理、彌綸參贊之事，其身之矣；任明道之責以師天下，而發揮精蘊、教誨啓迪之事，其身之矣。惟其君天下也，故有敘倫惇典，以建治法於無疆，而道行焉；惟其師天下也，故有垂世立教，以昭心法於不替，而道明焉。行道明道，非有二途；作君作師，實惟
translation_en:
… Your Majesty the Emperor truly possesses the gifts of keen perception and sagacious wisdom and has inherited an age of abundant prosperity and harmonious peace. You occupy the position of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu and possess their virtues. Since ascending the throne, you have revered Heaven and emulated your ancestors. Your lofty virtue fills the universe; you order human relationships and uphold the enduring norms, and your great achievements extend to the remotest shores. The fullness of your virtue and achievements rivals that of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, relegating the Han, Tang, and Song to an inferior place. Recently, in a respite from your myriad affairs, you summoned us, your servants, to court and questioned us about the transmission of the succession to the Way among emperors and kings. While in the schools, I have reverently recited the Admonition on Reverent Oneness and the Commentary on the Five Admonitions and have long been steeped in the transforming influence of the Way. How could I dare fail to respond to and extol even a ten-thousandth part of your illustrious edict?
Your servant has heard that Heaven brought forth the myriad people and, concerned that they had no one to govern them, established rulers to govern them. August Heaven bestowed an innate moral nature upon them and, concerned that they could not awaken to it themselves, established teachers to awaken them. Thus arose sages who continued Heaven’s work and established the supreme standard, standing at the center of Heaven and Earth as masters of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues. They assumed responsibility for putting the Way into practice as rulers of all under Heaven, personally undertaking the work of extending transformative governance, comprehensively ordering affairs, and assisting Heaven and Earth in their creative activity. They assumed responsibility for making the Way clear as teachers of all under Heaven, personally undertaking the work of unfolding its subtle profundities and instructing and enlightening the people. Precisely because they ruled all under Heaven, they ordered human relationships and upheld the enduring norms, establishing methods of government for all time, so that the Way was put into practice. Precisely because they taught all under Heaven, they established teachings to be handed down through the ages, illuminating the method of cultivating the mind so that it would never lapse, and thus the Way was made clear. Putting the Way into practice and making it clear are not two separate paths; serving as ruler and serving as teacher are truly …

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
一致皆聖人體天之意成天之能以無忝於
天之所以與我者耳粵稽諸古道之大原出
於天而寄於聖人故堯則得統於天而有允
執厥中之㫖道統之說昉於此矣人心惟危
道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中則舜之得統
於堯也祗台德先建中制心則禹之得統於
舜湯之得統於禹也緝熙敬止執競惟烈則
文武之得統於湯也一貫之傳博約之教則
孔子之得統於文也當其時若堯以明德睦
族而成時雍之治舜以徽典敘揆而成風動
===
之治禹以典則修和而成永賴之治湯以肇
修人紀而成允懷之治文武以綱紀建極而
成咸和永清之治是數聖人者達而在上故
其道行然精一執中以開萬世之心法羣聖
相傳昭垂罔極道之大明於天下萬世者不
可易也孔子窮而在下故其道明然斟酌禮
樂刪述六經以立萬世之治法而羣聖之統
賴以益光道之所在雖未嘗身親行之而所
以垂示於天下萬世者皆其功矣臣故曰治
法心法兼舉無遺所以得道統之傳者此也

punctuated: 一致，皆聖人體天之意，成天之能，以無忝於天之所以與我者耳。粵稽諸古，道之大原出於天，而寄於聖人。故堯則得統於天，而有「允執厥中」之㫖，道統之說昉於此矣。「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中」，則舜之得統於堯也。「祗台德先」、「建中制心」，則禹之得統於舜、湯之得統於禹也。「緝熙敬止」、「執競惟烈」，則文武之得統於湯也。「一貫」之傳、「博約」之教，則孔子之得統於文也。當其時，若堯以明德睦族而成時雍之治，舜以徽典敘揆而成風動之治，禹以典則修和而成永賴之治，湯以肇修人紀而成允懷之治，文武以綱紀建極而成咸和永清之治。是數聖人者，達而在上，故其道行。然精一執中，以開萬世之心法，羣聖相傳，昭垂罔極，道之大明於天下萬世者，不可易也。孔子窮而在下，故其道明。然斟酌禮樂，刪述六經，以立萬世之治法，而羣聖之統賴以益光。道之所在，雖未嘗身親行之，而所以垂示於天下萬世者，皆其功矣。臣故曰：治法心法，兼舉無遺，所以得道統之傳者，此也。
translation_en:
…are one in their ultimate purpose. In all this, the sage embodies Heaven’s intent and brings Heaven’s capacities to fulfillment, so as not to dishonor what Heaven has bestowed upon him. Examining antiquity, we find that the great source of the Way issues from Heaven and is entrusted to the sages. Thus Yao received the succession from Heaven and gave the injunction, “Truly hold fast to the Mean.” The teaching concerning the succession of the Way began here. “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded; truly hold fast to the Mean”: this represents Shun’s receiving the succession from Yao. “Reverently put my virtue first” and “Establish the Mean and regulate the mind”: these represent Yu’s receiving the succession from Shun and Tang’s receiving it from Yu. “Continue in brightness and abide in reverence” and “Mighty in strength, illustrious in achievement”: these represent Wen and Wu’s receiving the succession from Tang. The transmission of the teaching of “one thread running through all” and the instruction to “broaden learning and restrain oneself through ritual” represent Kongzi’s receiving the succession from Wen.

In their respective times, Yao illuminated virtue and brought harmony to his kin, achieving a reign of universal concord. Shun put the splendid norms in order and arranged the affairs of government, achieving a reign whose influence moved the people like the wind. Yu cultivated harmony through standards and rules, achieving a reign upon which people could rely forever. Tang began by setting human relationships in order, achieving a reign that truly won the people’s allegiance. Wen and Wu established the supreme standard through ordering principles, achieving universal harmony and lasting peace. These sages attained high position, and thus their Way was put into practice. Yet through discernment, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the Mean, they also disclosed the method of cultivating the mind for all ages. The sages transmitted it to one another, handing it down in undiminished radiance. That the Way was thereby made abundantly clear to all under Heaven for myriad generations is an unalterable truth.

Kongzi lacked opportunity and remained in a lowly position, and thus his Way was made manifest through teaching. Yet he weighed and ordered rites and music, edited and expounded the Six Classics, and thereby established methods of government for all ages; through these efforts, the succession of the sages gained still greater brilliance. Although he never personally put the Way into practice in government, all that was handed down as instruction to the world for myriad generations was his achievement. Thus I, your servant, say: to embrace both the methods of government and the methods of cultivating the mind, omitting neither—this is how one receives the transmission of the succession of the Way.

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
孟軻氏羣聖之敘曰堯舜湯文孔子者以明
傳之有屬曰禹皐陶伊尹萊朱太公望散宜
生者以明傳之有因故見知聞知之說興而
道統相傳之緒明矣韓愈原道之論首自堯
舜終於孔孟較諸孟氏之言雖詳畧不同語
其敘相傳之統夫豈有二乎哉然道之在天
下未嘗亡也由周而來以至於漢唐宋之世
英君誼辟間見迭興其德澤之所加功烈之
所著或寬仁愛人規摹弘遠或身致太平刑
措不用或仁厚立國以德化民即其功德之
===
成庶幾乎古帝王之盛亦宜其可以與於道
統之傳也特正心修己之功或有未至操存
涵養之學或有未純求其粹然一出於正卓
然獨得其宗以幾於精一執中之心法者不
可得也其所謂學既非二帝三王之學則其
所謂治亦非二帝三王之治矣烏足以語於
道統之傳哉韓愈所謂軻之死而不得其傳
者此也有宋之世真儒輩出道學大明周惇
頤奮於百世之下不由師傳默契道體建圖
屬書根極領要程顥辨異端似是之非開百

孟軻氏羣聖之敘，曰堯、舜、湯、文、孔子者，以明傳之有屬；曰禹、皐陶、伊尹、萊朱、太公望、散宜生者，以明傳之有因。故見知聞知之說興，而道統相傳之緒明矣。韓愈《原道》之論，首自堯舜，終於孔孟，較諸孟氏之言，雖詳畧不同，語其敘相傳之統，夫豈有二乎哉？然道之在天下，未嘗亡也。由周而來，以至於漢唐宋之世，英君誼辟，間見迭興。其德澤之所加，功烈之所著，或寬仁愛人，規摹弘遠；或身致太平，刑措不用；或仁厚立國，以德化民。即其功德之成，庶幾乎古帝王之盛，亦宜其可以與於道統之傳也。特正心修己之功，或有未至；操存涵養之學，或有未純。求其粹然一出於正，卓然獨得其宗，以幾於精一執中之心法者，不可得也。其所謂學，既非二帝三王之學，則其所謂治，亦非二帝三王之治矣。烏足以語於道統之傳哉？韓愈所謂軻之死而不得其傳者，此也。

Meng Ke, in his account of the succession of sages, names Yao, Shun, Tang, Wen, and Confucius to make clear to whom the transmission belonged; he names Yu, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Lai Zhu, Taigong Wang, and San Yisheng to make clear through whom it proceeded. Thus arose the explanation of knowing through seeing and knowing through hearing, and the thread of the successive transmission of the Way became clear. Han Yu’s discourse, An Inquiry into the Way, begins with Yao and Shun and ends with Confucius and Mengzi. Although it differs in fullness of detail from Mengzi’s account, how could the two differ in their account of this lineage of transmission?

Yet the Way has never disappeared from the world. From the Zhou down through the Han, Tang, and Song, outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns appeared from time to time and arose in succession. In the reach of their beneficence and the distinction of their achievements, some were magnanimous and humane, loving the people and planning on a grand and far-reaching scale; some personally brought about great peace, so that punishments were set aside and went unused; some founded their states upon humanity and generosity and transformed the people through virtue. Judged by their accomplishments and virtue, they approached the flourishing achievement of the ancient emperors and kings, and it would seem fitting that they too should participate in the transmission of the Way.

Nevertheless, their efforts to rectify their minds and cultivate themselves may not have reached completion, and their learning in preserving and nurturing the mind may not have been wholly pure. Among them one cannot find anyone whose conduct issued purely and entirely from what was correct, who stood preeminent in grasping its essential principle, and who thereby approached the method of the mind expressed in being discerning and single-minded and holding fast to the Mean. Since what they called learning was not the learning of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, what they called government was likewise not the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. How could they qualify to be spoken of as participants in the transmission of the Way? This is what Han Yu meant when he said that, upon Meng Ke’s death, the transmission found no successor.

In the Song era, true Confucian scholars emerged in succession, and the learning of the Way shone forth brightly. Zhou Dunyi arose a hundred generations later; without receiving instruction from a teacher, he silently apprehended the substance of the Way. He devised a diagram and composed writings, penetrating to the ultimate root and grasping the essentials. Cheng Hao distinguished the specious errors of heterodox teachings and dispelled the doubts of a hundred…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
年未明之惑而充養有道見於定性之書程
頤學極聖人之精微行全君子之純粹而道
德淵源發於四箴之警至於朱熹則窮理以
致其知反躬以踐其實而考訂探索註書釋
經有以集諸儒之大成自孟子而後若四子
者講求著述之功亦誠多矣但在當時其立
朝也不顯於位其筮仕也不竟其施所謂惇
敘化成之事彌綸參贊之功方諸皐夔伊傅
然且未可乃直躋諸二帝三王要非所敢當
也後儒黃幹推尊其功而曰堯舜禹湯文武
===
周公生而道始行孔子孟子生而道始明孔
孟之道周程張子繼之周程張子之道文公
朱先生又繼之於是陳淳李方真德秀吳澄
輩相祖其說昭布於天下漸漬於耳目蓋已
久矣
聖制所謂道統之傳歸諸臣下又盡出於宋儒之
論者此也夫幹之為是論也由其不知君師
之非有二致治教之非有二途故以行道明
道岐而二之遂有見於道而無見於統而不
知其言之過也其於名實之歸誠有未審者

punctuated:
年未明之惑，而充養有道，見於定性之書。程頤學極聖人之精微，行全君子之純粹，而道德淵源，發於四箴之警。至於朱熹，則窮理以致其知，反躬以踐其實，而考訂探索，註書釋經，有以集諸儒之大成。自孟子而後，若四子者，講求著述之功亦誠多矣。但在當時，其立朝也，不顯於位；其筮仕也，不竟其施。所謂惇敘化成之事、彌綸參贊之功，方諸皐夔伊傅，然且未可，乃直躋諸二帝三王，要非所敢當也。後儒黃幹推尊其功而曰：「堯舜禹湯文武周公生，而道始行；孔子孟子生，而道始明。孔孟之道，周程張子繼之；周程張子之道，文公朱先生又繼之。」於是陳淳、李方、真德秀、吳澄輩，相祖其說，昭布於天下，漸漬於耳目，蓋已久矣。
聖制所謂「道統之傳歸諸臣下，又盡出於宋儒之論」者，此也。夫幹之為是論也，由其不知君師之非有二致、治教之非有二途，故以行道明道岐而二之，遂有見於道而無見於統，而不知其言之過也。其於名實之歸，誠有未審者
translation_en:
…the perplexities that had remained unresolved for a hundred years; his method of nurturing and cultivating himself is evident in his Letter on Steadying the Nature. Cheng Yi’s learning fathomed the sages’ subtlest profundities, and his conduct fully embodied the gentleman’s purity; the deep sources of his moral understanding found expression in the admonitions of his Four Admonitions. As for Zhu Xi, he investigated principles to extend his knowledge and examined himself to put them into practice. Through critical examination and inquiry, annotating books and elucidating the classics, he brought together the great achievements of the various Confucian scholars. Since Mencius, the contributions of these four masters to inquiry and writing have indeed been considerable. Yet in their own times, they held no prominent rank at court, and their official careers did not allow them fully to implement their teachings. In strengthening human relationships and bringing transformation to completion, or in comprehensively ordering affairs and assisting the work of Heaven and Earth, they could not yet be compared even with Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue. To elevate them directly to the level of the Two Emperors and Three Kings was surely an honor they would not have dared accept. The later scholar Huang Gan exalted their achievements, saying: “With the birth of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou, the Way first came to be practiced; with the birth of Confucius and Mencius, the Way first came to be elucidated. The Way of Confucius and Mencius was carried on by Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, and Master Zhang Zai; their Way was in turn carried on by Master Zhu, posthumously titled Wengong.” Thereupon Chen Chun, Li Fang [?], Zhen Dexiu, Wu Cheng, and others took this account as their authority and spread it widely throughout the realm. It has long permeated what people hear and see.
This is what Your Majesty’s pronouncement refers to in saying that “the transmission of the succession to the Way is assigned to subjects, and this derives entirely from the arguments of Song Confucian scholars.” Huang Gan advanced this argument because he did not understand that the roles of ruler and teacher have no separate ultimate purposes, and that governing and teaching are not two distinct paths. He therefore divided practicing the Way and elucidating the Way into two separate things. Thus he perceived the Way but failed to perceive its succession, without recognizing the error in his words. In determining how names correspond to realities, he truly failed to examine the matter fully…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
矣臣嘗聞之聖王繼天立極以君天下自其
主張斯道也而有道統之名以是而治以是
而教天下萬世之所謂心學者已開矣然或
不得其位而無行道之責則自其講明斯道
也而有道學之名以弼其治以彰其教而天
下萬世之所謂道統者亦寓矣故世有聖君
則道統之傳以屬於上時無明主則道學之
儒遂見於下自四子而觀之其講求著述之
功以竊比於禹臯陶諸臣下之見知而為道
學可也然師道雖立而阻於君道之未弘心
===
法雖明而限於治法之未溥若以嗣帝王之
真傳如古聖人而遂謂之道統則不可也黃
幹諸儒之論豈為至當不易之言哉夫漢唐
宋之諸君有其位而無其學周程朱之四子
有其學而無其功此上下千數百年之間道
統之傳所以不續也天於斯道未嘗忘情必
當貞元會合之期篤生大聖者出而居君師
之位以任明道行道之責以續千載不傳之
統誠有非偶然者矣欽惟
太祖高皇帝以神聖之資汛掃胡元肇造區夏明

translation_en:
…indeed. Your servant has heard that sage kings carry on Heaven’s work and establish the supreme standard, thereby ruling all under Heaven. Because they uphold this Way, theirs is called the succession of the Way (daotong). Through it they govern, and through it they teach: thus what all the world and later generations call the learning of the mind has already been opened up. Yet some do not attain the sovereign’s position and bear no responsibility for putting the Way into practice. Because they expound and clarify this Way, theirs is called the learning of the Way (daoxue). Through it they assist the ruler’s government and illuminate his teaching; within it, too, resides what all the world and later generations call the succession of the Way. Thus, when a sage ruler exists, the transmission of the succession of the Way belongs to those above; when there is no enlightened sovereign, scholars of the learning of the Way appear among those below. Considering the four masters, it is permissible to venture to compare their achievements in inquiry and writing with those of Yu, Gao Yao, and other ministers who knew the Way through direct acquaintance with sages, and to call this the learning of the Way. Yet although the way of the teacher was established, it was obstructed because the way of the ruler had not been extended; although the method of the mind was clear, it was constrained because methods of government had not spread widely. To regard them as inheriting the true transmission of the emperors and kings, like the ancient sages, and consequently to call this the succession of the Way, is not permissible. Can the arguments of Huang Gan and the other scholars be deemed supremely fitting and unalterable pronouncements? The rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song held the position but lacked the learning; the four masters—Zhou, the two Chengs, and Zhu—possessed the learning but lacked the achievement in government. This is why the transmission of the succession of the Way did not continue throughout these thousand and several hundred years. Heaven has never ceased to care for this Way. Surely, at the destined convergence of the cycle’s end and its renewed beginning, Heaven would bring forth a great sage to occupy the position of ruler and teacher, assume responsibility for clarifying and practicing the Way, and resume the succession that had gone untransmitted for a thousand years. This assuredly was no mere accident.
Reverently considering Taizu, the Exalted Emperor: endowed with divine sagacity, he swept away the non-Han Yuan and founded anew the realm of China, making manifest…

典以淑民經綸之迹燦乎王道之大備莫非
古帝王之治法也
觀心有亭省躬有錄衍義有廡洪範有註體堯

translation_en:
…the Three Bonds after they had fallen into decay, and rectified the nine rules after they had been lost. He established rites to provide standards for the world and promulgated statutes to improve the people. His achievements in ordering the realm brilliantly displayed the full realization of the Kingly Way; all embodied the methods of government of the ancient emperors and kings. For contemplating the mind there was a pavilion; for examining oneself, a record; for elaborating meanings, a gallery [?]; and for the Great Plan, a commentary. He embodied the purport of the transmission from Yao to Shun and faithfully held to the Mean; he continued the essentials transmitted among the sages and unceasingly kept hold of and preserved the mind. I have read his admonition to Zeng Lu, which says: “The ruler’s mind alone is the foundation of government and moral transformation. If what he harbors within is not the mind of Yao and Shun, yet he wishes his administration to achieve the government of Yao and Shun, this cannot be done.” His admonition to Song Lian says: “The human mind comes and goes with the workings of vital energy; to grasp and preserve it is difficult. I dare not allow myself leisure or ease.” Through his efforts to maintain this vigilance, he possessed the complete virtue of Heaven as an undivided whole; all embodied the methods of cultivating the mind of the ancient emperors and kings. With methods of government to extend moral transformation, the Way of the ruler was established; with methods of cultivating the mind to advance virtue, the Way of the teacher was complete. Thus the succession of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and Confucius was at last renewed.
After one transmission came Emperor Chengzu Wen, who quelled the disturbances, secured the frontiers, and established the capital at Yanjing. Institutions were renewed, and the transforming influence of his government spread abundantly. He produced the works on the Five Classics and Four Books and the Complete Compendium of Nature and Principle, continuing the succession of the former kings and bringing about a luminous and harmonious transformation. His imperially composed preface says: “The government of emperors and kings is rooted entirely in the Way.” It also says: “When the Way of the Six Classics is made clear, the mind of the sages can be seen and the achievements of consummate government can be realized.” These methods of government and of cultivating the mind clearly embodied the purport of that transmission. Above, he carried on the orthodox succession of the Way of the august sovereigns and kings; below, …

皇上敬

translation_en:
…and laid the foundation for peace throughout the myriad ages—was it not through this? The successive sage emperors transmitted this inheritance, elucidating Heaven’s enduring norms and ordering human relationships. They grew ever more steadfast in handing down the methods of government and the discipline of the mind, never allowing them to lapse. The harmonious government of these hundred and eighty years has thus had its foundation. Now our Emperor reveres Heaven in occupying the imperial throne, remaining solemnly vigilant and unremitting; he labors for the people in administering government, practicing benevolence and righteousness together. He offers sacrifices to Fuxi, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius in the eastern chamber of Wenhua Hall. The ancient sages who transmitted the Way to one another are solemnly present before him, their spirits assembled in one hall. Across a thousand years, he is what is called one who “knows through hearing.”
Having gained insight from reading, he personally composed the Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi zhen), continuing the purport of what Yao and Shun transmitted and received. It begins by tracing why this mind must be preserved, then explains the essential importance of reverent unity, and proceeds to discuss the great matters that depend upon the sovereign. Its middle portion details the methods of vigilance and steadfast self-discipline, and it concludes with the effects of cultivating virtue and rectifying the realm, prolonging blessings and achieving good government. This is precisely the distinction between the precarious human mind and the subtle mind of the Way, the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness in holding fast to the mean, and the admonition to be mindful of one’s position and reverently cultivate oneself. He also composed the Commentary on the Five Admonitions (Wu zhen zhu), elucidating the ultimate standards of moral principle in all their subtlety. Reverence alone should govern the human mind, while the assaults of the many desires enter through seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting. Thus the work of holding fast to and preserving the mind is set forth in the commentary, leaving nothing unexplained in its elucidation of reverent unity. As for the Great Compendium on Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun dadian), it clearly displays the excellence of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues; the Record and Eulogy of Revering Heaven (Qintian jisong) radiantly expresses the sincerity of his illustrious service to Heaven; his verses on Chonghua [Shun] greatly elucidate the subtleties of this mind…

title: 嘉靖二十六年進士登科錄
text:
聖學有詩備述大學之要其存之而為敬一之
至德者逺而宗之固堯舜禹湯文武之心法
也近而守之非
祖宗之心法乎正祀
郊社以明隂陽之分鼎建
宗廟以序昭穆之義親定
祫禘以盡孝享之心肇舉
明堂以隆尊親之典其溥之而為惇叙之大業
者逺而宗之固堯舜禹湯文武之治法也近
而守之非
===
祖宗之治法乎有是心法以立出治之基而煥乎
斯道之大明有是治法以廣此心之用而沛
乎斯道之大行上而繼立之功既以克建下
而著述之盛又以兼能盖帝王之道賴以復
明而開創之烈賴以懋著其所以為天地立
心為生民立命為往聖繼絕學為萬世開太
平而有功於二帝三王者莫大於是矣書曰
作之君作之師其助上帝寵綏四方我
皇上之謂也
臨御以來道化流通至和宣暢仰焉與

translation_en:
…There are poems on sagely learning, fully expounding the essentials of the Great Learning. Preserved within, this constitutes the consummate virtue of reverent concentration on the One. In taking distant antiquity as its model, it is indeed the teaching of the mind transmitted by Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu; in upholding the nearer precedent, is it not the teaching of the mind transmitted by the imperial ancestors? Your Majesty has rectified the suburban sacrifices and those at the altars of the soil, clarifying the distinction between yin and yang; grandly established the imperial ancestral temples, giving proper order to the zhao and mu generational ranks; personally determined the regulations for the xia and di ancestral sacrifices, fully expressing the devotion of filial offerings; and inaugurated the rites of the Hall of Light, exalting the ceremonies for honoring one's parent. Extended outward, this constitutes the great undertaking of fostering harmony and proper order. In taking distant antiquity as its model, it is indeed the method of government transmitted by Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu; in upholding the nearer precedent, is it not the method of government transmitted by the imperial ancestors?
With this teaching of the mind, the foundation for government is established, and this Way shines forth brilliantly; with this method of government, the workings of this mind are extended, and this Way prevails abundantly. At the higher level, the achievement of continuing and establishing the tradition has already been accomplished; at the level below, excellence in writing has likewise been attained. Thus the Way of emperors and kings has been illuminated anew, and the glorious achievements of founding the dynasty have been made splendidly manifest. Nothing could surpass this in establishing the mind of Heaven and Earth, establishing the destiny of the living people, continuing the interrupted learning of past sages, and opening an age of Great Peace for countless generations—thereby rendering service to the Two Emperors and Three Kings. The Book of Documents says: “He made rulers for them and teachers for them, that they might assist the Lord on High in cherishing and pacifying the four quarters.” This speaks of our Emperor.

translation_en:
…Heaven in virtue, and above follows the same Way as your ancestor, carrying forward the succession that had gone untransmitted for a thousand years. Is this not truly a correspondence between name and reality? Were the Confucian scholars of the Song to live again, how greatly would they extol and celebrate your excellence! Yet, reverently reading Your Majesty’s decree, I find these words: “I wish, looking far back, to continue the succession of the great Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and, looking nearer, to emulate the transmission of the learning of the mind by my ancestors, the sage sovereigns. Apart from this, to what else could I fittingly devote my efforts?” This expresses Your Majesty’s disposition to look toward the Way as though you had not yet seen it, never presuming that you have attained fulfillment. Your servant has heard that the government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and their Way is rooted in the mind. Thus, the method of cultivating the mind is the foundation of the method of governing; the method of governing is the extension of the method of cultivating the mind. These two methods flow into and inform one another, and an enduring achievement extending without limit through ten thousand generations is accomplished through this mind.

Your Majesty follows Yao and Shun, preserving the virtue of the mind and nature through reverence and singleness of purpose. What more need be said? Yet your servant constantly fears that what the moral mind governs is difficult to preserve and nurture, while what issues from the human mind readily lapses into unrestrained indulgence. If scrutiny should ever be incomplete or steadfast adherence insufficient, there would be no means of discerning the incipient stirrings of what is subtle, nor of recognizing the gradual development of what is precarious. Moreover, the ruler’s single mind is above all the master of all under Heaven and of the state. If the mind lacks reverence, how can the Way be firmly established? If the Way is not firmly established, how can his achievement endure? Your servant wishes that Your Majesty’s vigilance and caution may become still more earnest than at the beginning, and that your learning, continually cultivated toward illumination, may become ever more rigorous hereafter. 治易經字子志行一年三十七七月十四日生
曾祖潮 祖文恭 父茂 嫡母劉氏 蕭氏 生母徐氏

治詩經字望之行四年三十四正月二十八日生

punctuated:
張師載〔貫湖廣承天府潜江縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字以道，行一，年三十四，五月二十四日生〕。曾祖貴，祖洪，父永祥，母胡氏。具慶下，弟師栻、師戢、師成、師儀、師戫，娶羅氏。湖廣鄉試第四十名，會試第五十名。

何璿〔貫直隸揚州府泰興縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字德齊，行四十三，年三十一，四月十三日生〕。曾祖顒，祖岱〔兵馬司指揮〕，父稟〔監生〕，母儲氏。具慶下，弟珹、璀、珊、琯、珒，娶徐氏，繼娶馬氏。應天府鄉試第九十五名，會試第四十四名。

蘇繼〔貫山東青州府壽光縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字子志，行一，年三十七，七月十四日生〕。曾祖潮，祖文恭，父茂，嫡母劉氏、蕭氏，生母徐氏。慈侍下，弟約、純、紳、鑰、銳、鎮、錦、欽，娶趙氏。山東鄉試第六十六名，會試第二百七十四名。

宋儀望〔貫江西吉安府永豐縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字望之，行四，年三十四，正月二十八日生〕。曾祖邦鉉〔壽官〕，祖魁昂〔七品散官〕，父聞義，前母嚴氏，母鍾氏。慈侍下，兄敏、鳳、掀、倣，娶郭氏。江西鄉試第三十名，會試第二百六十九名。
translation_en:
Zhang Shizai 張師載 was registered in a civilian household in Qianjiang County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, and was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yidao; he ranked first in family order, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Hong, his father Yongxiang, and his mother Lady Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shishi, Shiji, Shicheng, Shiyi, and Shiyu. He married Lady Luo. He placed fortieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Xuan 何璿 was registered in a civilian household in Taixing County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Deqi; he ranked forty-third in family order, was thirty-one years old, and was born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather Dai was a Commander in a Police Office; his father Bin was an Imperial University student; and his mother was Lady Chu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Cheng, Cui, Shan, Guan, and Jin. He married Lady Xu and subsequently Lady Ma. He placed ninety-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Ji 蘇繼 was registered in a military household in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zizhi; he ranked first in family order, was thirty-seven years old, and was born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chao, his grandfather Wengong, and his father Mao. His legal mothers were Lady Liu and Lady Xiao, and his birth mother was Lady Xu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brothers were Yue, Chun, Shen, Yue, Rui, Zhen, Jin, and Qin. He married Lady Zhao. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Yiwang 宋儀望 was registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wangzhi; he ranked fourth in family order, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Bangxuan held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his grandfather Kui’ang was an unassigned official of the seventh rank; and his father was Wenyi. His father’s former wife was Lady Yan, and his mother was Lady Zhong. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Min, Feng, Xian, and Fang. He married Lady Guo. He placed thirtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.
